post.summary: Acknowledge a fired event of a user alert
post.description: Marks a fired event of the user alert as seen, now, by the admin behind the credentials (its email, `?` for an api key used without a backoffice user). The events live in the database of the active user-analytics data exporter, in the tenant (organization) of the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The id of the user alert, the `id` of an `analytics.otoroshi.io` user alert entity

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The id of the fired event, its `id` in `GET /api/analytics/alerts/{alertId}/events`

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Tenant
parameters.description: The tenant (organization) whose data is read, `default` when absent. The admin must be a super admin or allowed to read it, and the answer is always restricted to it

200.description: The event is marked as seen, now, by the admin behind the credentials: `ok` is `true`

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is neither a super admin nor allowed to read the tenant (organization) of the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header

404.description: The alert has no such event in the tenant (organization)

412.description: No user-analytics data exporter is active

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The database of the active user-analytics data exporter could not be queried

post.summary: Import the certificates of a PKCS#12 file
post.description: Reads the certificates and the private keys of the PKCS#12 file (`.p12`, `.pfx`) of the body, decrypted with the `password` query parameter, and stores each of them as a certificate entity. Only a super admin can call it.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The password of the PKCS#12 file. Defaults to an empty password

requestBody.description: The raw bytes of the PKCS#12 file (`.p12`, `.pfx`) holding the certificates and their private keys

schema.description: The bytes of a PKCS#12 file

200.description: Every certificate of the file was stored as a certificate entity, answered as `{"done": true}`

400.description: The credentials are missing, or the body is not a PKCS#12 file that the password decrypts

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or the global configuration makes the admin api read only (`apiReadOnly`) and the call is not a GET

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is not a super admin: the admin the backoffice calls on behalf of (`Otoroshi-BackOffice-User`), or the rights the api key carries in its `otoroshi-access-rights` metadata. An api key without such rights is not refused

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

post.description: Generates a key pair and an intermediate certificate authority signed by the certificate authority of the path (basic constraint `CA:true` with a path length of 0, key usages `keyCertSign`, `cRLSign` and `digitalSignature`), from the settings of the body. The chain of the generated certificate authority holds it, its parent and the chain of its parent. The generated certificate is answered as a certificate entity, with its chain and its private key, and stored unless `persist=false`. Only a super admin can call it. The certificate authority is found by its id, or else by its serial number, as it is written or as a number.

parameters.name: ca
parameters.description: The certificate authority: the id of a certificate entity of otoroshi, or the serial number (as a decimal number) of one, that has to be a certificate authority

parameters.name: persist
parameters.description: Whether to store the generated certificate as a certificate entity (true by default). When stored, the answer holds its id in `certId`

requestBody.description: The settings of the intermediate certificate authority to generate

200.description: The intermediate certificate authority, as a certificate entity

400.description: The credentials are missing, the body does not describe a certificate (it gives neither `key` nor `keyType` and `keySize`), or the certificate authority cannot be generated, or the body is not json

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or the global configuration makes the admin api read only (`apiReadOnly`) and the call is not a GET

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is not a super admin: the admin the backoffice calls on behalf of (`Otoroshi-BackOffice-User`), or the rights the api key carries in its `otoroshi-access-rights` metadata. An api key without such rights is not refused

404.description: The parent certificate authority does not exist, or is not a certificate authority

post.summary: Deploy the draft of an api
post.description: Replaces the api with its draft: everything comes from the draft except the id, the documentation and the clients, which are the ones of the api, and the routes, whose ids get the `_prod` suffix. A draft in the `staging` state is published, otherwise the api keeps its state; an api in a state that cannot be deployed (a removed api) is refused. The deployment of the body, with a slim definition of the draft instead of its `apiDefinition`, becomes the first of the `deployments` of the api, which keeps the last five. An `ApiDeploymentEvent` analytics event is sent. The admin behind the credentials has to be able to write the api.

parameters.name: apiId
parameters.description: The `id` of the api, as listed by `GET /apis/apis.otoroshi.io/v1/apis`

requestBody.description: The deployment. Its `id` is generated and its `at` is now when absent; its `apiDefinition` is required but replaced by a slim definition of the deployed draft

400.description: The credentials are missing, the body is not valid json, it is not a deployment (`bad entity`), the api cannot be deployed from its state (`invalid_deploy_transition`), or it could not be saved

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or the global configuration makes the admin api read only (`apiReadOnly`) and the call is not a GET

403.description: The admin behind the credentials cannot write the entity

404.description: No entity has this id, no api has it while another entity does (`api not found`), the api has no draft, or its draft cannot be read as an api

415.description: The body is not sent with an `application/json` (or `text/json`) content type

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

get.description: Answers the statistics of the calls of the period made to a route (`service`), with an api key (`apikey`) or to the routes of a group (`group`), read from the Elasticsearch cluster of the global configuration (`elasticReadsConfig`): counts, bytes, durations and overheads, their histograms over time, and the calls by status code (and by route, for an api key or a group). `fields` keeps only some of them.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The id of the group of routes whose statistics are read

get.summary: Read the live statistics of a route
get.description: Answers the counters of the traffic of a route (calls, bytes in and out), and the rates and average durations of its latest calls. With `every`, answers a server sent events stream that sends them every `every` milliseconds, as long as the client keeps the connection open, the `data` of each event being a json `LiveStats`. Calling it is audited (`ACCESS_SERVICE_LIVESTATS`). On a leader, the rates add up, and the durations average, the ones the members of the cluster report. get.summary: Open the websocket of the state of the cluster
get.description: Upgrades the connection to a websocket on which the leader pushes the state of the cluster, and the worker sends its quotas updates, instead of polling `GET /api/cluster/state` and `PUT /api/cluster/quotas` (used by the workers when `otoroshi.cluster.worker.useWs` is enabled). Every `otoroshi.cluster.worker.state.pollEvery` milliseconds, the leader sends a json message holding the state (`state`, the bytes of the lines of `GET /api/cluster/state` as an array of numbers), the name and the version of the leader (`node_name`, `node_version`), and the number of lines, the digest and the date of the state (`data_count`, `data_digest`, `data_from`); as a binary message when the cluster compression is enabled, as a text message otherwise. The worker sends text messages holding itself as a member (`member`, a `MemberView`) and an update (`payload`, a `ClusterQuotasUpdate`: only `apkincr`, `srvincr` and `globstats` are applied). Only a super admin can open it.

post.description:
Runs a query of the user analytics catalog (see `GET /api/analytics/_schema`) on the PostgreSQL database of the active user-analytics data exporter and returns its result.

This is how the user analytics dashboards get their data: read a dashboard with `GET /apis/analytics.otoroshi.io/v1/user-dashboards/{id}`, then run one query per widget with its `query` and `params`.

The result is always restricted to the tenant (organization) given by the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header, and is cached for 30 seconds unless `nocache` is `true`. Only the leaders of a cluster (or an instance out of any cluster) serve this endpoint.

Built-in queries (admin extensions can add more):

| id | shape | params | compare |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requests_total` | `scalar` | | yes |
| `errors_total` | `scalar` | | yes |
| `requests_by_status` | `pie` | | no |
| `requests_by_method` | `pie` | | no |
| `requests_by_route` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_api` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_apikey` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_user` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_domain` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_by_country` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `top_error_routes` | `topN` | `top_n` | no |
| `requests_per_second` | `timeseries` (`points`) | | yes |
| `error_rate_ts` | `timeseries` (`points`) | | yes |
| `duration_avg_ts` | `timeseries` (`points`) | | yes |
| `overhead_avg_ts` | `timeseries` (`points`) | | yes |
| `duration_percentiles_ts` | `timeseries` (`series`: `p50`, `p75`, `p95`, `p99`) | | yes |
| `traffic_in_out_ts` | `timeseries` (`series`: `data_in`, `data_out`) | | yes |
| `requests_by_status_class_ts` | `timeseries` (`series`: `2xx`, `3xx`, `4xx`, `5xx`) | | yes |
| `response_time_heatmap` | `heatmap` | | no |

get.summary: Read the state of the cluster
get.description: Answers the whole state the workers load from the leaders: every key of the datastore (except the audit and alert events, the admins, the backoffice sessions, the health checks and the statistics), one json object per line. A leader answers the copy of the state it refreshes on its own, and registers the caller as a worker member when it sends an `Otoroshi-Worker-Name` header. A worker identifies itself with the `Otoroshi-Worker-*` headers (its name, id, version, java version, operating system, location, ports and relay routing settings). A worker answers its own datastore. The body is gzip compressed when the cluster compression is enabled (`otoroshi.cluster.compression` from 0 to 9), without a `Content-Encoding` header. Only a super admin can call it.

parameters.description: Read for compatibility, not used: a value that is not a number is answered as a server error

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Id
parameters.description: The id the worker generated when it started (`node_` followed by a uuid). A temporary `tmpnode_` id is used when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Version
parameters.description: The version of otoroshi the worker runs, `undefined` when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Java-Version
parameters.description: The java virtual machine of the worker, as a json `JavaVersion`

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Os
parameters.description: The operating system of the worker, as a json `OS`

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Location
parameters.description: The ip address of the worker (`otoroshi.cluster.selfAddress`, or the one it detected when it started), the `location` of the member; `--` when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Http-Port
parameters.description: The exposed http port of the worker

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Https-Port
parameters.description: The exposed https port of the worker

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Internal-Http-Port
parameters.description: The http port the worker listens on

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Internal-Https-Port
parameters.description: The https port the worker listens on

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Relay-Routing
parameters.description: The relay routing settings of the worker, as a json `RelayRouting`

With `full=true`, answers instead the anonymous usage report of the cluster (the one the anonymous reporting job sends, whether it is enabled or not): the features it uses, its traffic, its members and the number of its entities. post.summary: Replace the whole state with an export file
post.description: Replaces the whole state of otoroshi with the one of the file sent as the raw body: a json export (`OtoroshiExport`), or, when the `X-Content-Type` header is `application/x-ndjson`, an ndjson export of the datastore (one key per line, as answered by `GET /api/otoroshi.json` with `Accept: application/x-ndjson`), imported key by key once every line has been read and is a line of an export. The content type of the body itself is not read. The import then deletes every key of the datastore: the entities, the sessions, the quotas and the statistics. The admin api keeps working only if the import holds the api key used to call it (and the service group it is authorized on). Only a super admin can call it.

parameters.name: X-Content-Type
parameters.description: The format of the file: `application/x-ndjson` for an ndjson export of the datastore, anything else (or nothing) for a json export

requestBody.description: The file to import, as the raw body

200.description: The datastore is emptied and the state of the file imported: `done` is `true`

400.description: The credentials are missing (the route that serves the admin api refuses the call before the controller runs), the file, when it is not ndjson, is not a json object, or a line of the ndjson file is not a line of an otoroshi export. Nothing is imported

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or the global configuration makes the admin api read only (`apiReadOnly`) and the call is not a GET

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is not a super admin: the admin the backoffice calls on behalf of (`Otoroshi-BackOffice-User`), or the rights the api key carries in its `otoroshi-access-rights` metadata. An api key without such rights is not refused

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The file could not be imported: an entity cannot be read, or the datastore failed while importing. The datastore may be left partly imported

put.summary: Apply the quotas updates of a worker
put.description: Applies the quotas updates of the body, one json object per line: the calls of the api keys (`apkincr`), the traffic of the routes (`srvincr`), the counters of the custom quotas (`custquots`) and custom throttling (`custthrot`) plugins, and the statistics of the worker (`globstats`, that also registers the worker as a member). Workers call it on the leaders every `otoroshi.cluster.worker.quotas.pushEvery` milliseconds (2000 by default). The body is gzip compressed when the cluster compression is enabled (`otoroshi.cluster.compression` from 0 to 9), without a `Content-Encoding` header. Every line has to end with a new line, the last one included. A worker identifies itself with the `Otoroshi-Worker-*` headers (its name, id, version, java version, operating system, location, ports and relay routing settings). Only a super admin can call it.

parameters.name: budget
parameters.description: How long the leader may take to apply the updates, in milliseconds (2000 by default): beyond it, a warning is logged. Workers send their `otoroshi.cluster.worker.quotas.timeout`

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Name
parameters.description: The name of the worker (`otoroshi.cluster.worker.name`): the leaders register the worker as a member under this name. A body with a known update and no such header is answered with a server error

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Id
parameters.description: The id the worker generated when it started (`node_` followed by a uuid). A temporary `tmpnode_` id is used when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Version
parameters.description: The version of otoroshi the worker runs, `undefined` when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Java-Version
parameters.description: The java virtual machine of the worker, as a json `JavaVersion`

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Os
parameters.description: The operating system of the worker, as a json `OS`

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Location
parameters.description: The ip address of the worker (`otoroshi.cluster.selfAddress`, or the one it detected when it started), the `location` of the member; `--` when absent

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Http-Port
parameters.description: The exposed http port of the worker

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Https-Port
parameters.description: The exposed https port of the worker

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Internal-Http-Port
parameters.description: The http port the worker listens on

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Internal-Https-Port
parameters.description: The https port the worker listens on

parameters.name: Otoroshi-Worker-Relay-Routing
parameters.description: The relay routing settings of the worker, as a json `RelayRouting`

requestBody.description: The quotas updates, one json object per line

get.summary: Open a tunnel from a remote otoroshi
get.description: Upgrades the connection to a websocket a remote otoroshi uses as a tunnel: the routes of this cluster that call the tunnel (with the `Remote tunnel calls` plugin, `otoroshi.next.tunnel.TunnelPlugin`) send their requests through it to the remote otoroshi, which routes them as if it had received them. Every message is a binary message holding a json object, its `type` telling what it is. The instance sends `request` messages (a `TunnelRequest`), and the remote otoroshi answers each with a `response` message (a `TunnelResponse` with the same `request_id`). Every 10 seconds, the remote otoroshi also sends a `ping` message, answered with a `pong` unless `pong_ping=true`, and a `tunnel_meta` message describing itself (`tunnel_id`, `name`, `routes`), listed by `GET /api/tunnels`. A `pong` message is answered with a `ping`, and with `pong_ping=true` the instance sends a `pong` message every 10 seconds. The instance lists the tunnel in its `tunnels` as a member of the cluster while it is open. Any admin can open it.

parameters.name: tunnel_id
parameters.description: The id of the tunnel (`otoroshi.tunnels.<key>.id` on the remote otoroshi), as listed by `GET /api/tunnels` and named by the `tunnel_id` of the `Remote tunnel calls` plugin. Several remote otoroshi instances can connect under the same id: the requests go to them in turn

parameters.name: pong_ping
parameters.description: Whether the instance sends a `pong` message every 10 seconds and answers the `pong` messages of the remote otoroshi with a `ping` (reversed keep alive), instead of answering its `ping` messages with a `pong`. False by default

groupSize.description: The maximum number of events of a batch: a batch is sent once it is full or once `groupDuration` is elapsed. Defaults to 100

groupDuration.description: The maximum delay before a batch is sent, in milliseconds, even when it is not full. Defaults to 30000

projection.description: The fields of the events that are exported, as a json object: `{"field": true}` keeps a field, operators like `$at`, `$path`, `$jq` or `$date_from_unix_fmt` compute new ones (see the documentation of the data exporters). An empty object exports the whole events

customFilter.description: A custom filter, applied after `filtering`: the events it refuses are not exported. Null for none

customTransform.description: A custom transformation of the events, applied before they are exported. Null for none

example.name: Access logs to the log collector
example.desc: Access logs to the log collector, managed by the platform team

NgFrontend.description: What requests a route matches. A request has to satisfy every criterion. The legacy `domain` key, holding a single domain, is read too and replaces `domains`

items.description: A domain followed by an optional path. The domain can hold `*` wildcards (`*.oto.tools`), the path wildcards (`/users/*/bills`), named parameters (`/users/:id`) and named parameters with a regex (`/users/$id<[0-9]+>`)

domains.description: The domains, with an optional path, the route matches. The path matches as a prefix unless `exact` is true

strip_path.description: Whether the matched path is removed from the path of the request forwarded to the backend. Defaults to `true`

exact.description: Whether the path of the request must be the path of a domain exactly, instead of starting with it. Defaults to `false`

additionalProperties.description: The expected value: a value to match exactly, `Regex(<regex>)`, `Wildcard(<pattern with *>)`, `Exists()` (or `IsDefined()`) when the header must be present with any value, `NotDefined()` when it must be absent

headers.description: The headers the request must hold, by name (case insensitive). Empty: any headers

additionalProperties.description: The expected value, with the syntax of the headers: an exact value, `Regex(...)`, `Wildcard(...)`, `Exists()`, `IsDefined()` or `NotDefined()`

cookies.description: The cookies the request must hold, by name (case insensitive). Empty: any cookies

additionalProperties.description: The expected value, with the syntax of the headers: an exact value, `Regex(...)`, `Wildcard(...)`, `Exists()`, `IsDefined()` or `NotDefined()`

query.description: The query params the request must hold, by name. Empty: any query params

items.description: An http method, in upper case

methods.description: The http methods the route matches. Empty: any method

CertificateExtension.description: An extension of an X509 certificate

oid.description: The object identifier of the extension, in dotted notation: `2.5.29.17` for the subject alternative names, `2.5.29.19` for the basic constraints, `2.5.29.15` for the key usages, `2.5.29.37` for the extended key usages...

value.description: The DER encoded value of the extension, as its bytes in uppercase hexadecimal separated by colons

HealthCheck.description: How otoroshi checks the health of the targets of a backend: it calls a path of each target periodically, and the answer gives the health of the target, sent as a `HealthCheckEvent`: green, yellow when the logic check fails, red, or black when the target cannot be reached. A target that cannot be reached is left out of the load balancing until a check reaches it again

enabled.description: Whether the health of the targets is checked. Defaults to `false`

url.description: The path called on each target, appended to its scheme, host and port

timeout.description: How long the call can last at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `5000`

healthyStatuses.description: The statuses of a healthy target. When this list or `unhealthyStatuses` is not empty, a status in neither list is unhealthy. Both empty: a status from 200 to 499 is healthy

unhealthyStatuses.description: The statuses of an unhealthy target, checked before `healthyStatuses`

blockOnRed.description: Whether a target found red is flagged as unhealthy in the datastore, for the time to live of the health checks, as an unreachable target is. Defaults to `false`

logicCheck.description: Whether the call holds an `Otoroshi-Health-Check-Logic-Test` header with a number, the target having to answer that number plus 42 in the `Otoroshi-Health-Check-Logic-Test-Result` header to be green instead of yellow. Defaults to `true` when missing

healthyRegexChecks.description: Regexes looked for in a textual body: when not empty, the body must hold one of them for the target to be healthy

unhealthyRegexChecks.description: Regexes looked for in a textual body: a body holding one of them makes the target unhealthy

AnonymousReportMinMaxAvg.description: The smallest, the largest and the average of a number over entities, 0 when there is none

min.description: The smallest value over the entities, 0 when there is none

max.description: The largest value over the entities, 0 when there is none

avg.description: The average over the entities, 0 when there is none

UserAnalyticsAlertEvent.description: A fired event of a user alert, as stored in the `<table_prefix>_fired_alerts` table of the active user-analytics data exporter, with the evaluation of its conditions and its acknowledgement

id.description: The id of the fired event (the `@id` of the alert event, a snowflake id), to use in the paths that acknowledge it

ts.description: When the alert fired, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds

tenant.description: The tenant (organization) of the user alert: only the events of the tenant of the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header are answered

alert_id.description: The id of the user alert that fired, the `alertId` of the path

alert_name.description: The name of the user alert when it fired

severity.description: The severity of the user alert, like `info`, `warning` or `critical`

message.description: The `message` of the user alert when it fired
message.example: More than 5% of the requests failed

combine.description: How the conditions were combined: `AND` or `OR`

windowSeconds.description: The time window the conditions were evaluated on, in seconds

conditions.description: The evaluation of each condition of the alert

seen_at.description: When the event was acknowledged, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds

seen_by.description: The email of the admin who acknowledged the event, `?` when it was acknowledged through the admin api without a backoffice user

example.message: More than 5% of the requests failed

PluginDescription.description: A plugin of the proxy engine that can be added to a route

id.description: The id of the plugin, to use as the `plugin` of a route plugin: `cp:` followed by the name of its class

name.description: The readable name of the plugin, the one the route designer of the backoffice shows and searches on

description.description: What the plugin does, `null` when it has no description
description.example: This plugin expects to find an apikey to allow the request to pass

default_config.description: The configuration the plugin uses by default, `null` when it has none

config_schema.description: The form that edits the configuration of the plugin in the backoffice: the form generated from its configuration class (see `GET /api/forms`), merged with the one the plugin declares. Empty when it has none

config_flow.description: The names of the fields of the configuration form, in the order the backoffice shows them

no_js_form.description: Whether the plugin has no form of its own in the javascript of the backoffice: the backoffice then edits its configuration with the form of `config_schema` and `config_flow`

plugin_type.description: The kind of plugin, always `ng` (a plugin of the proxy engine)

plugin_visibility.description: Who can use the plugin, always `userland` here: the internal plugins are left out

plugin_categories.description: The categories of the plugin, see `GET /api/plugins/categories`

plugin_steps.description: The steps of the handling of a request where the plugin runs (see `GET /api/plugins/steps`)

plugin_tags.description: Free tags the plugin declares, empty for the plugins shipped with otoroshi

plugin_multi_inst.description: Whether a route can hold the plugin several times

plugin_backend_call_delegates.description: Whether the plugin, when it calls the backend itself, can delegate the call to the usual backend call of otoroshi

on_request.description: Whether the plugin acts on the request on its way to the backend: a pre route, an access validator, a route matcher, a request sink, a tunnel handler, a transformer of the request, or a websocket plugin of the client messages

on_response.description: Whether the plugin acts on the response on its way back to the client: a transformer of the response or of the errors, a websocket plugin of the backend messages, or a plugin of another kind (a backend call for instance) than the ones that only act on the request

example.name: Apikeys
example.description: This plugin expects to find an apikey to allow the request to pass

RestrictionPath.description: A path of the restrictions of an api key

method.description: The http method the restriction applies to, case insensitive, or `*` for every method

path.description: A regular expression the call has to match: on its path when it starts with `/`, on its domain followed by its path otherwise

authorized_entity.description: The entity the restriction is limited to: a route (or service descriptor) by id, an api, or a service group the api key is authorized on and the route belongs to. Null for every entity

VerificationSettings.description: The claims a jwt token has to hold, on top of a valid signature

fields.description: The expected values of the claims of the token, keyed by claim name. `iss`, `aud`, `sub` and `jti` are compared to their value, other claims accept the operators `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `ContainsOneOf(a, b)`, `ContainsNotOneOf(a, b)`, `ContainsAll(a, b)`... The values can hold expressions like `${req.headers.X-Tenant}`

additionalProperties.description: The expected value of the claim

arrayFields.description: The values an array claim of the token has to contain, keyed by claim name. Several values are separated by commas, the claim has to contain all of them

additionalProperties.description: The value, or the comma separated values, the array claim has to contain

ResourcesToBuild.description: The definitions of the entities to build

content.description: The definitions: a list of definitions, a single definition, or yaml (several documents separated by `---` lines)

oneOf.description: Yaml definitions, one document per entity
oneOf.example:
kind: proxy.otoroshi.io/Route
name: my-route
frontend:
  domains:
    - my-route.oto.tools
---
kind: apim.otoroshi.io/Apikey
clientName: my-key
