StatsPieChart.description: A pie chart of the traffic, read from Elasticsearch, in the shape the charts of the backoffice read

name.description: The name of the chart, always `Pie Chart`

colorPoint.description: Always `true`: each slice gets its own color

series.description: The series of the chart, always a single one holding the slices

name.description: What the slice counts (a status code, the name of a route)

y.description: The number of calls of the slice

OpenApiDocument.description: An openapi 3.0.3 document that describes the admin api of otoroshi

openapi.description: The version of the openapi specification the document follows

info.description: The title and the description of the api, its version (the version of otoroshi, or the `version` asked for), its contact and its license

example.title: Otoroshi Admin API
example.description: Admin API of the Otoroshi reverse proxy

externalDocs.description: Where to find the documentation of otoroshi

example.description: Otoroshi website

servers.description: The admin api of this otoroshi, as it is exposed

example.description: your local otoroshi server

tags.description: The tags the operations list in their `tags`: one per kind of entity (its singular name), one per group of entities, and one per family of the other operations of the admin api

name.description: The name of the tag, as the operations list it in their `tags`

description.description: What the operations of the tag are about
description.example: Create, read, update and delete the routes (proxy.otoroshi.io/Route)

example.name: route
example.description: Create, read, update and delete the routes (proxy.otoroshi.io/Route)

paths.description: The operations of the api, by path

additionalProperties.description: The operations of a path, by http method

components.description: The schemas the operations use, and how to authenticate

securitySchemes.description: How to authenticate, by name of scheme

info.title: Otoroshi Admin API
info.description: Admin API of the Otoroshi reverse proxy

tags.name: route
tags.description: Create, read, update and delete the routes (proxy.otoroshi.io/Route)

MemberView.description: An otoroshi instance member of a cluster, as known by the leaders: the leaders register themselves every few seconds, and register each worker that fetches the state or sends its quotas. A member is forgotten once its `timeout` has elapsed since it was last seen

id.description: The id the instance generates when it starts (`node_` followed by a uuid). A worker that sends no `Otoroshi-Worker-Id` header gets a temporary `tmpnode_` id

name.description: The name of the instance in the cluster (`otoroshi.cluster.leader.name` or `otoroshi.cluster.worker.name`, generated when absent). The leaders store the members by name: two instances with the same name are seen as one

version.description: The version of otoroshi the instance runs, `undefined` when a worker does not send it

location.description: The ip address of the instance (`otoroshi.cluster.selfAddress`, or the one detected when it starts), `--` when a worker does not send it. Tunnels use it to reach the instance a tunnel is connected to

httpPort.description: The exposed http port of the instance

httpsPort.description: The exposed https port of the instance

internalHttpPort.description: The http port the instance listens on

internalHttpsPort.description: The https port the instance listens on

lastSeen.description: When the instance was last seen by the leaders, a timestamp in milliseconds

timeout.description: How long after it was last seen the instance is forgotten, in milliseconds: 120000 for a leader, `otoroshi.cluster.worker.retries` times `otoroshi.cluster.worker.state.pollEvery` for a worker (30000 by default). Its health gets `orange` past half of it, `red` past three quarters

type.description: Whether the instance is a `Leader` or a `Worker` of the cluster (`Off` when the stored value is unknown)

stats.description: The last statistics the instance sent, `{}` before the first ones

tunnels.description: The ids of the tunnels connected to the instance (`GET /api/tunnels/register`). The workers send theirs only through the websocket of the state

items.description: The id of a tunnel connected to the instance

time.description: When the leader answered, a timestamp in milliseconds: only in the answers of the members listing, to compare with `lastSeen`

MetricsSettings.description: The settings of a metrics exporter: it feeds the metrics of the calls (counts, durations, sizes) exposed by otoroshi (Prometheus, ...), labelled with values taken from the events

labels.description: The labels of the metrics: each key is the path of a value of the event (`$at` stands for `@`), each value is the name of the label holding it

WasmVmKillOptions.description: When an instance of a wasm module is killed and replaced by a fresh one, to bound the memory and the state it accumulates

max_calls.description: The number of calls after which the instance is killed. 2147483647 (no limit) when absent

max_memory_usage.description: The ratio of its memory the instance can use before it is killed, between 0 and 1. 0 (no limit) when absent

max_avg_call_duration.description: The average duration of the calls, in milliseconds, above which the instance is killed. 0 (no limit) when absent

max_unused_duration.description: The time without any call, in milliseconds, after which the instance is killed. 300000 (5 minutes) when absent

InCookie.description: A jwt token read from a cookie of the request

type.description: The location of the token, always `InCookie`

name.description: The name of the cookie holding the token

PluginIndex.description: The position of a plugin in each phase of a call: in a phase, the plugins with a position run first, by increasing position, then the other ones in the order of the chain. Only the phases set are written

sink.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the router plugins choose a route, and the requests no route matched are handled

pre_route.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the request is checked before its access is validated

validate_access.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the access to the route is validated

transform_request.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the request is transformed before being forwarded

transform_response.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the response is transformed before being answered

match_route.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the route is matched

handles_tunnel.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where a tunnel is handled

handles_websocket.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the messages of a websocket are handled

handles_websocket_backend.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the messages a websocket backend sends are handled

call_backend.description: The position of the plugin among the plugins of the route during the phase where the backend is called

UserAnalyticsQueryDefinition.description: A query of the catalog: its id, what it computes, the shape of its result, its parameters and whether it can be compared with the previous period

id.description: The id to use in `POST /api/analytics/_query` and in dashboard widgets

name.description: The readable name of the query, the default title of the widgets the backoffice creates on it

description.description: What the query computes
description.example: Routes with the most requests.

shape.description: The shape of the result of the query, which tells the fields of its `data`

default_widget.description: The widget type that displays the query by default, one of the `widget_types` of the catalog for the built-in queries

params.description: The parameters the query reads in the `params` of a query request, a widget or an alert condition. Empty when it takes none

supports_compare.description: Whether the query can be compared with the previous period: `compare` is ignored when it cannot

example.name: Top routes
example.description: Routes with the most requests.

HSAlgoSettings.description: Tokens signed with HMAC and SHA-2 (`HS256`, `HS384`, `HS512`) using a shared secret

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `HSAlgoSettings`

size.description: The size of the SHA-2 hash of the algorithm, in bits: 256, 384 or 512 (`HS256`, `HS384`, `HS512`)

secret.description: The shared secret. It can be a vault reference like `${vault://local/jwt-secret}`, or an expression like `${env.JWT_SECRET}` or `${config.jwt.secret}`

base64.description: The secret is base64 encoded, it is decoded before use. False when missing

ClusterUserToken.description: A user token: the user an auth module identified, kept for the login flow that follows

token.description: The value the user is stored under: the login token of the login flow, that the callback of the auth module reads the user with

user.description: The user the token stands for: the json of the user the auth module identified (a basic or an ldap user, for a private app or for the backoffice)

MtlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the calls otoroshi makes to a remote server: the client certificates it presents, and the certificates it trusts

certs.description: The ids of the certificates of otoroshi presented as client certificates when `mtls` is true. A certificate can also be designated by its distinguished name, the valid one expiring last is then used

items.description: The id or the distinguished name of a certificate

trustedCerts.description: The ids of the certificates of otoroshi trusted to validate the certificate of the remote server, on top of the default trust store

mtls.description: Use these tls settings for the calls. When false, the default tls settings of otoroshi are used. The legacy `tls` key is read too

loose.description: Do not check the host name of the certificate of the remote server

trustAll.description: Trust any certificate of the remote server. For tests only

ApiTesting.description: The testing of the draft of an api: when enabled, otoroshi also serves the routes of the last saved draft of the api, to the calls that carry a secret header

enabled.description: Whether the routes of the draft are served. Defaults to `false`

headerKey.description: The name of the header the calls to the routes of the draft carry. Defaults to `X-OTOROSHI-TESTING`

headerValue.description: The value the header holds, a secret generated at random when missing

JsonPatchOperation.description: An operation of a json patch (RFC 6902)

op.description: What the operation does (RFC 6902): `add`, `remove` or `replace` the value at `path`, `move` or `copy` the value at `from` to `path`, or `test` that the value at `path` equals `value`

path.description: The json pointer (RFC 6901) of the value the operation applies to

from.description: The json pointer of the value to move or to copy, for the `move` and `copy` operations

value.description: The value to add, to replace with, or to test, for the `add`, `replace` and `test` operations

JavaVersion.description: The java virtual machine an otoroshi instance runs on

version.description: The version of the java virtual machine (its `java.version` system property). The leaders put the major version of their own java when a worker does not send it

vendor.description: The vendor of the java virtual machine (its `java.vendor` system property), `--` when a worker does not send it

SniSettings.description: How a tcp service routes the connections on the domain of the sni of the tls handshake

enabled.description: Whether the connections are routed on their sni domain, which lets several rules share the port. Defaults to `false`

forwardIfNoMatch.description: Whether the connections whose sni domain matches no rule go to `forwardsTo`, instead of being closed. Defaults to `false`

forwardsTo.description: The target of the connections whose sni domain matches no rule, when `forwardIfNoMatch` is true. It is called over plain tcp, its `tls` flag is not used. Defaults to `127.0.0.1:8080`

ExporterRef.description: The settings of a custom exporter, implemented by a plugin of type exporter

ref.description: The reference of the exporter plugin, `cp:` followed by its class name for a plugin of the classpath

config.description: The configuration given to the exporter plugin

FieldsPatch.description: The fields to change and their new value. A value given as a string is read as json when it is `null`, `true`, `false`, a number, an object or an array

items.description: A field and its new value

path.description: The path of the field to change, its keys separated by dots (`frontend.domains`, `metadata.owner`). The objects missing along the path are created

value.description: The new value of the field, replacing the current one. A string holding `null`, `true`, `false`, a number, a json object or a json array is read as that json value

oneOf.description: A string, read as json when it is one

WasmoTlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the calls to a wasmo server (the tls config of the wasm4s library)

certs.description: The ids of the certificates presented as client certificates. A single id given as `certId` or `cert_id` is read too. Empty when absent

trusted_certs.description: The ids of the certificates trusted to validate the certificate of the server. Empty when absent

enabled.description: Use these tls settings for the calls. `false` when absent

loose.description: Do not check the host name of the certificate of the server. `false` when absent

trust_all.description: Trust any certificate of the server. For tests only. `false` when absent

ApiDocumentation.description: The documentation of an api for a developer portal: its pages, its navigation, its logo, its banner, and a remote documentation to merge with it

enabled.description: Whether the documentation is shown. Defaults to `true`

source.description: A remote documentation merged with this one, `null` for none

home.description: The home page of the documentation. Defaults to an empty resource

logo.description: The logo of the api. Defaults to an empty resource

references.description: Links to the references of the api

resources.description: The pages and the files of the documentation

navigation.description: The sidebars of the documentation site, each one shown on the pages of its `path` with its links and its categories of links

redirections.description: The redirections between the paths of the documentation

footer.description: The footer of the documentation, `null` for none

search.description: The search in the documentation. Defaults to an enabled search

banner.description: The banner of the documentation, `null` for none

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the documentation

tags.description: Free tags of the documentation

home.title: Getting started
home.description: How to get an api key and make a first call
home.text_content:
# Getting started

Subscribe to a plan to get an api key, then call `https://api.oto.tools/v1/users` with it.

references.title: OpenAPI specification
references.description: The openapi document of the api

ApiBackend.description: A backend of an api: the targets its routes forward to, with the http client settings of one of the backend clients of the api

id.description: The id of the backend, unique in the api. The routes reference it in `backend`

name.description: The name of the backend, shown in the backoffice. The routes of the api reference the backend by its `id`, not by its name

backend.description: The targets of the backend and how they are reached. Its `client` settings are replaced by the ones of the backend client named by `client` when the routes are built

client.description: The id of the backend client (an entry of `clients_backend_config`) whose http client settings the backend uses, the default settings when it cannot be found. Defaults to `default_backend_client`

OtoroshiExport.description: The whole state of an otoroshi as json: its global configuration and every entity, grouped by kind. The import reads every group as optional (an absent group imports nothing of its kind, an absent `config` the default global configuration) and ignores `label`, `dateRaw`, `date` and `stats`

dateRaw.description: When the export was made, a timestamp in milliseconds

date.description: When the export was made, as `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` (a 24 hours clock)

stats.description: The traffic otoroshi handled since its datastore was created

calls.description: The number of calls otoroshi has handled, a global counter of its datastore

dataIn.description: The number of bytes otoroshi has received in the calls it handled, a global counter of its datastore

dataOut.description: The number of bytes otoroshi has sent in the calls it handled, a global counter of its datastore

config.description: The global configuration of otoroshi (`config.otoroshi.io/GlobalConfig`). The import saves the default one when it is missing

admins.description: The admins who log in with webauthn

items.description: An admin who logs in with webauthn: its username, password hash, webauthn credentials, rights and metadata

simpleAdmins.description: The admins who log in with a username and a password

apiKeys.description: Every api key (`apim.otoroshi.io/Apikey` entities), with its client secret

serviceDescriptors.description: Service descriptors of an export made before otoroshi 18: the import converts each one into a route. Never written by the export

errorTemplates.description: Every error template (`proxy.otoroshi.io/ErrorTemplate` entities), the custom error pages of the routes

certificates.description: Every certificate (`pki.otoroshi.io/Certificate` entities), with its private key

scripts.description: Every script (`plugins.otoroshi.io/Script` entities): the legacy plugins otoroshi compiles

backends.description: Every stored backend (`proxy.otoroshi.io/Backend` entities), the backends the routes can reference by id

drafts.description: Every draft (`proxy.otoroshi.io/Draft` entities): the versions of the entities edited in the backoffice and not published yet

apiSubscriptions.description: Every subscription to an api (`apis.otoroshi.io/ApiSubscription` entities)

extensions.description: The entities of the admin extensions, by id of extension

additionalProperties.description: The entities of an admin extension, by kind of entity

items.description: An entity of the admin extension

apiKeys.description: The apikey used by the Otoroshi UI

GroupRights.description: A virtual group of an LDAP auth module: rights added to some users

rights.description: The rights added to the users of the group. `[{"tenant": "*:rw", "teams": ["*:rw"]}]` makes a super admin

users.description: The emails of the users of the group

ApiFromOpenApiRequest.description: Where an openapi document is, and where the api built from it is exposed. Every field is required

domain.description: The domain the api is exposed on

openapi.description: The url of the openapi (or swagger) document, fetched by otoroshi. A yaml document has to be served with an `application/yaml` or `text/yaml` content type, anything else is read as json

contextPath.description: The path the routes of the api are exposed under

backendHostname.description: The hostname of the targets of the backend of the api, one target per server of the document

backendPath.description: The root path of the backend of the api

_loc.description: The location of the api to build, which the admin behind the credentials has to be able to write. The default tenant (organization) and team when absent. The api built is in the default location anyway

ServiceDescriptor.description: A legacy service descriptor, the way otoroshi 17 and older described a service. Its main fields are described here, the other ones (headers, security, client settings, canary, plugins, ...) are read the way otoroshi 17 wrote them. Every field is optional: the template of a new descriptor gives the missing ones

id.description: The id of the descriptor, kept as the id of the route

name.description: The name of the descriptor, given to the converted route

description.description: The description of the descriptor, given to the converted route
description.example: The users service

enabled.description: Whether the descriptor serves calls

groups.description: The ids of the service groups of the descriptor

items.description: The id of a service group

env.description: The environment of the descriptor, part of its legacy domain (`<subdomain>.<env>.<domain>`, without the env when it is `prod`)

domain.description: The domain of the legacy domain of the descriptor

subdomain.description: The subdomain of the legacy domain of the descriptor

hosts.description: The hosts the descriptor matches, besides the legacy domain built from `subdomain`, `env` and `domain` (unless `handleLegacyDomain` is false). Each host, followed by each of the `paths` (by `matchingRoot`, or `/`, when there is none), becomes a domain of the converted route

paths.description: The path prefixes the descriptor matches on each of its hosts. Each of them, after each host, becomes a domain of the converted route

matchingRoot.description: The path prefix the descriptor matches, removed from the forwarded path

stripPath.description: Whether the matched path is removed from the forwarded path

root.description: The path prefix of the calls forwarded to the targets

targets.description: The targets the calls are forwarded to

items.description: A target of the descriptor. Its other fields (protocol, predicate, ip address, mtls configuration, backup, ...) are read the way otoroshi 17 wrote them

host.description: The host of the target, with its port if any

scheme.description: The scheme of the target, `https` by default

weight.description: The weight of the target in the load balancing, 1 by default

publicPatterns.description: The regular expressions of the paths that need no api key

privatePatterns.description: The regular expressions of the paths that need an api key even when they match a public pattern

forceHttps.description: Whether http calls are redirected to https

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the descriptor, given to the converted route along with the `otoroshi-core-` keys that keep its legacy settings (`otoroshi-core-legacy`, `otoroshi-core-env`...)

tags.description: Free tags of the descriptor, given to the converted route with an `env:<env>` tag added

DataExporterConfig.otlp-metrics.description: A data exporter of type `otlp-metrics`: metrics computed from the events are sent to an OpenTelemetry collector

type.description: The type of the exporter: `otlp-metrics`, metrics computed from the events are sent to an OpenTelemetry collector

enabled.description: Whether the exporter runs. A disabled exporter keeps its settings but exports nothing. Defaults to false

id.description: The unique id of the exporter, the key it is stored under and the `{id}` of its urls in the admin api. The templates generate `data_exporter_<uuid>` (`data_exporter_<env>_<uuid>` outside the `prod` environment)

name.description: The display name of the exporter, shown in the backoffice

desc.description: A description of the exporter. Defaults to `--`
desc.example: Metrics to the OpenTelemetry collector, managed by the platform team

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the exporter

tags.description: Free tags of the exporter, to search and sort it

bufferSize.description: The maximum number of events waiting to be exported. Once it is reached, the oldest waiting events are dropped. Defaults to 5000

jsonWorkers.description: The number of events turned into json (and enriched) in parallel. Defaults to 1

sendWorkers.description: The number of batches sent in parallel. Defaults to 5

groupSize.description: The maximum number of events of a batch: a batch is sent once it is full or once `groupDuration` is elapsed. Defaults to 100

groupDuration.description: The maximum delay before a batch is sent, in milliseconds, even when it is not full. Defaults to 30000

projection.description: The fields of the events that are exported, as a json object: `{"field": true}` keeps a field, operators like `$at`, `$path`, `$jq` or `$date_from_unix_fmt` compute new ones (see the documentation of the data exporters). An empty object exports the whole events

customFilter.description: A custom filter, applied after `filtering`: the events it refuses are not exported. Null for none

customTransform.description: A custom transformation of the events, applied before they are exported. Null for none

example.name: Metrics to the OpenTelemetry collector
example.desc: Metrics to the OpenTelemetry collector, managed by the platform team

HostMetrics.description: The metrics of the jvm and of the host of the otoroshi instance that answers

cpu_usage.description: The cpu load of the otoroshi process, in percent

heap_used.description: The memory of the heap in use, in megabytes

heap_size.description: The memory of the heap the jvm holds, in megabytes

live_threads.description: The number of threads alive in the jvm, the daemon threads included

live_peak_threads.description: The highest number of live threads since the jvm started

daemon_threads.description: The number of daemon threads alive in the jvm, a part of `live_threads`

env.description: The `APP_ENV` environment variable, `--` when it is not set

commit_id.description: The `COMMIT_ID` environment variable, `--` when it is not set

instance_number.description: The `INSTANCE_NUMBER` environment variable, `--` when it is not set

app_id.description: The `APP_ID` environment variable, `--` when it is not set

instance_id.description: The `INSTANCE_ID` environment variable, `--` when it is not set

ApiDocumentationSidebar.description: A sidebar of a documentation: its links and its categories of links

label.description: The label of the sidebar. Defaults to an empty string

oneOf.description: The path as a single string

path.description: The path the sidebar is shown on, as segments or as a single string

items.description: An entry of the sidebar, a category when its `kind` is `category`, a link otherwise
The entries of the sidebar: links, and categories of links

icon.description: The icon shown next to the label of the sidebar: a documentation resource holding an image or a css icon class (`css_icon_class`). Optional

DataExporterConfigFiltering.description: The events a data exporter keeps. An event is exported when it matches one of the `include` filters (or when there is none) and none of the `exclude` filters. A filter is a json object the event has to match, field by field, with operators like `$wildcard`, `$regex`, `$gt`, `$in`, `$contains`, `$or`, `$not` (see the documentation of the data exporters)

include.description: The filters of the events to export, one of them has to match. Empty to export every event

items.description: A filter the event has to match

exclude.description: The filters of the events not to export, an event matching one of them is dropped

items.description: A filter the event must not match

EntityGraph.description: The entities that use an entity. Empty for the kinds of entities that are not supported

routes.description: The routes, among the ones the admin behind the credentials can read, whose plugin configurations contain the id of the jwt verifier, as route entities. Only answered for a jwt verifier

NoneMailerSettings.description: No mailer: the emails are dropped

type.description: The type of the mailer, `none`

security.otoroshi.io.AuthModuleUser.description: The session of a user logged in to a private app (a route using the `Authentication` plugin) through an auth module. It is created when the user logs in, and removed when it logs out or when it expires: the api reads and deletes them, it does not create nor update them

randomId.description: The id of the session, a random token

name.description: The display name of the user, read from the profile given by the identity provider (the `nameField` of the module for instance), shown in the list of the private apps sessions of the backoffice

email.description: The email of the user, read from its profile: the `allowedUsers` and `deniedUsers` of the module are checked against it, and the `dataOverride` of the module is keyed by it

authConfigId.description: The id of the auth module the user logged in with. `none` when missing

profile.description: The profile of the user given by the identity provider, checked by the user validators of the module. Its shape depends on the provider

token.description: The tokens given by the identity provider (access token, refresh token...). Its shape depends on the provider. `{}` when missing

realm.description: The realm of the session: the type and the id of its auth module, also the suffix of its cookie. `none` when missing

otoroshiData.description: The otoroshi data of the user sent to the backends of the private apps (in the otoroshi claim): any json value, usually an object, null when the user has none

createdAt.description: When the session was created, a timestamp in milliseconds

expiredAt.description: When the session expires, a timestamp in milliseconds

lastRefresh.description: When the tokens of the session were last refreshed, a timestamp in milliseconds

metadata.description: The metadata of the session, free key/value pairs

tags.description: Free tags of the session: the tags of the auth module for an OAuth2 / OpenID Connect login, the ones the plugin or the workflow answers for a wasm or a workflow module, none for the other modules

NodeInfos.description: What an otoroshi instance is: its cluster, its version, its runtime and its datastore

otoroshi_cluster_id.description: The id of the otoroshi cluster (the `otoroshiId` of the global configuration)

otoroshi_version.description: The version of otoroshi the instance runs, as written (the `raw` of `otoroshi_version_sem`)

backoffice_url.description: The url of the backoffice of the instance, built from `app.rootScheme`, the backoffice subdomain (`app.backoffice.subdomain`), `app.domain` and the exposed port

datastore.description: The kind of datastore of the instance, as set by `app.storage` (`lettuce` when not set): `inmemory`, `file`, `lettuce`, `redis`, `postgresql`, `cassandra`, `s3`, `http`...

env.description: The environment of the instance, as set by `app.env` (`prod` when not set, `dev` for a development instance)

HttpCallSettings.description: The settings of an http exporter: each batch of events is sent in an http call whose body is built from a template

url.description: The url each batch of events is sent to

method.description: The http method of the call. Defaults to `GET`

headers.description: The http headers sent with each call, for instance its `Content-Type` or an `Authorization` header

name.description: The name of the cookie. Mandatory: settings holding a cookie without name cannot be read

value.description: The value of the cookie. Mandatory: settings holding a cookie without value cannot be read

path.description: The `Path` attribute of the cookie, null for none

domain.description: The `Domain` attribute of the cookie, null for none

http_only.description: Whether the cookie is http only. Defaults to false

max_age.description: The max age of the cookie, in seconds

secure.description: Whether the cookie is secure. Defaults to false

body.description: The template of the body of the call, sent once its placeholders are replaced: `${events}` or `${events.stringify}` by the events as a json array, `${events.prettify}` by the same array pretty printed, `${events.nd_stringify}` by the json of each event separated by an empty line, `${events.nd_prettify}` by the pretty printed json of each event separated by an empty line, `${events.length}` by their number, `${now}` by the current timestamp in milliseconds, `${now_epoch}` by the current timestamp in seconds and `${now_str}` by the current date. Empty when absent

timeout.description: The timeout of a call, in milliseconds. Defaults to 60000

tls_config.description: The tls settings of the calls to the url

UserAnalyticsSetActiveExporterResponse.description: The outcome of the activation of a user-analytics data exporter

ok.description: Always `true`: the exporter is now the active one

active.description: The id of the data exporter that is now the active user-analytics data exporter, the `id` of the path

demoted_count.description: The number of the other exporters that were flagged as active before

seeded_default.description: The `otoroshi-default-id` metadata of the default dashboards that were missing and are now created

ApiPricing.description: What a plan costs, shown in a developer portal. Otoroshi does not charge the consumers itself

id.description: An id of the pricing, stored as it is sent: otoroshi does not use it

enabled.description: Whether the plan is charged

name.description: The name of the offer the pricing describes, shown with its price in a developer portal

price.description: The price of the plan, in `currency`

currency.description: The code of the currency of the price (ISO 4217)

params.description: Free parameters of the pricing, any json value (for instance the billing period). Defaults to an empty object

SignCertResponse.description: A certificate signed by a certificate authority of otoroshi from a certificate signing request. Nothing is stored

csr.description: The certificate signing request the certificate was signed from, PEM encoded

ca.description: The certificate of the certificate authority that signed the certificate, PEM encoded

TunnelsEndpoint.description: How this otoroshi is reached: what a remote otoroshi needs to connect its tunnels to it

domain.description: The domain this otoroshi exposes its admin api and its services under (`app.domain`, `oto.tools` by default)

scheme.description: The scheme this otoroshi is exposed with (`app.rootScheme`)

exposed_port_http.description: The http port clients reach this otoroshi on (`app.exposed-ports.http`, the http port it listens on by default)

exposed_port_https.description: The https port clients reach this otoroshi on (`app.exposed-ports.https`, the https port it listens on by default)

Proxies.description: The http proxies the calls of otoroshi go through, one per kind of call. null: the calls are direct. A proxy without host or port reads as null

alertEmails.description: The proxy of the calls to the apis of the mailers

eventsWebhooks.description: The proxy of the calls to the webhooks of the events

clevercloud.description: The proxy of the calls to the api of Clever Cloud

services.description: The proxy of the calls to the backends of the routes, of their health checks and of the traffic mirroring

auth.description: The proxy of the calls to the identity providers of the auth modules (OAuth2, OIDC)

authority.description: The proxy of the calls to the remote validation authorities (client certificate validators, external validations)

jwk.description: The proxy of the calls fetching the JWKS of the jwt verifiers

elastic.description: The proxy of the calls to Elasticsearch

WorkflowCallSettings.description: The settings of a workflow exporter: each batch of events is given to a workflow, as `events` in its input (with the exporter as `config`)

LoadBalancingCookieHash.description: The `CookieHash` load balancing: sends the requests to the target chosen by consistent hashing of the value of a cookie, in turn when the request does not hold the cookie

type.description: Selects the load balancing on a cookie: the requests holding the same value of the `cookie_name` cookie go to the same target

cookie_name.description: The name of the cookie. Defaults to `session-id`

BulkOperationError.description: A line a bulk operation refused

status.description: The http status the line would get as a single call: 404 when the entity to update does not exist, the status of the refusal when the validation of the entity refused it, 400 otherwise (a line that cannot be read, an entity the credentials cannot change, an entity to patch or to delete that does not exist)

error.description: The error, as a short code, like `bad_entity`, or `bad_request` when the validation of the entity refused it

error_description.description: Why the line was refused: a message, the messages of the validation, the errors of the fields that could not be read, or the error of the lookup of the entity

oneOf.description: The errors of the fields that could not be read, or the error of the lookup

entity.description: The line refused. For a bulk patch whose entity is not found, the patch of the line

catalogs.otoroshi.io.RemoteCatalog.description: A remote catalog: a source outside otoroshi (an http endpoint, a file, a git repository of github, gitlab, bitbucket, gitea, forgejo or codeberg, an s3 bucket, a consul kv store) holding entity definitions in json or yaml. Deploying the catalog reconciles otoroshi with the source: the entities it holds are created or updated, the ones it created before and that the source no longer holds are deleted. It is deployed through the api, on a schedule, or from a webhook

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams the remote catalog belongs to. The default tenant and team when absent

id.description: The unique id of the remote catalog, used to deploy it. The entities it creates carry it in their metadata, as `created_by: remote_catalog=<id>`

name.description: The display name of the remote catalog, shown and searched in the list of the remote catalogs of the backoffice

description.description: A free text describing the remote catalog, shown in its form of the backoffice. `--` when absent
description.example: The routes and backends of the infrastructure repository

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the remote catalog, with string values. The admin api stores the date of the last write of the entity under `created_at` or `updated_at`

tags.description: Free tags of the remote catalog, to sort and search the catalogs

enabled.description: Whether the remote catalog is deployed by its schedule and by the webhook plugin, true when absent. A disabled catalog can still be deployed through the api

source_kind.description: The kind of source the entities are fetched from, that tells how `source_config` is read: `http`, `file`, `github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket` (bitbucket cloud), `bitbucketserver` (bitbucket server / data center), `gitea`, `forgejo`, `codeberg`, `git` (any git repository, cloned), `s3` or `consulkv`, or the kind of a source registered by an extension. `http` when absent

source_config.description: The configuration of the source, read according to `source_kind`: each kind reads the fields listed below that name it, and ignores the others. Free json object, empty when absent

url.description: `http`: the url of the document to fetch, that holds entities or is a catalog listing naming the documents to deploy (relative to the same url)

headers.description: `http`: the headers sent with the request, by name

timeout.description: `http`: the timeout of the request, in milliseconds, 30000 when absent

path.description: `file`: the path of the file or directory to read on the otoroshi host. Git sources: the path of the file or directory in the repository, the root of the repository when absent. A file can be a catalog listing that names the files to deploy

pre_command.description: `file`: a command run before the files are read (to pull a repository for instance), as the program followed by its arguments

items.description: The program or one of its arguments

repo.description: `github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`, `bitbucketserver`, `gitea`, `forgejo`, `codeberg`: the repository, as `owner/name`, or an organization, a group, a workspace or a project to scan all its repositories. `git`: the url of the repository to clone, over https or ssh

branch.description: Git sources: the branch to read, `main` when absent

token.description: Git sources: the token used to call the api of the forge, or added to the https url of a `git` repository. `consulkv`: the acl token

username.description: `bitbucket`, `bitbucketserver`, `git`: the user name that goes with the token

base_url.description: `github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`, `bitbucketserver`, `gitea`, `forgejo`, `codeberg`: the base url of the api of the forge, for a self hosted one. `https://api.github.com`, `https://gitlab.com`, `https://api.bitbucket.org`, `http://localhost:7990`, `http://localhost:3000` (gitea, forgejo) and `https://codeberg.org` when absent

repo_patterns.description: Git forges, when `repo` is an organization: the glob patterns of the names of the repositories to scan, all of them when absent

items.description: A glob pattern of repository names

ssh_private_key_path.description: `git`: the path of the private ssh key used to clone a repository over ssh

key.description: `s3`: the key of the object to read, that can be a catalog listing naming the objects to deploy

endpoint.description: `s3`: the url of the s3 endpoint, `https://s3.amazonaws.com` when absent. `consulkv`: the url of the consul http api, `http://localhost:8500` when absent

region.description: `s3`: the region of the bucket, `eu-west-1` when absent

prefix.description: `consulkv`: the key to read, or the prefix of the keys to read (the ones ending with `.json`, `.yaml` or `.yml`)

dc.description: `consulkv`: the datacenter to read from, the one of the agent when absent

scheduling.description: Deploys the remote catalog as a job of otoroshi: once, at a fixed interval or on a cron expression. Not scheduled when absent or invalid

test_deploy_args.description: The arguments given to the source when the catalog is deployed or tested from the backoffice. Free json object, empty when absent

example.name: Infrastructure catalog
example.description: The routes and backends of the infrastructure repository

proxy.otoroshi.io.RouteComposition.description: Several routes sharing the same settings and plugins, written as one entity: each of its routes becomes a route of the proxy with the settings, the client and the plugins of the composition

id.description: The unique id of the route composition, also the id of the routes it generates

name.description: The display name of the route composition

description.description: A free text describing the route composition
description.example: The routes of the users api

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the route compositions, also used by automation tools

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the route composition

enabled.description: Whether the routes of the composition are served. Defaults to `true`

debug_flow.description: Whether the execution report of each call holds the input and the output of every step and plugin, to debug the routes. Defaults to `false`

export_reporting.description: Whether the execution report of each call is sent as a `RequestFlowReport` event to the data exporters. Defaults to `false`

capture.description: Whether each call generates a `TrafficCaptureEvent` holding the request and the response, bodies included, for the data exporters. Defaults to `false`

items.description: The id of a service group

groups.description: The ids of the service groups the routes belong to. An api key authorized on one of them can call the routes. Defaults to `["default"]`

routes.description: The routes of the composition. A route that cannot be read is left out

client.description: How otoroshi calls the targets of every route of the composition

plugins.description: The plugins applied to the calls of every route of the composition, after the plugins of the route itself

example.name: Users API
example.description: The routes of the users api

OAuth2RemoteAccessModeConfiguration.description: The access mode `oauth2-remote`: the consumers call with a token of an OAuth2 / OIDC provider, checked against the settings of an auth module, the consumer being the client id read from a claim of the token. Each consumer gets an api key of its own built from the plan

verifier.description: The id of the auth module whose OAuth2 / OIDC settings check the tokens

client_id_path.description: The claim of the token holding the client id of the consumer (`client_id`, `azp` or `cid` depending on the provider). `null` for `client_id`

fetch_user.description: Whether the userinfo endpoint of the module is called to store the profile of the holder of the token in a metadata of the api key. The call stays a consumer call, no user session is attached to it. Defaults to `false`

user_metadata_key.description: The metadata of the api key holding the profile of the user. Defaults to `user_profile`

create_if_missing.description: Whether the api key minted for a consumer seen for the first time is stored, and shows up in the api keys of otoroshi. Otherwise it only lives for the duration of the call. Either way the call is served and counted. `true` when the configuration does not say, and for a plan without any configuration

ScalewayTEMSettings.description: A mailer sending the emails through Transactional Email, the email api of Scaleway

type.description: The type of the mailer, `scaleway`

secretKey.description: The secret key of the Scaleway api key

projectId.description: The id of the Scaleway project the emails are sent from

region.description: The Scaleway region of the api. `fr-par` when absent or blank

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

ESKPAlgoSettings.description: Tokens signed with ECDSA and SHA-2 (`ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512`) using the key pair of a certificate of otoroshi

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `ESKPAlgoSettings`

size.description: The size of the SHA-2 hash of the algorithm, in bits: 256, 384 or 512 (`ES256`, `ES384`, `ES512`)

certId.description: The id of the certificate holding the EC key pair. Its id is also the `kid` of the tokens otoroshi signs

ConsoleMailerSettings.description: A mailer that only writes the emails to the logs of otoroshi, for tests

type.description: The type of the mailer, `console`

JWKSAlgoSettings.description: Tokens verified with the public keys of a remote JSON Web Key Set, like the `jwks_uri` of an OpenID Connect provider. The key is chosen by the `kid` of the token. The key set is cached for `ttl` milliseconds. Only verifies tokens, it cannot sign them

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `JWKSAlgoSettings`

url.description: The url of the JSON Web Key Set

timeout.description: The timeout of the call fetching the key set, in milliseconds. 2000 when missing

headers.description: The http headers sent with the call fetching the key set

ttl.description: How long the fetched key set is cached, in milliseconds. 3600000 (one hour) when missing

kty.description: The type of the keys of the key set (`RSA` or `EC` to verify RSA or ECDSA signatures). `RSA` when missing

proxy.description: The http proxy used to fetch the key set, null to use the jwk proxy of the global configuration

tls_config.description: A copy of `mtlsConfig`, written for the older clients. It is only read when `mtlsConfig` and `tlsConfig` are missing

mtlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the call fetching the key set. The legacy `tlsConfig` and `tls_config` keys are read when it is missing

ApiDuplicationResult.description: The outcome of the duplication of an api: the id of the copy, saved in the `staging` state

id.description: The id generated for the copy (`api_<uuid>`), to read it with `GET /apis/apis.otoroshi.io/v1/apis/{id}`

UserAnalyticsTimeseriesSeries.description: A named series of a multi-series timeseries

name.description: The name of the series, like `p95`, `data_in` or `5xx`

points.description: The points of the series, one per bucket

RemoteUserValidatorSettings.description: A remote service that validates the users logging in through an auth module: otoroshi posts it `{"user": ..., "auth_module": ..., "route": ...}` (`service_descriptor` instead of `route` for the backoffice) and lets the user in when it answers 200 with `{"valid": true}`. Otherwise the `reason` of the answer (`{"display": ..., "internal": ...}`) is the error

url.description: The url otoroshi posts the user to

headers.description: The http headers sent with the call

timeout.description: The timeout of the call, in milliseconds. 10000 when missing

tls_settings.description: The tls settings of the call to the remote service: the certificates it trusts and the client certificate it presents (mtls). The default settings when missing

UserAnalyticsQueryData.description: The result of a query. Its fields depend on `shape`: `scalar` has `value` and `label`, `pie` has `label` and `items` (with `key` and `value`), `topN` has `items` (with `key`, `label` and `value`), `timeseries` has `bucket` and either `points` (one series) or `series` (several named series), `heatmap` has `bucket`, `xBuckets`, `yBuckets` and `values`. The layout of `metric` and `table` results, and of the results of the queries of admin extensions, is up to the extension providing the query

label.description: The label of a `scalar` or `pie` result

items.description: The items of a `pie` or `topN` result, biggest first

bucket.description: The time bucket size of a `timeseries` or `heatmap` result

points.description: The points of a single series `timeseries` result, one per bucket

series.description: The series of a multi-series `timeseries` result

xBuckets.description: The time buckets of a `heatmap` result (X axis), as unix timestamps in milliseconds

yBuckets.description: The response time ranges of a `heatmap` result (Y axis), from `<50ms` to `>=3s`

values.description: The request counts of a `heatmap` result, one row per `yBuckets` entry and one column per `xBuckets` entry

SAMLCredential.description: A certificate and its private key used by a SAML auth module: given in PEM format, or taken from a certificate of otoroshi

certificate.description: The certificate in PEM format, null when it is taken from otoroshi

privateKey.description: The private key of the certificate in PEM format, null when it is taken from otoroshi

certId.description: The id of the certificate of otoroshi to use when `useOtoroshiCertificate` is true

useOtoroshiCertificate.description: Use the certificate of otoroshi `certId` instead of `certificate` and `privateKey`. False when missing

WasmAuthModuleConfig.description: A wasm auth module: the login flow is implemented by a wasm plugin

type.description: The type of the auth module, `wasm` for a wasm auth module

id.description: The unique id of the auth module, named by the `module` of the `Authentication` plugin of the routes, the `modules` of the `Multi Authentication` plugin, or the `backOfficeAuthRef` of the global configuration

name.description: The display name of the auth module, shown in the backoffice and on the login page of the routes that offer several auth modules (`Multi Authentication` plugin)

desc.description: The description of the auth module. A `description` key is read first. `--` when missing
desc.example: Login with the custom flow of the company

tags.description: Free tags of the auth module, to search and sort it

metadata.description: The metadata of the auth module, free key/value pairs

sessionMaxAge.description: How long a session lasts, in seconds. 86400 (a day) when missing

clientSideSessionEnabled.description: Also keep the session of the users of the private apps in an encrypted cookie, so that a session missing from the datastore of otoroshi (not synchronized yet on an instance of the cluster, lost by a restart) is restored from it. False when missing, as for a new module

sessionCookieValues.description: The `HttpOnly` and `Secure` flags of the session cookies set on the private apps once a user has logged in through the module. Both true when missing

userValidators.description: The checks of the profile of a user that logs in. Every check has to pass for the user to get in

example.error: the user is not a member of the admins group

remoteValidators.description: The remote services that validate a user that logs in. Every service has to accept the user

allowedUsers.description: The users allowed to log in, by email. Everybody when empty

pki.otoroshi.io.Certificate.description: A certificate: an X509 certificate chain and its private key, stored in otoroshi and used to serve tls (picked by SNI from its domain and SANs), to present a client certificate to backends (mtls), to trust remote servers or clients, or as a key pair to sign and verify jwt tokens. Otoroshi can generate them with its own pki, get them from Let's Encrypt, and renew them. The boolean flags are also read from the strings `true` and `false`

id.description: The id of the certificate, referenced by the routes, backends, verifiers and tls settings

domain.description: The main domain of the certificate, the common name of its subject. Computed from the chain by otoroshi when the certificate is saved, read back as is otherwise. `--` when unknown

name.description: The display name of the certificate, shown and searched in the list of the certificates of the backoffice. Defaults to the domain

description.description: A free text describing the certificate, shown and searched in the list of the certificates of the backoffice. `Certificate for <domain>` when absent
description.example: Certificate of the public api

chain.description: The certificate chain, PEM encoded: the certificate first, then the certificates of the authorities that signed it. Empty for a key pair only entity

caRef.description: The id of the certificate of the authority (an otoroshi CA) that signed this one, used to renew it. Null when it was not signed by an otoroshi CA

privateKey.description: The private key of the certificate, PEM encoded (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1). Empty for a certificate only trusted, like the certificate of a remote authority

selfSigned.description: Whether the certificate is self signed. Computed from the chain by otoroshi when the certificate is saved, read back as is otherwise

ca.description: Whether the certificate is a certificate authority, able to sign other certificates. Computed from the chain by otoroshi when the certificate is saved, read back as is otherwise

valid.description: Whether the private key matches the chain, so that the certificate can be used to serve tls. Computed from the chain by otoroshi when the certificate is saved, read back as is otherwise

exposed.description: Whether the public key of the certificate is exposed in the JWKS of otoroshi (`/.well-known/otoroshi/security/jwks.json`), so that others can verify the tokens it signs

revoked.description: Whether the certificate is revoked: otoroshi stops using it and its OCSP responder says so

autoRenew.description: Whether otoroshi renews the certificate before it expires (with its CA, or with Let's Encrypt for a Let's Encrypt certificate)

letsEncrypt.description: Whether the certificate was issued by Let's Encrypt (ACME), and is renewed through it

subject.description: The distinguished name of the subject of the certificate. Computed from the chain by otoroshi when the certificate is saved, read back as is otherwise. `--` when unknown

from.description: The start of the validity of the certificate, a timestamp in milliseconds. Computed from the chain by otoroshi when the certificate is saved, read back as is otherwise

to.description: The end of the validity of the certificate, a timestamp in milliseconds. Computed from the chain by otoroshi when the certificate is saved, read back as is otherwise

client.description: Whether the certificate is a client certificate, presented by otoroshi to the backends that require mtls. A client certificate is not used to serve tls

keypair.description: Whether the entity is only used as a key pair, for instance to sign and verify jwt tokens, and not to serve tls

sans.description: The subject alternative names of the certificate: the other domains it is valid for. Computed from the chain by otoroshi when the certificate is saved, read back as is otherwise

items.description: A domain name, possibly a wildcard

certType.description: The kind of certificate, written by otoroshi from its flags, in this order of precedence: `client`, `ca`, `letsEncrypt`, `keypair`, `selfSigned`, then `certificate`. It is not read back

password.description: The password of the private key when it is encrypted, null otherwise. A blank password is read as null

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the certificate

tags.description: Free tags of the certificate, to search and sort it

outageDurationTo.description: The longest duration of an outage, in milliseconds. Defaults to 3600000 (1 hour)

targetGroups.description: The ids of the groups whose routes can be put in outage. Empty: every group

issuerDN.description: The distinguished name of the issuer of the certificate

notAfter.description: The end of the validity period of the certificate, a timestamp in milliseconds

notBefore.description: The start of the validity period of the certificate, a timestamp in milliseconds

serialNumber.description: The serial number of the certificate, in lowercase hexadecimal

serialNumberLng.description: The serial number of the certificate, as a number. It can be greater than a 64 bits integer: `serialNumber` holds the exact value, as a json or yaml reader that keeps 34 significant digits, like the one of otoroshi, rounds the larger ones (a serial number has up to 49 digits)

sigAlgName.description: The name of the signature algorithm of the certificate

sigAlgOID.description: The object identifier of the signature algorithm of the certificate

_signature.description: The signature of the certificate, base64 encoded

signature.description: The sha-256 digest of the signature of the certificate, as uppercase hexadecimal bytes separated by colons

subjectDN.description: The distinguished name of the subject of the certificate

domain.description: The main domain of the certificate: its first subject alternative name, or the common name of its subject, or its whole subject

rawDomain.description: The common name of the subject of the certificate, null when it has none

version.description: The version of the X509 format of the certificate

type.description: The type of the certificate, as named by the java certificate factory: always `X.509`

publicKey.description: The public key of the certificate, PEM encoded

selfSigned.description: Whether the certificate is self signed

constraints.description: The basic constraints of the certificate: -1 when it is not a certificate authority, otherwise the number of intermediate certificate authorities allowed under it (2147483647 when unlimited)

ca.description: Whether the certificate is a certificate authority

client.description: Whether the certificate can authenticate a client (extended key usage `clientAuth`)

subAltNames.description: The subject alternative names of the certificate

cExtensions.description: The extensions of the certificate marked critical, that a reader has to understand to accept the certificate (like the basic constraints or the key usages)

ncExtensions.description: The extensions of the certificate that are not marked critical (like the subject alternative names)

version.description: The version of the copy. `vnew` when absent

NodeHealth.description: The health of an otoroshi instance and of its components

datastore.description: The health of the datastore, probed with a call to it: `healthy` when it answers, `unreachable` when the call fails, `unhealthy` when its driver reports it so

proxy.description: Whether the http handler of the instance processes a test request (`GET /otoroshi-engine-self-health-check` on the host `otoroshi-engine.self-health-check.local`)

status.description: `healthy` when the test request was processed, `down` when processing it failed

storage.description: The health of the datastore again, in the shape of the other components

initialized.description: Always `true`: the datastore probe needs no initialization

eventstore.description: The health of the Elasticsearch cluster the analytics are read from (`elasticReadsConfig` of the global configuration), checked every 10 seconds

initialized.description: Whether the event store was checked at least once

status.description: `healthy` when the last check reached Elasticsearch, `down` when it failed, `unknown` before the first check or when the analytics are not read from Elasticsearch

certificates.description: Whether the certificates are loaded into the tls stack of the instance

initialized.description: Whether the first load of the certificates is done

status.description: `loaded` once the first load of the certificates is done, `loading` before

scripts.description: Whether the scripts (the plugins otoroshi compiles) are compiled

compiling.description: Whether scripts are being compiled right now

initialized.description: Whether the first compilation of the scripts is done (always `true` when there is no script)

cluster.description: The health of the cluster, absent when the cluster mode is `Off`. A leader tells the health of its members (`health`), a worker its link to the leaders (`status`, `lastSync`, `worker`)

health.description: On a leader, the worst health of the members: `healthy`, `notthathealthy` when a member was not seen for half its timeout, `unhealthy` for three quarters of it

lastSync.description: On a worker, when the state was last loaded from the leaders

worker.description: On a worker, whether it loaded the state and can serve requests

status.description: `loaded` when the worker has loaded the state from the leaders and can serve requests, `loading` otherwise

initialized.description: Whether the worker can serve requests

enabled.description: Whether the remote catalog is deployed as a job, false when absent

kind.description: When the job runs: `ScheduledOnce` once after `initial_delay`, `ScheduledEvery` after `initial_delay` then every `interval`, `Cron` on `cron_expression`, `Autonomous` once after `initial_delay`. Read without case, an unknown value is read as `ScheduledEvery`, which is also the default

instantiation.description: Where the job runs in a cluster: `OneInstancePerOtoroshiInstance` on every instance, `OneInstancePerOtoroshiWorkerInstance` on every worker, `OneInstancePerOtoroshiLeaderInstance` on every leader, `OneInstancePerOtoroshiCluster` on a single instance of the cluster. initial_delay.description: The delay before the first deployment, in milliseconds. No delay when null

interval.description: The delay between two deployments of a `ScheduledEvery` job, in milliseconds. A `ScheduledEvery` job without interval only runs once

cron_expression.description: The quartz cron expression (seconds, minutes, hours, day of month, month, day of week) of a `Cron` job

deploy_args.description: The arguments given to the source on each scheduled deployment. Free json object, empty when absent

id.description: The unique id of the route, written as `@serviceId` in the analytics events of its calls. An api key is authorized on the route with `route_<id>` in its `authorizedEntities`. The template generates `route_<uuid>`

name.description: The name of the route, shown in the backoffice and written as `@service` in the analytics events of its calls

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the routes, also used by automation tools

enabled.description: Whether the route is served. A disabled route is ignored by the router. Defaults to `true`

debug_flow.description: Whether the execution report of each call holds the input and the output of every step and plugin, to debug the route. Defaults to `false`

export_reporting.description: Whether the execution report of each call is sent as a `RequestFlowReport` event to the data exporters. Defaults to `false`

capture.description: Whether each call generates a `TrafficCaptureEvent` holding the request and the response, bodies included, for the data exporters. Use with care. Defaults to `false`

groups.description: The ids of the service groups the route belongs to. An api key authorized on one of them can call the route. Defaults to `["default"]`

items.description: The id of an http listener

bound_listeners.description: The ids of the http listeners the route is bound to. A listener that is exclusive only serves the routes bound to it. Empty: the route is served by the standard listeners

frontend.description: What requests the route matches: domains, paths, methods, headers, query params and cookies

UserAnalyticsExporterSettings.description: The settings of a user-analytics data exporter (its `config`): the PostgreSQL database the exporter writes the events to, where the user analytics queries, dashboards and alerts read them

uri.description: A PostgreSQL connection uri, like `postgresql://user:password@host:5432/database`. Used instead of the other connection settings when present and not empty

host.description: The host name or ip address of the PostgreSQL server. Ignored when `uri` is set

port.description: The port of the PostgreSQL server. Ignored when `uri` is set

database.description: The PostgreSQL database that holds the tables. Ignored when `uri` is set

user.description: The PostgreSQL user otoroshi connects as. It must be allowed to create the schema, the tables and the indexes, which the exporter does when it starts. Ignored when `uri` is set

password.description: The password of `user`. Ignored when `uri` is set

schema.description: The PostgreSQL schema of the tables, created when it does not exist

table_prefix.description: The name of the table of the gateway events, and the prefix of the names of the other tables (`<table_prefix>_fired_alerts`, the tables of the projections of the admin extensions). `table` is read instead when it is absent or empty

table.description: The former name of `table_prefix`, always written with its value for the nodes that predate the rename. Only read when `table_prefix` is absent or empty, as in the configs saved before the rename

pool_size.description: The maximum number of connections the exporter opens to the database

ssl.description: Whether the connection to the database requires tls (`sslmode=require`). Ignored when `uri` is set: the uri tells it

retention_days.description: How long the events of every projection are kept, in days: an hourly job deletes the older ones from the tables of the active user-analytics data exporter. `0` (or less) keeps them forever

statement_timeout_ms.description: The maximum duration of a query, in milliseconds. Reserved: it is not applied yet

rollup_enabled.description: Reserved: rollup tables are not computed yet

excluded_projections.description: The ids of the projections whose events are not stored (see `GET /api/analytics/_projections`). Their tables are still created and pruned, and their queries keep answering with the events stored before

ApiPlan.description: A consumer plan of an api: how its consumers are identified (its access mode), how they are rate limited, the plugins applied to their calls, how their subscriptions are validated and what they cost. Whatever the access mode, a consumer is an api key: the ones of the `apikey` and `oauth2-local` plans are minted for the subscriptions, the other modes mint one for each consumer seen at call time. A plan is stored as it is sent, the fields below being the ones otoroshi reads

id.description: The id of the plan, unique in the api. The subscriptions reference it in `plan_ref`

name.description: The name of the plan, shown in the backoffice and available as `${plan.name}` in the `clientNamePattern` of the api keys minted for it

description.description: The description of the plan. Defaults to `No description`
description.example: Free access with an api key, rate limited

status.description: The lifecycle state of the plan: `staging` while it is designed, `published` when its access mode applies to the routes of the api, `deprecated` when it accepts no new subscription, `closed` when its `apikey` and `oauth2-local` subscriptions are deleted, with their api keys, on their next update. Subscriptions can be created on a plan in `staging` or `published` only. Read case insensitively, an unknown value is read as `closed`. Defaults to `published`

access_mode_configuration_type.description: How the consumers of the plan are identified: `keyless` by an expression evaluated on the call (the ip address by default), `apikey` by an api key, `jwt` by a claim of a jwt token, `mtls` by a client certificate, `oauth2-local` by a token otoroshi issues itself through the client credentials flow, `oauth2-remote` by a token checked against the OAuth2 settings of an auth module. It gives the shape of `access_mode_configuration`. Defaults to `keyless`, an unknown value adds no access plugin

rateLimiting.description: The rate limiting of the consumers of the plan. Also read from `rate_limiting`. Without a strategy the plan uses the legacy one with the default quotas, the one an api key created by hand gets

strategy.description: The throttling strategy of every consumer of the plan, whether it got its api key through a subscription or at call time. A strategy that cannot be read is replaced by the legacy one with the default quotas

plugins.description: The plugins applied to the calls of the consumers of the plan, on top of the flow of the route

validation.description: How the subscriptions to the plan are validated. Defaults to `auto`

visibility.description: How the plan is shown in a developer portal. Defaults to `public`

pricing.description: What the plan costs, for a developer portal to show: otoroshi stores it, it does not charge the consumers

tags.description: The tags of the plan, given to the api keys of its consumers unless the plan has an `apikey` access mode configuration, whose tags are used instead

metadata.description: The metadata of the plan, given to the api keys of its consumers unless the plan has an `apikey` access mode configuration, whose metadata are used instead

example.description: Free access with an api key, rate limited
