A certificate can be designated by its id or by its distinguished name (the valid one expiring last is then used). The legacy `certId` and `cert_id` keys, holding a single certificate, are read too

items.description: The id or the distinguished name of a certificate

certs.description: The certificates presented as client certificates to the target (mtls)

items.description: The id or the distinguished name of a certificate

trusted_certs.description: The certificates trusted to validate the certificate of the target, instead of the default trust store

enabled.description: Whether these tls settings are used to call the target. When false, the default tls settings of otoroshi are used. Defaults to `false`

loose.description: Whether the host name of the certificate of the target is not checked. Defaults to `false`

trust_all.description: Whether any certificate of the target is trusted, self signed ones included. For tests only. Defaults to `false`

Transform.description: Verifies the token of the request with the `algoSettings` of the verifier, rewrites its claims, then signs it again with other algorithm settings and sends it to the backend at another location

type.description: The strategy, always `Transform`

verificationSettings.description: The claims the token has to hold

transformSettings.description: How the token is rewritten, and where it is sent

algoSettings.description: How the token sent to the backend is signed

UserRight.description: The rights of a user on a tenant (organization) and on some of its teams

tenant.description: The tenant (organization) the right applies to, followed by its access level: `<tenant>:r` (read only), `<tenant>:rw` (read and write) or `<tenant>:not` (no access). `*` stands for every tenant. A value without level is read as `rw`, the api always writes the level, in lower case

teams.description: The teams of the tenant (organization) the right applies to, each one followed by its access level the same way: `<team>:r`, `<team>:rw` or `<team>:not`, `*` standing for every team of the tenant

items.description: A team followed by its access level

StatsHistogramSeries.description: A series of a histogram: a named curve, with a point per time bucket

name.description: The name of the series: a class of status codes (`1**` to `5**`) for the statuses histogram, `count`, `min`, `max`, `avg` or `std deviation` for a statistics histogram, a percentile (`1.0` to `99.0`) for a percentiles histogram

count.description: The number of calls of the series. Only in the statuses histogram

data.description: The points of the series, one per time bucket

UserAnalyticsQueryResult.description: The result of a user analytics query on a period

shape.description: The shape of the result, which tells the fields of `data` (see `UserAnalyticsQueryData`) and the widget types that can draw it

raw.description: The rows behind `data`, when the query provides them. Empty for multi-series timeseries and heatmaps

items.description: A row: an item of a `pie` or `topN` result, a point of a timeseries, the `value` of a `scalar` result

meta.description: Execution details, merged into the details the query adds itself (none for the built-in queries). In `compare`, only the details the query adds

execution_ms.description: The time it took to run the query, in milliseconds. Missing when the result comes from the cache

from_cache.description: Whether the result, and its comparison when there is one, comes from the 30 seconds result cache

bucket.description: The time bucket size used by the query

IndexSettings.description: How the events are indexed in Elasticsearch

action.description: The action of the bulk calls: `index`, or `create` to write to a data stream. `index` when absent

clientSide.description: Let otoroshi spread the events over one index per time interval, named `<index>-<date>`, instead of writing everything to a single index (for instance one rolled over by an ILM policy, or a data stream). `true` when absent

interval.description: The time interval each index covers, when clientSide is true. Read without case, an absent or unknown value reads as `Day`

numberOfShards.description: The number of primary shards of the indexes, set by the index template. 1 when absent

numberOfReplicas.description: The number of replicas of each shard, set by the index template. 1 when absent

config.otoroshi.io.GlobalConfig.description: The global configuration of otoroshi: the single, instance wide settings that apply to every request and to the whole instance (quotas, ip filtering, tls, analytics, alerts, global plugins, proxies, templates of the new entities...). It is a singleton, always read and written under the id `global`: it can be read and updated, not created nor deleted. A change applies at once to every instance of the cluster. The fields absent from a body take the value given in their description, which can differ from the one of a new instance (the template)

tags.description: The tags of the global configuration, free labels to search and organize the entities. Empty when absent

lines.description: The lines (environments, like `prod` or `preprod`) of the instance. Only used by the removed service descriptors, kept for compatibility. `["prod"]` when absent

anonymousReporting.description: Send anonymous statistics about the instance (number of entities, enabled features, versions) to the otoroshi team, when the anonymous reporting is also enabled in the configuration of the instance (`otoroshi.anonymous-reporting.enabled`). `false` when absent

initWithNewEngine.description: Whether the instance was initialized for the proxy engine of the routes: its first start created the route that exposes the backoffice and the admin api. Informative once the instance has started. `true` for a new instance and when absent

maintenanceMode.description: Put every route in maintenance: every proxied request is answered with a 503 error instead of being forwarded, except the ones to the backoffice and the ones of the routes that turn the legacy checks off (metadata `otoroshi-core-apply-legacy-checks: false`). `false` when absent

enableEmbeddedMetrics.description: Compute the live metrics of the routes (calls, data in and out, durations) and store them in the datastore, for the backoffice. It performs many writes in the datastore. `true` when absent

streamEntityOnly.description: Not used anymore, the bodies are always streamed. Kept for compatibility. `true` when absent

autoLinkToDefaultGroup.description: Add a new service descriptor without group to the default group. Only used by the removed service descriptors, kept for compatibility. `true` when absent

limitConcurrentRequests.description: Limit the number of requests handled at the same time by each instance to maxConcurrentRequests, the requests above being answered with a 429 error. Recommended for resilience. `false` when absent

maxConcurrentRequests.description: The maximum number of requests handled at the same time by each instance. Above it, an audit event and an alert are sent, and the requests are refused with a 429 error when limitConcurrentRequests is true. 1000 when absent

maxHttp10ResponseSize.description: The maximum size, in bytes, of a response to an HTTP/1.0 request: such a response is held in memory, the bytes above the limit are dropped. Choose it so that maxConcurrentRequests times maxHttp10ResponseSize fits in the memory of the process. 4194304 (4 MB) when absent

useCircuitBreakers.description: Always `true` and ignored on input: the circuit breakers are set on the backends of the routes since the service descriptors were removed

apiReadOnly.description: Freeze the datastore: the admin api and the backoffice refuse every call that is not a GET. It can then only be turned off directly in the datastore. The panic mode of the backoffice turns it on. `false` when absent

u2fLoginOnly.description: Disable the login to the backoffice through the auth module of backOfficeAuthRef: the admins log in with their otoroshi account only (login, password and their WebAuthn device when they have one). `false` when absent

superAdminWhenNoRights.description: Give the super admin rights to an admin or a user of the backoffice that has no rights at all. `false` for a new instance, `true` when absent (the instances that predate the flag, where missing rights meant super admin rights): turn it off before going live

trustXForwarded.description: Read the client address, the protocol and the host of the original request from the headers set by the reverse proxies in front of otoroshi (see trustedProxies and clientAddressHeader). When false, the address, protocol and host of the connection are used. `true` when absent

trustedProxies.description: The reverse proxies allowed to tell otoroshi who the client is: ip addresses, CIDR ranges or patterns where `*` matches anything. They are added to the ones given at startup (`OTOROSHI_OPTIONS_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `OTOROSHI_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `CC_REVERSE_PROXY_IPS`). When the list is not empty, the loopback is trusted too and the forwarded headers of anyone else are ignored; when it is empty, the forwarded headers of anyone are trusted. A single string is read as a one entry list, the entries that are not strings are left out

items.description: An address, a CIDR range or a pattern. An entry can hold a comma separated list, like a vault reference to an environment variable

clientAddressHeader.description: The header the client address is read from: `X-Forwarded-For`, `Forwarded`, or any header holding the address like `X-Real-IP`. It must be one the reverse proxies build or overwrite. `OTOROSHI_OPTIONS_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADER` wins over this value when it is set. `X-Forwarded-For` when absent or blank

useLegacyClientIpAddress.description: Temporary way back to the resolution of the client address used before the trusted proxies: the leftmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry, whoever sent it, when trustXForwarded is true, the address of the connection otherwise. Also turned on by `OTOROSHI_OPTIONS_USE_LEGACY_CLIENT_IP_ADDRESS=true`. Will be removed. `false` when absent

throttlingQuota.description: The maximum number of requests otoroshi handles, all clients together, during each throttling window (`app.throttlingWindow`, 10 seconds by default). The requests above are answered with a 429 error. 10000000 when absent

perIpThrottlingQuota.description: The maximum number of requests otoroshi handles for one client address during each throttling window (`app.throttlingWindow`, 10 seconds by default), unless the address has a quota of its own. The requests above are answered with a 429 error. 10000000 when absent

analyticsWebhooks.description: Legacy: the webhooks every analytics event is posted to. Prefer the data exporters. A list holding a webhook that cannot be read reads as empty

alertsWebhooks.description: Legacy: the webhooks every alert event is posted to. Prefer the data exporters. A list holding a webhook that cannot be read reads as empty

elasticWritesConfigs.description: Legacy: the Elasticsearch clusters every analytics event is written to. Prefer the data exporters. A list holding a config that cannot be read reads as empty

elasticReadsConfig.description: The Elasticsearch cluster the analytics shown by the backoffice and served by the analytics api are read from. null: no analytics are read. A config without any url reads as null

alertsEmails.description: The email addresses the alerts are sent to, through the mailer of mailerSettings. Empty when absent

logAnalyticsOnServer.description: Also write every analytics event to the logs of the instance. `false` when absent

useAkkaHttpClient.description: Use the Pekko (formerly Akka) http client for the http calls of otoroshi, the calls to the backends included, instead of the default client. `false` when absent

endlessIpAddresses.description: The client addresses answered with an endless response, about 128 GB of zeros or of middle finger emojis (see middleFingers), to waste the time of the bots: ip addresses, CIDR ranges or patterns where `*` matches anything. Empty when absent

items.description: An address, a CIDR range or a pattern

statsdConfig.description: The StatsD (or Datadog) agent the metrics of otoroshi are pushed to. null: none. A config without host or port reads as null

kafkaConfig.description: Legacy: the Kafka cluster every analytics and audit event is sent to. Prefer the data exporters. null: none. A config that cannot be read reads as null

backOfficeAuthRef.description: The id of the auth module the admins can log in to the backoffice with, on top of their otoroshi accounts. null: none

mailerSettings.description: The mailer otoroshi sends its emails with: the alerts to alertsEmails, the links of the users of the private apps... null: no email is sent. A config that cannot be read reads as null

cleverSettings.description: The credentials of the Clever Cloud api, to expose the applications of a Clever Cloud organization. null: none

maxWebhookSize.description: Not used anymore: the number of events posted at once to the analytics webhooks is set by `app.webhooks.size`. 100 when absent

middleFingers.description: Selects what the endless responses sent to endlessIpAddresses are made of: zeros, or middle finger emojis. `false` when absent

maxLogsSize.description: The maximum number of alert events and of audit events kept in the datastore, the older ones being dropped. 100 when absent, `app.events.maxSize` for a new instance (50 in the default configuration, 100 when it is not set)

otoroshiId.description: The unique id of the instance (of the whole cluster), set at its first start from `otoroshi.instance.instanceId` or to a random uuid. Sent with the anonymous reporting. A random uuid when absent

wasmoSettings.description: The wasmo server the wasm plugins are built by and fetched from. null: none. The legacy wasmManagerSettings key is read when wasmoSettings is absent or null

metadata.description: The metadata of the global configuration: free string keys and values. Empty when absent

env.description: Free json shared with the whole instance: read by the `local` vault (`vault://local/path/to/value`, a json pointer in this object), by the expression language (`${global_config.env.path}`, when `otoroshi.elSettings.allowGlobalConfigAccess` is true) and handed to the jobs. `{}` when absent

extensions.description: Settings stored in the global configuration by the admin extensions, each one under a key of its own (usually its id). `{}` when absent

additionalProperties.description: The settings of an admin extension, any json value

id.description: The id of the global configuration, always `global`: the global configuration is a singleton. The admin api adds it to the global configuration it answers, and ignores it on input

DatadogCallSettings.description: The settings of a Datadog exporter: the events are sent as logs to the Datadog logs intake

token.description: The Datadog api key, sent as `DD-API-KEY`

url.description: The url of the logs intake. Defaults to `https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.eu/api/v2/logs`

headers.description: Additional http headers of the calls

timeout.description: The timeout of a call, in milliseconds. Defaults to 60000

tls_config.description: The tls settings of the calls to the logs intake

ddsource.description: The `ddsource` of the logs, `otoroshi` when unset. Not written when unset

ddtags.description: The `ddtags` of the logs. Not written when unset

service.description: The `service` of the logs, the name of the route of the event when unset. Not written when unset

hostname.description: The `hostname` of the logs, the name of the otoroshi cluster when unset. Not written when unset

LatencyInjectionFaultConfig.description: A fault of the snow monkey that delays the responses by a random duration

ratio.description: The share of the requests affected by the fault, between 0 and 1

from.description: The shortest delay added to an affected request, in milliseconds

to.description: The longest delay added to an affected request, in milliseconds

UserAnalyticsUpdatedResponse.description: How many fired events of a user alert a call acknowledged

updated.description: The number of events that were acknowledged by the call

MaxmindGeolocationSettings.description: The geolocation of the clients in a MaxMind city database (GeoLite2 or GeoIP2), loaded in memory

type.description: The type of the geolocation, `maxmind`

path.description: Where the database is loaded from: the path of a `.mmdb` file, or the http(s) url of a `.mmdb` file, of a `.zip` archive or of a `.tar.gz` archive holding it. Settings without a path read as `none`

enabled.description: Geolocate the clients. `false` when absent

apis.otoroshi.io.ApiSubscription.description: A subscription of a consumer to a plan of an api. A subscription to an `apikey` or an `oauth2-local` plan is given an api key built from the plan, referenced in `token_refs`; the other access modes build their consumer at call time. A subscription is written only when its api is in `staging` or `published` and holds its plan, and is created only on a plan in `staging` or `published`, of the access mode of the subscription

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams of the subscription, against which the rights of the admins are checked

id.description: The unique id of the subscription, kept in the `apiRef` (`sub`) of the api keys minted for it. The template generates `api-subscription_<uuid>`, with the environment of otoroshi before the uuid outside of `prod`

name.description: The name of the subscription, shown in the backoffice. The api keys minted for it are not named after it but by the `clientNamePattern` of the plan

description.description: A free text describing the subscription, shown in the backoffice. The api keys minted for it get the description of the plan instead
description.example: The subscription of ACME Corp to the free tier

tags.description: Free tags of the subscription, given to its api keys

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the subscription, given to its api keys

status.description: The status of the subscription: `pending` until it is confirmed, `enabled`, `disabled` (its api keys are disabled) or `deprecated`. Any other value is kept as a custom status. Defaults to `disabled`

dates.description: The dates of the lifecycle of the subscription

owner_ref.description: The id of the client of the api (an entry of its `clients`) that owns the subscription

plan_ref.description: The id of the plan of the api the subscription is made to

payment_ref.description: Free information about the payment of the subscription, for instance its reference in a billing system. Defaults to an empty object

api_ref.description: The id of the api the subscription is made to

subscription_kind.description: The access mode of the subscription, the one of its plan (checked on creation). Read case insensitively, an unknown value is refused

items.description: A credential of the subscription. Otoroshi writes `{"apikey": "<client id>"}` for the api key it minted, and keeps the api keys referenced that way in sync with the plan

apikey.description: The client id of an api key of the subscription

token_refs.description: The credentials of the subscription. Otoroshi keeps every entry as it is sent

example.name: ACME Corp free tier
example.description: The subscription of ACME Corp to the free tier

Version.description: A version of otoroshi, as written and split into its parts

raw.description: The version as written, before it is parsed (`18.0.0-dev`, `18.0.0-preview2`...)

major.description: The first number of the version (`18` for `18.0.0-dev`), 0 when it cannot be read

minor.description: The second number of the version (`0` for `18.0.0-dev`), 0 when it is absent or cannot be read

patch.description: The third number of the version (`0` for `18.0.0-dev`), 0 when it is absent or cannot be read

build.description: The fourth number of the version, when it has one (`3` for `17.6.0.3`), null otherwise

suffix.description: The kind of pre-release of the version, null for a release

suffix_version.description: The number of the pre-release (`2` for `preview2`), null when it has none

str.description: The version written back from its parts: `<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, then `.<build>`, `-<suffix>` and `.<suffix_version>` when present, so `18.0.0-preview.2` for `18.0.0-preview2`

value.description: A number derived from the version: its digits put together (the pre-release number included), minus 0.5 for `dev` and `snapshot`, 0.4 for `alpha`, 0.3 for `beta`, 0.25 for `preview` or 0.2 for `rc` (`1799.5` for `18.0.0-dev`)

Outage.description: An outage the snow monkey injects into a route: during it, the chaos settings of the snow monkey apply to the calls of the route

descriptorId.description: The id of the route under outage (the field is named after the legacy service descriptors)

descriptorName.description: The name of the route under outage, as it was when the outage started

until.description: The time of the day the outage ends at, as `HH:mm:ss.SSS`

duration.description: The duration of the outage, in milliseconds

NgCustomTimeouts.description: Timeouts applying to the requests whose path matches a pattern, instead of the timeouts of the client. The durations are in milliseconds

path.description: The pattern the path of the request must match, `*` being a wildcard. Defaults to `*`

call_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, the streaming of the response excluded, in milliseconds. Defaults to `30000`

call_and_stream_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, the streaming of the response included, in milliseconds. Defaults to `3600000`

connection_timeout.description: How long connecting to the target can last at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `10000`

idle_timeout.description: How long a connection can stay idle at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `60000`

global_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, its retries included, in milliseconds. Defaults to `30000`

FixedWindowStrategyConfig.description: A fixed window counter local to each otoroshi instance: at most `quota.window` calls per window of `windowDurationMs` milliseconds. The daily and monthly quotas are counted too

id.description: Selects the fixed window strategy: a counter local to each otoroshi instance, reset at the end of each window

windowDurationMs.description: The duration of a window, in milliseconds. Defaults to 10000

bucketKey.description: The key of the bucket the calls are counted in, an expression language string evaluated on each call (for instance `${req.ip}`). It is only used when the strategy is the config of a rate limiting plugin: the strategy of an api key or of a plan counts the calls of the api key

OtlpMetricsExporterSettings.description: The settings of an OTLP metrics exporter: it computes the metrics it lists from the events and sends them to an OpenTelemetry collector

type.description: Written by otoroshi, not read back

tags.description: Tags added to every metric

metrics.description: The metrics computed from the events. A metric that cannot be read is dropped

otlp.description: The collector the metrics are sent to

TlsSettings.description: The tls settings of the instance: the certificate used when none matches the domain of a connection, the CAs trusted on both sides, and the client authentication

defaultDomain.description: The domain whose certificate is used when no certificate matches the domain (SNI) of a tls connection. null or blank: none

randomIfNotFound.description: When no certificate matches the domain of a connection, nor defaultDomain, use the first available certificate. `false` when absent

includeJdkCaServer.description: Trust the CAs of the JDK to validate the client certificates of the incoming connections, and propose them in the certificate request of the handshake. `true` when absent

includeJdkCaClient.description: Trust the CAs of the JDK to validate the certificates of the servers otoroshi calls (backends, identity providers...). `true` when absent

trustedCAsServer.description: The ids of the CA certificates trusted to validate the client certificates of the incoming connections, the only CAs proposed in the certificate request of the handshake. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a CA certificate

bannedAlpnProtocols.description: The ALPN protocols never negotiated for some domains: the key is the domain (SNI) of the tls connection. Empty when absent

additionalProperties.description: The ALPN protocols refused for the domain

items.description: The id of an ALPN protocol, like `h2` or `http/1.1`

clientAuth.description: Whether the clients are asked for a certificate during the tls handshake, on the listeners whose client authentication is `Dynamic` (the default of `otoroshi.ssl.fromOutside.clientAuth`): `None` never, `Want` asked but optional, `Need` required. Read without case, `Dynamic`, an absent or an unknown value reads as `None`

strictBackendServerValidation.description: Strictly validate the certificates of the backend servers on the mTLS calls (targets with a tls config enabled): the untrusted certificates and the ones whose host name does not match are refused, and trustAll takes precedence. Only used when `otoroshi.ssl.trust.strictBackendServerValidation` is `global` (the default). `true` for a new instance, `false` when absent, to keep the historical permissive behavior of the existing configs

proxy.otoroshi.io.TcpService.description: A tcp proxy: otoroshi listens on a port and forwards the raw tcp connections to targets, optionally terminating tls or routing on the sni of the tls handshake. No http processing is applied

id.description: The unique id of the tcp service, written as `@serviceId` in the `TcpEvent` analytics events of its connections

name.description: The name of the tcp service, shown in the backoffice and written as `@service` in the `TcpEvent` analytics events of its connections

description.description: A free text describing the tcp service
description.example: The proxy of the postgres cluster

enabled.description: Whether otoroshi listens on the port of the tcp service. Defaults to `false` when missing

tls.description: How tls is handled: `Disabled` forwards the connections as they are, `Enabled` terminates tls with the certificates of otoroshi (chosen with the sni), `PassThrough` forwards the tls connections to targets that terminate tls themselves. Defaults to `Disabled`

sni.description: How the connections are routed on the domain of the sni of the tls handshake

clientAuth.description: Whether a client certificate is asked for when tls is enabled: `None` does not ask for one, `Want` asks for one without requiring it, `Need` requires one. `Dynamic` is read but asks for none on a tcp service (it does not follow the tls settings of the global configuration here). Defaults to `None`

port.description: The port otoroshi listens on for the tcp service

interface.description: The network interface otoroshi listens on. Defaults to `0.0.0.0`

rules.description: The routing rules. With sni routing, the first rule whose domain matches the sni domain of the connection gives its targets. Without it, the connections go to the targets of all the rules in turn

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the tcp service

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the tcp services

example.name: PostgreSQL proxy
example.description: The proxy of the postgres cluster

LargeRequestFaultConfig.description: A fault of the snow monkey that adds bytes to the body of the requests sent to the backends

ratio.description: The share of the requests affected by the fault, between 0 and 1

additionalRequestSize.description: The number of bytes added to the body of an affected request

GoReplayS3Settings.description: The settings of a GoReplay S3 exporter: the captured traffic (`TrafficCaptureEvent`, emitted by the routes with `capture` enabled) is written in the GoReplay format (`.gor`) to an S3 compatible object storage

s3.description: Where the capture files are uploaded

maxFileSize.description: The maximum size of a capture file, in bytes. A new file is started once it is reached. Defaults to 10485760 (10 MB)

captureRequests.description: Whether the requests are captured. Defaults to true

captureResponses.description: Whether the responses are captured. Defaults to false

preferBackendRequest.description: Whether the captured request is the one otoroshi sent to the backend rather than the one the client sent. Defaults to false

preferBackendResponse.description: Whether the captured response is the one the backend sent rather than the one otoroshi sent to the client. Defaults to false

methods.description: The http methods of the calls captured. Empty for every method

ApiDeployTransitionError.description: The deployment would move the api to a state it cannot reach from its own: a `removed` api refuses the deployment of a draft in `staging`, which would publish it

error_description.description: A message naming the state of the api and the state the deployment would set

from.description: The state the api is in, `removed` being the only one a deployment can fail from

to.description: The state the deployment would have set, `published` for a draft in `staging`

GenCsrQuery.description: The settings of a certificate (or of a certificate signing request) to generate with the pki of otoroshi: its key pair, its subject, its alternative names, its usages and its lifetime. Its key pair is described by `key`, or by `keyType` and `keySize`: a query that gives none of them is refused. The certificate is a server certificate (extended key usage `serverAuth`) unless `client` or `ca` says otherwise

hosts.description: The dns names written as subject alternative names of the certificate (ignored for a ca)

key.description: The key pair of the certificate. Required unless `keyType` and `keySize` are given, `{}` giving a 2048 bits rsa key pair

keyType.description: The algorithm of the key pair (`RSA`, `ECDSA`...), read lowercased when `key` is absent, `keySize` being then required too. Never written back

keySize.description: The size of the key in bits, read when `key` is absent, `keyType` being then required too. Never written back

name.description: The parts of the distinguished name of the subject (`CN`, `OU`, `O`, `L`, `ST`, `C`...), used when `subject` is absent

additionalProperties.description: The value of the part of the distinguished name

subject.description: The distinguished name of the subject of the certificate. When absent, it is built from `name`

client.description: Whether the certificate is a client certificate (extended key usages `clientAuth` and `serverAuth`). Defaults to false

ca.description: Whether the certificate is a certificate authority (basic constraint `CA:true`, key usages `keyCertSign` and `cRLSign`). Defaults to false

includeAIA.description: Whether to add the authority information access extension (the ocsp responder and the ca issuers urls of otoroshi) to a certificate signed by the root ca of otoroshi. Defaults to false, never written back

duration.description: How long the certificate is valid from now, in milliseconds. Defaults to 365 days

signatureAlg.description: The signature algorithm of the certificate, as known by BouncyCastle. Defaults to `SHA256WithRSAEncryption`, `SHA256withECDSA` being the one of an elliptic curve key pair

digestAlg.description: The digest algorithm of the signature. Defaults to `SHA-256`

LetsEncryptCertificateQuery.description: The domain of a certificate to order from Let's Encrypt

host.description: The domain of the certificate. It has to resolve to this otoroshi, Let's Encrypt validating the order with an http-01 challenge served by otoroshi

BadEntityResponse.description: Why an entity was refused: an error, or the errors of the fields that could not be read

plugins.otoroshi.io.WasmPlugin.description: A wasm plugin: a webassembly module and the way to run it, that the wasm plugins of the routes, of the apis and of the global configuration reference by its id instead of repeating its configuration

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams of the wasm plugin, checked against the rights of the admins

id.description: The unique id of the wasm plugin, the reference the wasm plugins of the routes use (`Local` source kind)

name.description: The name of the wasm plugin, displayed in the backoffice

description.description: A free text describing what the wasm plugin does
description.example: Checks the api key of the calls against a remote registry

config.description: The webassembly module and how it runs. A missing config reads as the default one

steps.description: The steps of a route the plugin can be used at, to offer it in the backoffice. A step otoroshi does not know is left out

items.description: A step of the proxy engine

metadata.description: Free metadata of the wasm plugin, as string keys and values

tags.description: Free tags of the wasm plugin, used to sort and find it in the backoffice

example.name: New wasm plugin
example.description: New wasm plugin

UDPExporterSettings.description: The settings of a UDP exporter: the events are sent as json datagrams (or to a unix socket)

host.description: The host to send to, or the path of the socket when `unix_socket` is true. Defaults to `127.0.0.1`

port.description: The port to send to. Defaults to 514

unix_socket.description: Whether `host` is the path of a unix socket. Defaults to false

connect_timeout.description: The timeout of the connection, in milliseconds. Defaults to 10000

S3ExporterSettings.description: The settings of an S3 exporter: the events are written to files, as newline delimited json, uploaded to an S3 compatible object storage

maxFileSize.description: The maximum size of a file, in bytes. A new file is started once it is reached. Defaults to 10485760 (10 MB)

maxNumberOfFile.description: The maximum number of files kept, the oldest ones being deleted. Null (or 0) to keep them all

ElasticAnalyticsConfig.description: The connection to an Elasticsearch (or OpenSearch) cluster: the cluster events are written to, or the one the analytics are read from. A config without any url cannot be read

clusterUri.description: The first entry of uris, written for the clients of the legacy single url setting. On input it is still read, and added to uris

uris.description: The urls of the nodes of the cluster. An entry can hold a comma separated list of urls

index.description: The name of the index, or the prefix of the indexes when indexSettings.clientSide is true. null: `otoroshi-events`. Blank reads as null

type.description: The type of the documents, only needed by the Elasticsearch versions before 7. null: `event`. Blank reads as null

user.description: The user of the basic authentication on the cluster. null: no authentication. Blank reads as null

password.description: The password of the basic authentication on the cluster. Blank reads as null

headers.description: The http headers added to each call to the cluster, for instance an api key. Empty when absent

applyTemplate.description: Create or update the index template of otoroshi on the cluster before writing to it. `true` when absent

version.description: The version of the cluster. null or blank: it is asked to the cluster

maxBulkSize.description: The maximum number of events written by one bulk call. 100 when absent

sendWorkers.description: The number of bulk calls sent in parallel. 4 when absent

MtlsAccessModeConfiguration.description: The access mode `mtls`: the consumers call with a tls client certificate, the consumer being read from its subject. Each consumer gets an api key of its own built from the plan

items.description: A regular expression on the subject dn

regex_subject_dns.description: The regular expressions the subject dn of the client certificate may match. A certificate matching one of them, or one of `regex_issuer_dns`, is accepted. Both lists empty, any trusted certificate is

items.description: A regular expression on the issuer dn

apis.otoroshi.io.Api.description: An api: the routes, the backends, the plugin flows, the consumer plans and the documentation of a service exposed under one domain and one context path, with a lifecycle (`staging`, `published`, `deprecated`, `removed`). Otoroshi turns each of its routes into a route of the proxy engine: the domain and the context path of the api in front of the path of the route, the access plugins of its published plans added to the flow of the route

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams of the api, against which the rights of the admins are checked

kind.description: The kind of the entity, `Api` by default. The admin api answers `apis.otoroshi.io/Api` in its place, and the group of a kind sent as `apis.otoroshi.io/Api` is dropped

id.description: The id of the api, unique among the apis

name.description: The name of the api, shown in the backoffice, written as `@service` in its `ApiDeploymentEvent` events, and available as `${api.name}` in the `clientNamePattern` of the api keys of its plans

description.description: The description of the api, also given to the routes built from it
description.example: Manage the users of the platform

domain.description: The domain the api is exposed on: the routes of the api match it, followed by the context path and by the path of the route. Defaults to an empty string

contextPath.description: The path prefix of every route of the api, between the domain and the path of the route. Defaults to an empty string

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the api, also given to the routes built from it with `Otoroshi-Api-Ref` holding the id of the api

tags.description: Free tags of the api, also given to the routes built from it

visibility.description: How the api is shown in a developer portal. Defaults to `public`

owner.description: The owner of the api. Defaults to the reference `owner`

members.description: The users or the teams that work on the api with its owner. An entry without `ref` is left out

version.description: The current version of the api, written in the `ApiDeploymentEvent` of each of its deployments. Defaults to `0.0.1`

debug_flow.description: Whether the execution report of each call to the routes of the api holds the input and the output of every plugin. Defaults to `false`

capture.description: Whether the routes of the api emit a `TrafficCaptureEvent` for each call, with the bodies of the request and of the response, to export with a data exporter. Defaults to `false`

export_reporting.description: Whether the routes of the api emit the report of the execution of each call as a `RequestFlowReport` event, to export with a data exporter. It costs cpu and memory. Defaults to `false`

items.description: The id of a service group

groups.description: The ids of the service groups the routes of the api belong to, on top of a group of their own (`virtual_group_for_<api id>`), for instance to authorize api keys on them

state.description: The lifecycle state of the api: `staging` while it is designed, only its draft routes are served (when its testing is enabled); `published`, its routes are served; `deprecated`, its routes are still served but its subscriptions can no longer be created nor updated; `removed`, nothing is served. An api is created in `staging` and goes to `published` through a deployment of its draft. An unknown value is read as `staging`, the default

enabled.description: Whether the api is served at all: disabled, neither its production routes nor its draft routes are served. Defaults to `true`

blueprint.description: The kind of api, it does not change how otoroshi serves it. An unknown value is refused. Defaults to `REST`

plans.description: The consumer plans of the api: who can call it and how. The access plugins of the published plans are added to every route of the api, the plugins of a plan apply to the calls of its consumers. An entry that is not an object is left out

routes.description: The routes of the api. A route that cannot be read is left out

backends.description: The backends of the api, referenced by its routes. A backend that cannot be read is left out

flows.description: The plugin chains of the api, referenced by its routes and by its plans. A flow that cannot be read is left out

clients_backend_config.description: The http client settings of the api, referenced by its backends. Written with the default client `default_backend_client` alone when empty

documentation.description: The documentation of the api for a developer portal, `null` when the api has none

deployments.description: The last five deployments of the api, the most recent first. Otoroshi adds one each time a draft of the api is deployed

versions.description: A free list of the versions of the api, stored as it is sent: otoroshi does not read it, `version` holding the current version. The template holds `0.0.1`, an empty list when missing

testing.description: The testing of the draft of the api

clients.description: The consumers of the api, the owners of its subscriptions

hooks.description: The hooks of the lifecycle of the api. Otoroshi stores them, it does not call them itself

analytics.otoroshi.io.UserAlert.description: A user analytics alert: conditions on the analytics queries of the active user-analytics data exporter, evaluated periodically on a sliding window. When they hold, an alert event (`AlertEvent` with `alert` set to `UserAnalyticsAlert`) is sent to the data exporters, at most once per cooldown period

id.description: The id of the alert, used in the paths of `/api/analytics/alerts/{alertId}/events` and copied as `alertId` into the events it emits. A random one is generated when it is missing or empty

name.description: The name of the alert, shown in the backoffice and copied as `alertName` into the events it emits
name.example: High error rate on the billing api

description.description: A free text telling what the alert watches, shown under its name on the page of its fired events in the backoffice. Unlike `message`, it is not copied into the events
description.example: More than 5% of the calls fail

tags.description: Free tags of the alert, to search and sort it

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the alert

enabled.description: Whether the alert is evaluated: a disabled alert never fires. Defaults to true

windowSeconds.description: The duration of the sliding window the queries are run on, in seconds. Defaults to 300

evaluationIntervalSeconds.description: The delay between two evaluations of the alert, in seconds. Defaults to 60. The evaluation job runs every 60 seconds on a single instance of the cluster, so a shorter delay acts as 60 seconds

cooldownSeconds.description: The minimum delay between two events emitted by the alert, in seconds. Defaults to 600

severity.description: The severity of the alert, copied into the events it emits. Defaults to `warning`

message.description: The text of the events the alert emits (their `message`), for the people and the systems that receive them
message.example: The error rate of the billing api is above 5%

combine.description: How the conditions are combined: `AND` when all of them must hold, `OR` when one is enough. Defaults to `AND`, the value is case insensitive

conditions.description: The conditions of the alert. An alert without condition never fires. A condition that cannot be read is dropped

example.name: High error rate on the billing api
example.description: More than 5% of the calls fail
example.message: The error rate of the billing api is above 5%

queries.description: The queries a query request, a dashboard widget or an alert condition can run, the built-in ones first

widget_types.description: The values the `type` of a dashboard widget can take

UserAnalyticsAlertConditionEval.description: How a condition of a user alert was evaluated when the alert fired: the reduced result of its query, compared to its threshold

query.description: The id of the query of the condition

reducer.description: How the query result was reduced to a single value: `avg`, `max`, `min`, `sum` or `last`

operator.description: How the value was compared to the threshold: `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `==` or `!=`

threshold.description: The value the reduced value was compared to, the `threshold` of the condition

value.description: The result of the query reduced to a single number, `null` when the query answered no value or could not run

error.description: Why the condition could not be evaluated (no active user-analytics data exporter, an unknown query, a failed query), `null` when it was

clientSideSessionEnabled.description: Also keep the session of the users of the private apps in an encrypted cookie, so that a session missing from the datastore of otoroshi (not synchronized yet on an instance of the cluster, lost by a restart) is restored from it. True when missing

sessionMaxAge.description: How long a session lasts, in seconds. 86400 (a day) when missing

userValidators.description: The checks of the profile of a user that logs in. Every check has to pass for the user to get in

example.error: the user is not a member of the admins group

remoteValidators.description: The remote services that validate a user that logs in. Every service has to accept the user

clientId.description: The client id of otoroshi on the identity provider. `client` when missing

clientSecret.description: The client secret of otoroshi on the identity provider. It can be a vault reference like `${vault://local/client-secret}`. `secret` when missing

authorizeUrl.description: The authorization endpoint of the identity provider

tokenUrl.description: The token endpoint of the identity provider, called to exchange the authorization code for the tokens

userInfoUrl.description: The userinfo endpoint of the identity provider, called to get the profile of the user

introspectionUrl.description: The token introspection endpoint (RFC 7662) of the identity provider, used to check opaque access tokens

loginUrl.description: The url the users are redirected to in order to log in, usually the authorization endpoint

logoutUrl.description: The url the users are redirected to when they log out, the client id being added to it. Nothing is called when empty

scope.description: The scopes asked to the identity provider, separated by spaces. `openid profile email name` when missing

claims.description: The `claims` parameter sent to the identity provider, not sent when empty. `email name` when missing

useCookie.description: Keep the route the user comes from in a cookie instead of a query parameter of the redirect uri, for the identity providers that refuse query parameters in redirect uris. False when missing

useJson.description: Send the payloads of the calls to the token, userinfo and introspection endpoints as json instead of form urlencoded. False when missing

pkce.description: The PKCE settings of the authorization code flow, null to not use PKCE

noWildcardRedirectURI.description: Send the callback url as is as the redirect uri, without query parameters, as OAuth 2.1 requires. False when missing

readProfileFromToken.description: Read the profile of the user from the claims of the access token, verified with `jwtVerifier`, instead of calling the userinfo endpoint. Only used when `jwtVerifier` is set. False when missing

accessTokenField.description: The field of the answer of the token endpoint holding the access token. `access_token` when missing

jwtVerifier.description: How the signature of the access tokens of the identity provider is verified when the profile of the user is read from them (`readProfileFromToken`), null when the profile comes from the userinfo endpoint

nameField.description: The field of the profile holding the name of the user. `name` when missing

emailField.description: The field of the profile holding the email of the user. `email` when missing

apiKeyMetaField.description: The field of the profile holding the metadata of the api keys the user creates (client credentials). `apkMeta` when missing

apiKeyTagsField.description: The field of the profile holding the tags of the api keys the user creates (client credentials). `apkTags` when missing

otoroshiDataField.description: The path of the field of the profile holding the otoroshi data of the user (sent to the backends), the parts of the path being separated by `|`. `app_metadata | otoroshi_data` when missing

callbackUrl.description: The url the identity provider redirects the users to once logged in: the callback of the private apps, or the one of the backoffice (`/backoffice/auth0/callback`)

oidConfig.description: The url of the OpenID Connect discovery document of the identity provider (ending with `.well-known/openid-configuration`), null when the endpoints are set by hand

mtlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the calls to the identity provider

proxy.description: The http proxy of the calls to the identity provider, null to use the auth proxy of the global configuration

extraMetadata.description: A json object merged into the otoroshi data of the users that log in, sent to the backends of the private apps

metadata.description: The metadata of the auth module, free key/value pairs. They are copied to the sessions of the users that log in to the private apps

tags.description: Free tags of the auth module, to search and sort it. They are copied to the sessions of the users that log in to the private apps

refreshTokens.description: Refresh the access token of the users with their refresh token when it expires. False when missing

sessionCookieValues.description: The `HttpOnly` and `Secure` flags of the session cookies set on the private apps once a user has logged in through the module. Both true when missing

superAdmins.description: Give super admin rights to every user that logs in to the backoffice. When false, the rights come from `rightsOverride`, then from the `otoroshiRightsField` of the profile, then from the location of the module. True when missing, for the modules written before the field existed

rightsOverride.description: The rights given to some users in the backoffice, by email. They replace the rights the user gets otherwise

additionalProperties.description: The rights of the user. `[{"tenant": "*:rw", "teams": ["*:rw"]}]` makes a super admin

dataOverride.description: The otoroshi data of some users, by email: merged into the otoroshi data of the user sent to the backends of the private apps

additionalProperties.description: The otoroshi data of the user, any json object

otoroshiRightsField.description: The field of the profile holding the rights of the user in the backoffice. `otoroshi_rights` when missing

allowedUsers.description: The users allowed to log in, by email. Everybody when empty

items.description: A user allowed to log in. An email, or a pattern: `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `Not(x)`, `ContainedIn(a, b)` or `NotContainedIn(a, b)`

deniedUsers.description: The users that cannot log in, by email

items.description: A user that cannot log in. An email, or a pattern: `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `Not(x)`, `ContainedIn(a, b)` or `NotContainedIn(a, b)`

adminEntityValidatorsOverride.description: The validators the entities written in the backoffice by some users have to pass, by email of the user, then by entity kind

additionalProperties.description: The validators of the entities written by the user, keyed by the singular name of the entity kind or `all`
The validators of an entity kind, keyed by the singular name of the kind (`route`, `apikey`, `certificate`...) or `all` for every kind. Every validator has to pass for the entity to be written

route.error: routes can only be exposed on oto.tools
routes can only be exposed on oto.tools

example.desc: Login with the Keycloak of the company

LuaDistributedRedisThrottlingStrategyCon.description: Like `DistributedRedisThrottlingStrategyConfig`, the calls being counted atomically by a Lua script run by the Redis shared by all the otoroshi instances

id.description: Selects the atomic distributed strategy: the calls are counted by a Lua script run by the rate limiter Redis shared by all the otoroshi instances

bucketKey.description: The key of the bucket the calls are counted in, an expression language string evaluated on each call (for instance `${req.ip}`). It is only used when the strategy is the config of a rate limiting plugin: the strategy of an api key or of a plan counts the calls of the api key

Plugins.description: The global plugins, run on every request: the legacy plugins of refs, and, through config, the plugins of the proxy engine and its settings

enabled.description: Run the legacy plugins of refs on every request. `false` when absent

refs.description: The ids of the legacy plugins run on every request. A new instance runs the proxy engine of the routes, `cp:otoroshi.next.proxy.ProxyEngine`. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a plugin: `cp:` followed by its class name for a plugin of the classpath

config.description: The configuration of the global plugins, any json object. `ng` holds the plugins of the proxy engine run on every request (a list of plugin instances, like the plugins of a route), `NextGenProxyEngine` the settings of the proxy engine, `incoming_request_validators` the validators of every incoming request, and the other keys the configuration of the legacy plugins of refs, under their configuration root. `{}` when absent

excluded.description: The regular expressions of the paths of the requests the legacy plugins of refs are not run on. An entry `only:<plugin id>:<regex>` only excludes that plugin. Empty when absent

items.description: A regular expression matching the whole path of a request, or `only:<plugin id>:<regex>`

PulsarConfig.description: The settings of a Pulsar exporter: the events are sent to an Apache Pulsar topic

uri.description: The service url of the Pulsar cluster: `pulsar://<host>:6650`, or `pulsar+ssl://<host>:6651` over tls

tlsTrustCertsFilePath.description: The path of a file of trusted certificates given to the Pulsar client. Only used when `mtls` of `mtlsConfig` is true. Null for none

tenant.description: The Pulsar tenant of the topic: the events are sent to `persistent://<tenant>/<namespace>/<topic>`

namespace.description: The Pulsar namespace of the topic, within the tenant

topic.description: The name of the topic the events are sent to, within the namespace

token.description: A token to authenticate to Pulsar, null for none. Not used when `mtls` of `mtlsConfig` is true. A blank value is read as null

username.description: The user to authenticate to Pulsar with (basic authentication, when there is no token), null for none. Not used when `mtls` of `mtlsConfig` is true. A blank value is read as null

password.description: The password of the user, null for none. A blank value is read as null

mtlsConfig.description: The tls settings of the connection to Pulsar: when `mtls` is true, the certificates of otoroshi are used

BulkOperationOutcome.description: The outcome of a line of a bulk operation

GlobalStatusUpdate.description: The statistics an otoroshi instance of a cluster gives the leaders: its resources and its traffic. Workers send them as the last line of their quotas updates, the leaders compute their own, and the leaders keep them as the `stats` of the member

typ.description: Selects the statistics of the sender (`globstats`): the leaders register the sender as a member of the cluster with these statistics

cpu_usage.description: The cpu usage of the process of the instance, in percent of the cpu of the machine. 0 when the java virtual machine does not tell it

load_average.description: The system load average of the machine of the instance over the last minute, negative when the system does not provide it

heap_used.description: The heap memory used by the java virtual machine, in megabytes

heap_size.description: The heap memory currently allocated by the java virtual machine, used and free, in megabytes

live_threads.description: The number of live threads of the java virtual machine, daemon threads included

live_peak_threads.description: The highest number of live threads of the java virtual machine since it started

daemon_threads.description: The number of live daemon threads of the java virtual machine

counters.description: The number of requests the instance received since it started: `requests` for all of them, and one counter per protocol (`http`, `https`, `h2`, `h2c`, `h3`, `ws`, `wss`, `grpc`, `grpcs`), present once a request used it

additionalProperties.description: The number of requests counted, since the instance started

rate.description: The number of calls per second over all the routes, from the statistics of the instance

duration.description: The mean duration of the calls over all the routes, in milliseconds

overhead.description: The mean overhead of otoroshi on the calls over all the routes, in milliseconds

dataInRate.description: The number of bytes received per second over all the routes, from the statistics of the instance

dataOutRate.description: The number of bytes sent per second over all the routes, from the statistics of the instance

concurrentHandledRequests.description: The number of requests the instance is handling when it builds the statistics

MetricSettings.description: A metric a custom metrics or OTLP metrics exporter updates for each event it exports: the events it applies to, the value it reads and its labels

id.description: The name of the metric: the one it is exposed under by otoroshi (custom metrics exporter) or sent to the collector with (OTLP metrics exporter), tagged with the `tags` of the exporter and its own `labels`

selector.description: The path of the numeric value of the event the metric is computed from (for instance `duration`). A counter without selector counts the events, a histogram or a timer without selector records nothing

kind.description: The kind of metric: a counter incremented by the value (or by one), a histogram of the values, or a timer of the values in milliseconds. Defaults to `Counter`

eventType.description: The events the metric is computed from: the ones whose `@type` (or `alert`) is this value. Null for every event. A missing value is read as `AlertEvent`

labels.description: The labels of the metric: each key is the path of a value of the event (`$at` stands for `@`), each value is the name of the label holding it

organize.otoroshi.io.Team.description: A team of an organization: a partition of the entities of the organization (their `_loc.teams`). Admins are granted rights per organization and team

id.description: The id of the team, the value listed in `_loc.teams` of its entities. It is lowercased and trimmed when read, and unique within its organization

tenant.description: The id of the tenant (organization) the team belongs to. It is lowercased and trimmed when read

name.description: The name of the team, for humans. Defaults to the id

description.description: A free text describing the team, shown and searched in the list of the teams of the backoffice. Empty when absent
description.example: The team running the payment apis

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the team

tags.description: Free tags of the team, to search and sort it

_loc.description: The location of the team, written by otoroshi from its tenant (organization) and its id: a team is in its organization and in itself. It is not read back

example.name: Payments
example.description: The team running the payment apis

NgClientConfig.description: How otoroshi calls the targets of a backend: retries, timeouts, circuit breaker and http proxy. The durations are in milliseconds

retries.description: How many times a failed call is retried before giving up. Defaults to `1`

max_errors.description: How many consecutive failed calls open the circuit breaker of a target, which then fails the calls without trying until `sample_interval` has elapsed. Defaults to `20`

retry_initial_delay.description: The delay before the first retry, in milliseconds. Defaults to `50`

backoff_factor.description: The factor the delay is multiplied by at each retry. Defaults to `2`

call_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, the streaming of the response excluded, in milliseconds. A soft timeout enforced by the circuit breaker. Defaults to `30000`

call_and_stream_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, the streaming of the response included, in milliseconds. The connection is closed after it. Defaults to `120000`

connection_timeout.description: How long connecting to the target can last at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `10000`

idle_timeout.description: How long a connection can stay idle at most, in milliseconds. Defaults to `60000`

global_timeout.description: How long a call can last at most, its retries included, in milliseconds. Defaults to `30000`

sample_interval.description: How long an open circuit breaker fails the calls before letting a call try the target again, in milliseconds. Defaults to `2000`

proxy.description: The http proxy the calls to the targets go through. An empty object when the calls do not use a proxy of their own (the proxy of the global configuration for the services is used then)

custom_timeouts.description: Timeouts replacing the ones above for some paths, the first one matching the path of the request applying

cache_connection_settings.description: The pool of connections kept open to each target

TargetPredicateNetworkLocationMatch.description: A target predicate on the location of the otoroshi instance handling the request (its cluster relay location): the target only serves the requests handled by the instances of the location. Each criterion is a pattern where `*` is a wildcard, null matching any value

type.description: Selects the predicate on the location of the otoroshi instance handling the request: the target only serves the requests handled by the instances of that location

provider.description: The pattern the provider of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its provider from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_PROVIDER` (or `otoroshi.instance.provider`), `local` by default. Null for any provider

region.description: The pattern the region of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its region from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_REGION` (or `otoroshi.instance.region`), `local` by default. Null for any region

zone.description: The pattern the zone of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its zone from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_ZONE` (or `otoroshi.instance.zone`), `local` by default. Null for any zone

dc.description: The pattern the datacenter of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its datacenter from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_DATACENTER` (or `otoroshi.instance.dc`), `local` by default. Null for any datacenter

rack.description: The pattern the rack of the otoroshi instance must match, case insensitively. An instance gets its rack from `OTOROSHI_CLUSTER_RELAY_LOCATION_RACK` (or `otoroshi.instance.rack`), `local` by default. Null for any rack

AuditEvent.description: An audit event as stored by otoroshi: what an admin or the admin api did. Every kind of audit event adds its own fields to the ones described here: an `AdminApiEvent`, for instance, adds `user`, `apiKey`, `action`, `from`, `message` and `metadata`

@id.description: The unique id of the event: a snowflake id generated by the otoroshi instance that emitted it, a number written as a string that grows with time

@timestamp.description: When the event happened, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds

@type.description: The family of the event, always `AuditEvent` here

@product.description: The name of the product that emitted the event, the `otoroshi.events.name` setting (`otoroshi` by default)

@serviceId.description: The id of the entity the event is about, `--` for the events of otoroshi itself

@service.description: The name of the entity the event is about, `Otoroshi` for the events of otoroshi itself

@env.description: The environment of the otoroshi instance (the `app.env` setting)

audit.description: The kind of the audit event, like `AdminApiEvent` (a call of the admin api), `BackOfficeEvent` (an action in the backoffice) or `SnowMonkeyOutageRegisteredEvent`

user-agent-details.description: What the user agent detection of the global configuration found about the user agent of the caller. `null` when it is disabled or found nothing

origin-details.description: What the geolocation of the global configuration found about the ip address of the caller. `null` when it is disabled or found nothing

instance-number.description: The number of the otoroshi instance that emitted the event (the `app.instance.number` setting)

instance-name.description: The name of the otoroshi instance that emitted the event

instance-zone.description: The zone of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.zone`)

instance-region.description: The region of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.region`)

instance-dc.description: The datacenter of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.datacenter`)

instance-provider.description: The provider of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.provider`)

instance-rack.description: The rack of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.rack`)

cluster-mode.description: The cluster mode of the otoroshi instance

cluster-name.description: The name of the otoroshi instance in its cluster, `none` when it is not part of a cluster

AnonymousReport.description: The anonymous usage report of an otoroshi cluster, the one the anonymous reporting job posts every 6 hours (to `https://reporting.otoroshi.io/ingest` by default) when the anonymous reporting is enabled: its version, its runtime, the features it uses, its traffic, its members, and the number of entities of each kind, without any name nor configuration. The entities are counted in the in-memory state of the instance that builds the report

@timestamp.description: When the report was built, a timestamp in milliseconds

timestamp_str.description: When the report was built, an ISO 8601 date in the time zone of the instance

@id.description: A random uuid generated for each report

otoroshi_cluster_id.description: The id of the otoroshi cluster (the `otoroshiId` of the global configuration), the same in every report of the cluster

otoroshi_version.description: The version of otoroshi the instance that builds the report runs, as written

datastore.description: The kind of datastore of the instance, as set by `app.storage` (`lettuce` when not set)

env.description: The environment of the instance, as set by `app.env` (`prod` when not set)

additional_data.description: The additional data of a configuration of the anonymous reporting job set programmatically (by an application that embeds otoroshi), its expressions evaluated. `{}` otherwise, and always `{}` when the report is answered by the admin api

features.description: The features the global configuration of the cluster turns on

snow_monkey.description: Whether the snow monkey (the chaos engineering of otoroshi) is enabled

clever_cloud.description: Whether the Clever Cloud settings are set in the global configuration

kubernetes.description: Whether a global plugin or a global job whose id contains `kube` is enabled in the global configuration (the kubernetes integration)

elastic_read.description: Whether the analytics are read from Elasticsearch (`elasticReadsConfig` of the global configuration is set)

lets_encrypt.description: Whether Let's Encrypt is enabled in the global configuration

auto_certs.description: Whether otoroshi generates certificates on the fly, during the tls handshake, for the domains it has none for (`autoCert.enabled` of the global configuration)

wasmo.description: Whether the wasmo settings (the server the wasm plugins are built by) are set in the global configuration

wasm_manager.description: Whether the wasmo settings are set (the former name of `wasmo`)

backoffice_login.description: Whether an auth module lets the admins log in to the backoffice on top of their otoroshi accounts (`backOfficeAuthRef` of the global configuration)

stats.description: The traffic of the cluster: the totals of its datastore, and the live rates of its members

calls.description: The total number of calls handled by the cluster, read from the `global` counter of the datastore

data_in.description: The total number of bytes of the request bodies received, read from the `global` counter of the datastore

data_out.description: The total number of bytes of the response bodies sent, read from the `global` counter of the datastore

rate.description: The calls handled per second: the recent rate recorded in the datastore plus the rates the members last reported

duration.description: The mean duration of the recent calls, in milliseconds, averaged over the value of the datastore and the values the members last reported

overhead.description: The mean overhead of otoroshi on the recent calls (the time spent in otoroshi itself), in milliseconds, averaged like `duration`

data_in_rate.description: The bytes of request bodies received per second: the recent rate recorded in the datastore plus the rates the members last reported

data_out_rate.description: The bytes of response bodies sent per second: the recent rate recorded in the datastore plus the rates the members last reported

concurrent_requests.description: The number of requests being handled right now: the count of the instance plus the counts the members last reported

engine.description: Whether the `ProxyEngine` global plugin, the former switch of the new proxy engine, is enabled in the global configuration

uses_new.description: Whether the global plugins are enabled, with the `cp:otoroshi.next.proxy.ProxyEngine` plugin among them and its `NextGenProxyEngine` configuration enabled

uses_new_full.description: Whether `uses_new` is true and the `NextGenProxyEngine` configuration applies to every domain (`domains` holds `*` and `deny_domains` is empty)

cluster.description: The cluster of the instance: its mode and the members registered in the datastore

mode.description: The cluster mode of the instance that builds the report (`otoroshi.cluster.mode`), `Off` for a standalone instance

all_nodes.description: The number of members registered in the datastore (a member expires when it is not seen for its timeout)

alive_nodes.description: The number of members seen within their timeout

leaders_count.description: The number of registered members whose type is `Leader`

workers_count.description: The number of registered members whose type is `Worker`

nodes.description: The members registered in the datastore, with their runtime and the system statistics they last sent

generic_entities.description: The number of entities of each kind the admin api serves, by `<group>/<plural name>` (the kinds of the admin extensions excluded)

additionalProperties.description: The number of entities of this kind

entities.description: The number of entities of the main kinds, with details on their use

scripts.description: The scripts (the plugins whose Scala code is stored in otoroshi and compiled at runtime), by plugin type: `app`, `transformer`, `validator`, `preroute`, `sink`, `listener`, `job`, `exporter`, `tunnel-handler`, `request-handler` or `composite`

routes.description: The route entities, disabled ones included, and the number of plugins they configure

count.description: The number of route entities, disabled ones included

plugins.description: The number of plugins configured on each route

router_routes.description: The routes the router matches the requests against: the enabled routes, and the routes built from the route compositions and from the apis

count.description: The number of routes the router knows, the ones built from the route compositions and the apis included

http_clients.description: The number of router routes by http client used to call their backends, chosen with the metadata of the route

ahc.description: The routes that call their backends with the default http client: they set neither `otoroshi-core-use-akka-http-client` nor `otoroshi-core-use-netty-http-client` to `true` in their metadata

akka.description: The routes that call their backends with the pekko http client: their metadata `otoroshi-core-use-akka-http-client` is `true`

netty.description: The routes that call their backends with the netty http client: their metadata `otoroshi-core-use-netty-http-client` is `true`

akka_ws.description: The routes that open their websockets with the pekko http client: their metadata `otoroshi-core-use-akka-http-ws-client` is `true`

plugins.description: The number of plugins of each route the router knows

route_compositions.description: The route compositions (entities grouping several routes, each with its own frontend and backend, under shared plugins)

count.description: The number of route composition entities, disabled ones included

plugins.description: The number of plugins of the route compositions and of their routes

by_kind.description: The number of route compositions by where their plugins are: `global` when none of their routes has plugins of its own, `local` when some have, `local_with_override` when one of them also overrides the plugins of the composition

additionalProperties.description: The number of route compositions of this kind

apikeys.description: The api keys, the number of them that use each feature, and the number of entities they are authorized on

count.description: The number of api keys, disabled ones included

by_kind.description: The number of api keys that use each feature, an api key counting under every feature it uses

disabled.description: The api keys whose `enabled` flag is false

with_rotation.description: The api keys whose secret rotation is enabled (`rotation.enabled`)

with_read_only.description: The api keys flagged `readOnly`: they only allow calls with the `GET`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` methods

with_client_id_only.description: The api keys flagged `allowClientIdOnly`: they can be presented with their client id alone, on the routes that accept it

with_constrained_services.description: The api keys flagged `constrainedServicesOnly`: they are only accepted by the routes that constrain the api keys they accept (with tag or metadata based routing)

with_meta.description: The api keys with at least one metadata entry

with_tags.description: The api keys with at least one tag

authorized_on.description: The number of entities (service groups, routes, route compositions, apis) each api key is authorized on

jwt_verifiers.description: The jwt verifier entities, by strategy and by kind of verification settings

count.description: The number of jwt verifier entities, disabled ones included

by_strategy.description: The number of jwt verifiers by strategy: `default_token`, `pass_through`, `sign` or `transform`

additionalProperties.description: The number of jwt verifiers with this strategy

by_alg.description: The number of jwt verifiers by kind of verification settings: `HSAlgoSettings` (hmac secret), `RSAlgoSettings`, `ESAlgoSettings` (public key), `JWKSAlgoSettings` (keys of a JWKS url), `RSAKPAlgoSettings`, `ESKPAlgoSettings` (key pair of a certificate) or `KidAlgoSettings` (the certificate named by the `kid` of the token)

additionalProperties.description: The number of jwt verifiers with this kind of verification settings

certificates.description: The certificates, by flag: `auto_renew`, `client`, `keypair`, `exposed` and `revoked`. A certificate counts under each of its flags, and a flag no certificate has is absent

auth_modules.description: The auth modules, by type: `basic`, `ldap`, `oauth2`, `oauth1`, `saml`, `wasm` or `workflow`

teams.description: The number of teams, the groups of entities of a tenant (organization) the rights of the admins are given on

tenants.description: The number of tenants (organizations), the top level partition of the entities and of the rights of the admins

service_groups.description: The number of service groups, the groups of routes an api key can be authorized on as a whole

otoroshi_admins.description: The admins stored in otoroshi, by type: `simple` (login and password) or `webauthn`

backoffice_sessions.description: The live sessions of the admins in the backoffice, by type of the auth module they logged in with, `simple` for an admin stored in otoroshi, `unknown` when the module no longer exists

private_apps_sessions.description: The live sessions of the users of the private apps (the routes protected by an auth module), by type of auth module, `unknown` when the module no longer exists

tcp_services.description: The number of tcp services, the entities that proxy raw tcp connections

plugins_usage.description: The number of uses of each plugin, by plugin id: its occurrences in the plugins of the routes the router knows, plus the global plugins and the global scripts of the global configuration when they are enabled

additionalProperties.description: The number of uses of this plugin

TunnelInfos.description: A tunnel connected to the cluster: the remote otoroshi at the other end, the routes it exposes, and the instances of the cluster it is connected to. A tunnel is listed for two minutes after the remote otoroshi last described it (every 10 seconds); a remote otoroshi that does not export its routes (`export-routes`) never describes it

tunnel_id.description: The id of the tunnel (`otoroshi.tunnels.<key>.id` on the remote otoroshi, the key by default): the `tunnel_id` of the `Remote tunnel calls` plugin of the routes that use it

name.description: The name the remote otoroshi gives the tunnel in its configuration (`otoroshi.tunnels.<key>.name`, `default` when absent): the label of the tunnel in the backoffice

routes.description: The routes the remote otoroshi exposes through the tunnel: all its routes, or only the ones tagged with its `export-routes-tag`

last_seen.description: When the remote otoroshi last described the tunnel, with a `tunnel_meta` message

nodes.description: The instances of the cluster the tunnel is connected to, one per address and ports

BadResponse.description: An error response answered by the snow monkey

status.description: The http status of the response. A string holding a number is read too. 500 when absent

body.description: The body of the response. `{"error":"..."}` when absent

headers.description: The http headers of the response. Empty when absent

GoReplayFileSettings.description: The settings of a GoReplay file exporter: the captured traffic (`TrafficCaptureEvent`, emitted by the routes with `capture` enabled) is written to a local file in the GoReplay format (`.gor`)
