maxFileSize.description: The maximum size of a capture file, in bytes. A new file is started once it is reached. Defaults to 10485760 (10 MB)

captureRequests.description: Whether the requests are captured. Defaults to true

captureResponses.description: Whether the responses are captured. Defaults to false

preferBackendRequest.description: Whether the captured request is the one otoroshi sent to the backend rather than the one the client sent. Defaults to false

preferBackendResponse.description: Whether the captured response is the one the backend sent rather than the one otoroshi sent to the client. Defaults to false

methods.description: The http methods of the calls captured. Empty for every method

StatsdConfig.description: The StatsD agent, or Datadog agent, the metrics of otoroshi are pushed to

onlyExposedCerts.description: Only use the key pairs of the certificates that are `exposed`, whose public keys otoroshi serves in its jwks (`/.well-known/otoroshi/security/jwks.json`). When false, any key pair of otoroshi can verify a token. False when missing

ApiDocumentationSearch.description: The search in a documentation: otoroshi only stores whether the developer portal offers it

LoadBalancingRoundRobin.description: The `RoundRobin` load balancing: sends the requests to the targets in turn, in the order of the list. The default

proxy.otoroshi.io.Draft.description: The draft of an entity being edited in the backoffice (an api for instance): the version of the entity not published yet, kept apart from the live one. A draft has the id of the entity it is the draft of

id.description: The unique id of the draft, the id of the entity it is the draft of

name.description: The display name of the draft, usually the name of the entity

description.description: A free text describing the draft, usually the one of the drafted entity: a draft subscription saved by the admin api gets the description of the subscription

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the draft

NgCacheConnectionSettings.description: The pool of connections the pekko http client keeps open to each target: the requests wait in a queue for a connection of the pool instead of opening their own

enabled.description: Whether the requests go through the pool of connections. Defaults to `false`

queue_size.description: How many requests can wait for a connection, the requests beyond being dropped. Defaults to `2048`

UserAnalyticsProjection.description: A family of events the user-analytics data exporter can store, each one in its own table: the gateway events, the fired user alerts, and the families of the admin extensions

id.description: The id of the projection, to use in `excluded_projections`

name.description: The readable name of the projection, shown in the settings of the user-analytics data exporter where projections can be excluded

description.description: What the events of the projection are and what stops working without them, shown next to its name
description.example: Every request proxied by Otoroshi. Feeds the core queries, the default dashboards and most alerts.

core.description: Whether the projection is built into otoroshi (`false` when an admin extension provides it)

table.description: The table the events are written to, with its schema, computed from the `schema` and `table_prefix` query parameters. `null` when the projection cannot tell

example.name: Gateway events
example.description: Every request proxied by Otoroshi. Feeds the core queries, the default dashboards and most alerts.

plugins.otoroshi.io.Workflow.description: A workflow of the workflows extension: a json tree of nodes (function calls, control flow, data transformations) that otoroshi runs on demand through the api, as a scheduled job, or from a route through the workflow plugins (backend, request and response transformers)

_loc.description: The tenant (organization) and the teams the workflow belongs to. The default tenant and team when absent

id.description: The unique id of the workflow, used to call it, to schedule it and to reference it from a plugin or from another workflow

name.description: The display name of the workflow, shown and searched in the list of the workflows of the backoffice

description.description: A free text describing what the workflow does, shown and searched in the list of the workflows of the backoffice
description.example: Greets the name given as input and logs the greeting

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the workflow, with string values. The admin api stores the date of the last write of the entity under `created_at` or `updated_at`

tags.description: Free tags of the workflow, to sort and search the workflows

config.description: The root node of the workflow, run with the input of the workflow (available to the nodes as `workflow_input`). A node is a json object whose `kind` selects what it does, its other fields depend on its kind: a `workflow` node runs its `steps` (an array of nodes) in sequence, a `call` node calls the function named by `function` with its `args`, `if`, `switch`, `foreach`, `map`, `filter`, `flatmap`, `parallel`, `while`, `try`, `jump` and `async` nodes hold other nodes. The strings of a node can read the memory of the run with `${<name>}` or `${<name>.<path>}`, and objects with a single key starting with `$` are operators (`$mem_ref`, `$str_concat`, `$eq`, ...). An empty object when absent

id.description: The id of the node, shown in the logs, the errors and the debugger of the run. A random id when absent

kind.description: The kind of the node: `workflow`, `call`, `assign`, `value`, `if`, `switch`, `foreach`, `map`, `filter`, `flatmap`, `parallel`, `while`, `try`, `jump`, `async`, `wait`, `error`, `pause`, `end` or `breakpoint`, or the kind of a node registered by an extension. A node of an unknown kind does nothing

description.description: What the node does, for the readers of the workflow
description.example: Greets the input name then logs the greeting

enabled.description: Whether the node runs, true when absent. A disabled node is skipped and returns null

breakpoint.description: Whether the debugger of the editor pauses the run before this node, false when absent

result.description: The name of the memory slot the result of the node is stored in, for the next nodes to read it with `${<name>}`

returned.description: A json value that replaces the output of the node, its operators applied first (for instance `{"$mem_ref": {"name": "call_res"}}` returns the content of the memory slot `call_res`)

example.description: Greets the input name then logs the greeting

test_payload.description: The input sent to the workflow when it is run from the editor of the backoffice, available to the nodes as `workflow_input`. Free json object, `{"name": "foo"}` when absent

orphans.description: The nodes of the editor canvas that are not connected to the tree of the workflow, kept with the edges between them so that the editor shows them again. They are never run

nodes.description: The nodes that are not connected to the tree of the workflow

items.description: A workflow node (the same shape as `config`) with its place on the canvas

id.description: The id of the node, that the `source` and `target` of the edges name

kind.description: The kind of the node, as in `config`

position.description: The position of the node on the canvas, in pixels

edges.description: The edges of the canvas that start from or end at an orphan node

items.description: An edge of the editor canvas between two nodes. Free json object, the editor writes the fields below

id.description: The id of the edge on the canvas, generated by the editor

source.description: The id of the node the edge starts from

target.description: The id of the node the edge ends at

sourceHandle.description: The handle of the source node the edge starts from

targetHandle.description: The handle of the target node the edge ends at

type.description: The kind of edge drawn by the editor

animated.description: Whether the editor animates the edge

job.description: Runs the workflow as a job of otoroshi: once, at a fixed interval or on a cron expression. Not scheduled when absent

functions.description: The functions of the workflow, by name: nodes a `call` node of the workflow runs with `"function": "self.<name>"`, the arguments of the call being available to the function as `function_args`. Empty when absent

additionalProperties.description: The node run when the function is called, the same shape as `config`

id.description: The id of the root node of the function, shown in the logs, the errors and the debugger of the run

kind.description: The kind of the node, as in `config`

notes.description: The notes placed on the canvas of the editor. They are not part of the workflow, and a note without `id`, `kind`, `position` or `measured` makes otoroshi drop every note

items.description: A note of the editor canvas: a text box with its colors, its place and its size

content.description: The text of the note, empty when absent

color.description: The background color of the note, a css color, `var(--bg-color_level3)` when absent

titleColor.description: The color of the text of the note, a css color, `#fff` when absent

position.description: The position of the note on the canvas, in pixels

measured.description: The size of the note on the canvas, in pixels

width.description: The width of the note, in pixels

height.description: The height of the note, in pixels

id.description: The id of the note on the canvas

kind.description: The kind of the canvas node, `note` for a note

example.description: Greets the name given as input and logs the greeting

config.description: Greets the input name then logs the greeting

ApiAccessModeConfiguration.description: The configuration of the access mode of a plan. Its shape depends on the `access_mode_configuration_type` of the plan: `KeylessAccessModeConfiguration` for `keyless`, `ApikeyAccessModeConfiguration` for `apikey`, `JWTAccessModeConfiguration` for `jwt`, `MtlsAccessModeConfiguration` for `mtls`, `OAuth2AccessModeConfiguration` for `oauth2-local` and `OAuth2RemoteAccessModeConfiguration` for `oauth2-remote`. A configuration that cannot be read for the access mode of the plan is ignored, the access mode then runs with its defaults

BasicAuthUser.description: A user of an in memory auth module

name.description: The display name of the user, the `name` of its profile and of its sessions, shown in the lists of sessions of the backoffice

password.description: The bcrypt hash of the password of the user. The api stores the value as sent: send a bcrypt hash

email.description: The email of the user, the login it uses

metadata.description: The metadata of the user, any json object: part of its profile, and its otoroshi data sent to the backends of the private apps

tags.description: Free tags of the user, written in its profile (`profile.tags`) where the user validators of the module can check them

webauthn.description: The WebAuthn devices of the user, used when the module enables the WebAuthn login, null when it has none

rights.description: The rights of the user on the tenants (organizations) and teams of otoroshi when it logs in to the backoffice. Missing rights are no rights, unless `superAdminWhenNoRights` of the global configuration is on. `[{"tenant": "*:rw", "teams": ["*:rw"]}]` makes a super admin

adminEntityValidators.description: The validators the entities written by this user through the backoffice have to pass, by entity kind

additionalProperties.description: The validators of an entity kind, keyed by the singular name of the kind (`route`, `apikey`, `certificate`...) or `all` for every kind. Every validator has to pass for the entity to be written

route.error: routes can only be exposed on oto.tools

ErrorResponse.description: An error answered by the admin api

error.description: The error, as a short code or as a message

error_description.description: What went wrong: a message, the messages of the validation, or the errors of the fields that could not be read

kind.description: The group and the kind of the entity the call was about

Otoroshi-Error.description: The error, when the call is refused before reaching the admin api: missing or wrong credentials, exceeded quotas

JMSExporterSettings.description: The settings of a JMS exporter: the events are sent to a JMS queue or topic (ActiveMQ)

url.description: The url of the broker. Defaults to `tcp://localhost:61616`

name.description: The name of the queue or the topic. Defaults to `otoroshi-events`

topic.description: Whether `name` is a topic (true) or a queue (false). Defaults to true

username.description: The user to connect with, null for none. A blank value is read as null

password.description: The password of the user, null for none. A blank value is read as null

green-score.extensions.otoroshi.io.Green.description: A green score group: routes whose eco design otoroshi scores. name.description: The display name of the green score group, shown in the table of the green score groups of the backoffice

description.description: A free text describing the green score group, shown in the table of the green score groups of the backoffice
description.example: The green score of the routes of the public apis

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the green score group, with string values. The admin api stores the date of the last write of the entity under `created_at` or `updated_at`

tags.description: Free tags of the green score group, to sort and search the groups

routes.description: The routes of the group with the green rules each one follows. Empty when absent

kind.description: The visibility of the api: `public`, `semi_public`, `private`, or `custom` when its configuration says who sees it. An unknown value is read as `private`, a missing one as `public`

MailgunSettings.description: A mailer sending the emails through the api of Mailgun

domain.description: The sending domain of the Mailgun account

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

BuiltResourceOutcome.description: An entity built, or the error of its definition

ApiKeyRotation.description: The automatic rotation of the secret of an api key: once the rotation period is over, a new secret is generated (`nextSecret`), both secrets are accepted during the grace period, then the new one replaces the old one

enabled.description: Whether the secret rotates. Defaults to false

rotationEvery.description: The lifetime of a secret, in hours. Defaults to 744 (31 days)

ServiceStatusDate.description: The health checks of a route on a day

date.description: The start of the day, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds

dateAsString.description: The start of the day, as Elasticsearch writes it

total.description: The number of health checks of the day

status.description: The health checks of the day, by health

id.description: The id the instance generated when it started (`node_` followed by a uuid)

version.description: The version of the json format of a dropwizard registry: the registry otoroshi uses does not write it

gauges.description: The gauges by name, tags included, each with its `value`

counters.description: The counters by name, tags included, each with its `count`

histograms.description: The histograms by name, tags included, each with its `count` and the statistics of its values

meters.description: The meters by name, tags included, each with its `count` and its rates

serial.description: The serial number of the certificate. It can be greater than a 64 bits integer

csr.description: A certificate signing request built for the domain and the subject of the certificate, PEM encoded

key.description: The private key of the certificate, PEM encoded (PKCS#8)

ca.description: The certificate of the authority that issued the certificate, PEM encoded

query.description: The domain and the subject of the certificate, as a certificate query

certId.description: The id of the certificate entity otoroshi stored for the certificate

CustomMetricsSettings.description: The settings of a custom metrics exporter: it computes the metrics it lists from the events and adds them to the metrics exposed by otoroshi (Prometheus, ...)

tags.description: Tags added to every metric

metrics.description: The metrics updated for each exported event, each with its name, its kind, the events it applies to and its labels

UserAnalyticsQueryFilters.description: The data a query runs on. The tenant (organization) is not a filter: it always comes from the `Otoroshi-Tenant` header

from.description: The start of the time range (inclusive): `now`, `now-<n><unit>` with a unit among `s`, `m`, `h` and `d` (like `now-30m` or `now-7d`), or an ISO-8601 instant (like `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`). `now-1h` when missing or invalid

to.description: The end of the time range (exclusive): `now`, `now-<n><unit>` with a unit among `s`, `m`, `h` and `d` (like `now-30m` or `now-7d`), or an ISO-8601 instant (like `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`). `now` when missing or invalid

route_id.description: Only keep the requests handled by this route (its id)

api_id.description: Only keep the requests handled by this api (its id)

apikey_id.description: Only keep the requests made with this api key (its client id)

group_id.description: Only keep the requests handled by a route of this service group (its id)

err.description: Only keep the requests in error (`true`) or the successful ones (`false`)

ApiPlanVisibility.description: How a plan is shown in a developer portal, with a free configuration for the portal

kind.description: The visibility of the plan: `public`, `semi_public`, `private`, or `custom` when its configuration says who sees it. An unknown value is read as `private`, a missing one as `public`

config.description: The configuration of the visibility, for the portal that shows the plan. Defaults to an empty object

LoadBalancingRandom.description: The `Random` load balancing: sends each request to a target chosen at random

type.description: Selects the random load balancing: each request goes to a target picked at random

ApiDocumentationSource.description: A remote documentation: otoroshi fetches it (a documentation in the same json format) and merges it with the local one. The lists of both are concatenated, the remote footer and banner win over the local ones, and every other field but the source comes from the remote documentation. When it does not answer a `200` with a documentation, the api has none

url.description: The url of the remote documentation. The relative urls of the resources (starting with `.`) are resolved against it. Without it nothing is fetched

headers.description: The http headers sent to fetch the remote documentation

timeout.description: The timeout of the call, in milliseconds. Defaults to `30000`

follow_redirects.description: Whether the redirections are followed. Defaults to `true`

RSAKPAlgoSettings.description: Tokens signed with RSA and SHA-2 (`RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512`) using the key pair of a certificate of otoroshi

type.description: The algorithm settings, always `RSAKPAlgoSettings`

size.description: The size of the SHA-2 hash of the algorithm, in bits: 256, 384 or 512 (`RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512` for instance)

certId.description: The id of the certificate holding the RSA key pair. Its id is also the `kid` of the tokens otoroshi signs

HttpListenerConfig.description: The settings of the http server of an http listener: the port and interface it binds to, the protocols it speaks and its tls settings

enabled.description: Whether the server of the listener runs, false when absent

exclusive.description: Whether the listener only serves the routes bound to it through their `bound_listeners`. A listener that is not exclusive also serves the routes bound to no listener. False when absent

tls.description: Whether the listener speaks https, with the certificates of otoroshi, instead of plain http. True when absent

http1.description: Whether the listener speaks http/1.1, true when absent

http2.description: Whether the listener speaks http/2 over tls (negotiated with alpn), true when absent

h2c.description: Whether the listener speaks http/2 in clear text, without tls, false when absent

http3.description: Whether the listener speaks http/3 (quic), on an udp socket of the same port. Only with `tls`. False when absent

port.description: The port the listener binds to, 7890 when absent

exposedPort.description: The port the clients reach the listener on, when it differs from `port` (behind a load balancer, a proxy or a container port mapping). `port` when absent

host.description: The network interface the listener binds to, `0.0.0.0` (every interface) when absent

accessLog.description: Whether the listener writes an access log of the calls it serves, false when absent

clientAuth.description: Whether the tls handshake asks the client for a certificate (mtls): `None` never, `Want` asks for an optional one, `Need` requires one, `Dynamic` follows the client auth of the tls settings of the global configuration. Read without case, `None` when absent or unknown

TunnelRoute.description: A route a remote otoroshi exposes through its tunnel

name.description: The name of the route on the remote otoroshi. The tunnels page of the backoffice names the route it creates to expose it after it

id.description: The id of the route on the remote otoroshi, kept in the `from_route_id` metadata of the route the backoffice creates to expose it

frontend.description: The first domain of the frontend of the route, its path included: the backoffice uses it as the hostname and the root of the target of the route it creates to expose it

IpFiltering.description: The client addresses allowed or refused on every request, before any route is looked for. An entry is an ip address (v4 or v6), a CIDR range (`10.0.0.0/8`) or a pattern where `*` matches anything (`192.168.1.*`). In each list, a single string is read as a one entry list and the entries that are not strings are left out

whitelist.description: The addresses allowed to call otoroshi. When the list is not empty, a client whose address matches no entry is refused with a 403 error. Empty when absent

items.description: An address, a CIDR range or a pattern

blacklist.description: The addresses refused with a 403 error. Empty when absent

items.description: An address, a CIDR range or a pattern

blacklistMatchesForwardedChain.description: Also refuse a request when a blacklisted address appears anywhere in the proxy chain of the client address header, not only when it is the resolved client address. Only applies while trustXForwarded is true. The client writes part of that chain, so it never applies to the whitelist. `false` when absent

ApiDeployment.description: A deployment of an api: a snapshot of what a deploy of its draft put in production, kept for audit and rollback

id.description: The id of the deployment, generated when missing

apiRef.description: The id of the deployed api, the one holding the deployment in its `deployments`. Also the `apiRef` of the `ApiDeploymentEvent` sent for the deployment

owner.description: Who deployed the api: the name or the id of the admin, or the `created_by` metadata of the api for the deploys of a remote catalog

at.description: When the api was deployed, a timestamp in milliseconds. Defaults to the time it is read

apiDefinition.description: The design that was deployed: the fields of the api locked in production. It is kept as it is sent

routes.description: The routes that were deployed, in the format of the `routes` of the api

backends.description: The backends that were deployed, in the format of the `backends` of the api

flows.description: The flows that were deployed, in the format of the `flows` of the api

documentation.description: The documentation of the api, `null` for none

version.description: The version of the api that was deployed. Defaults to `0.0.1`

GeneratedCertificate.description: A certificate generated by the pki of otoroshi, as a certificate entity, with the id it was stored under

allOf.description: The id the certificate was stored under

certId.description: The id of the stored certificate entity, the same as its `id`. Absent when the certificate is not stored (`persist=false`)

UserAnalyticsAlertEventsPage.description: A page of fired events of a user alert

limit.description: The maximum number of events of the page, the `limit` query parameter brought back between 1 and 2000 (200 by default)

offset.description: The number of events skipped before the page, the `offset` query parameter (0 by default)

items.message: More than 5% of the requests failed

WasmSource.description: Where the wasm of a module comes from

kind.description: The kind of source: `Base64` (the module itself, base64 encoded, in `path`), `Http` (an url), `Wasmo` (a plugin built by the wasmo of the global configuration), `Local` (another wasm plugin, by id), `File` (a file of the host), `ClassPath` (a resource of the classpath of otoroshi), `Unknown` when none. Read whatever its case, `wasmmanager` being read as `Wasmo`

path.description: The module, where to find it: the base64 module, the url, the wasmo plugin name, the id of the wasm plugin, the file path or the classpath resource, depending on the kind

opts.description: The options of the source. `Http`: `method`, `headers`, `timeout` (milliseconds), `followRedirect`, `proxy` and `tls`. `Wasmo`: `follow_redirect` and `timeout` (milliseconds)

InHeader.description: A jwt token read from a header of the request. When otoroshi writes a token (signed or transformed), it is written in the same header, prefixed by `remove`

type.description: The location of the token, always `InHeader`

name.description: The name of the header holding the token

remove.description: A text removed from the value of the header to get the token, like `Bearer ` (with its trailing space). Empty when missing

ApiDocumentationResourceRef.description: A link to a reference of an api, for instance its openapi document

title.description: The text of the link to the reference. Required

description.description: A short text shown with the link to the reference. Optional
description.example: The openapi document of the api

link.description: The url the link leads to: the openapi document of the api, a guide, a status page... Required

icon.description: The icon shown next to the link to the reference: a documentation resource holding an image or a css icon class (`css_icon_class`). Optional

example.title: OpenAPI specification
example.description: The openapi document of the api

AllowedQuota.description: The numbers of calls a throttling strategy allows per window, per day and per month. A missing quota is 10000000 calls

window.description: The number of calls allowed per window of the strategy (the throttling window, or `windowDurationMs`). Not used by the token bucket strategy. Defaults to 10000000

daily.description: The number of calls allowed per day. Defaults to 10000000

monthly.description: The number of calls allowed per month. Defaults to 10000000

TunnelRequest.description: A request sent through a tunnel to the remote otoroshi, that routes it as if it had received it

request_id.description: The id of the request, its answer carrying the same one. Generated when absent, as `<otoroshiId of the global configuration>-<id of the instance>-<uuid>-<counter>`

type.description: Marks the message as a request to route (the other messages of a tunnel are `response`, `ping`, `pong` and `tunnel_meta`)

url.description: The full url of the request, as the route that sends it through the tunnel would call its backend (the target of its backend, then the path and the query). The remote otoroshi takes the path and the query of the request from it

path.description: The path and the query of the request, informative: the remote otoroshi takes them from `url`

method.description: The http method the remote otoroshi handles the request with, like `GET` or `POST`

headers.description: The headers of the request, one value per name, as the route would send them to its backend

query.description: The query parameters of the request, by name, informative: the remote otoroshi takes the query from `url`

version.description: The http protocol version of the request, like `HTTP/1.1` or `HTTP/2.0`

addr.description: The ip address of the client of the request

secured.description: Whether the request came over https, as a boolean. The instances of the cluster write it as the string `true` or `false`, which the remote otoroshi reads as false

oneOf.description: Whether the request came over https
The string the instances of the cluster write, `true` or `false`

hasBody.description: Whether the request has a body

body.description: The body of the request, base64 encoded, read by the remote otoroshi when present. The `Remote tunnel calls` plugin does not send it: the requests of a route go through the tunnel without their body

cookies.description: The cookies of the request, the remote otoroshi reading their `name`, `value`, `path`, `domain`, `maxAge`, `secure` and `httpOnly`

client_cert_chain.description: The client certificate chain of the request, as PEM certificates the remote otoroshi gives the route as the client certificates of the request. `null` without client certificates

backend.description: The target the route picked for the request, as json (an `NgTarget`: `id`, `hostname`, `port`, `tls`...). Informative, not read by the remote otoroshi

CustomDataExporterRefConfig.description: A custom filter or transformation of the events of a data exporter, done by a plugin, a wasm plugin or a workflow

kind.description: What `ref` designates: a custom data exporter filter or transformer plugin (`plugin`), a wasm plugin (`wasm`) or a workflow (`workflow`). Lowercased when read, defaults to `plugin`

ref.description: The reference of the plugin, the id of the wasm plugin or the id of the workflow. A filter or transformation with an empty ref is read as null

config.description: The configuration given to the plugin, the wasm plugin or the workflow

WorkflowJobConfig.description: How a workflow runs as a job of otoroshi, and the input of each run. The job is scheduled as soon as the workflow is saved with `enabled` true, and stopped when it is disabled or deleted. A job without `kind` or `instantiation` is read as the default job (disabled)

enabled.description: Whether the workflow is scheduled as a job, false when absent

kind.description: When the job runs: `ScheduledOnce` once after `initial_delay`, `ScheduledEvery` after `initial_delay` then every `interval`, `Cron` on `cron_expression`, `Autonomous` once after `initial_delay`. Read without case, an unknown value is read as `ScheduledEvery`

instantiation.description: Where the job runs in a cluster: `OneInstancePerOtoroshiInstance` on every instance, `OneInstancePerOtoroshiWorkerInstance` on every worker, `OneInstancePerOtoroshiLeaderInstance` on every leader, `OneInstancePerOtoroshiCluster` on a single instance of the cluster. Read without case, an unknown value is read as `OneInstancePerOtoroshiInstance`

initial_delay.description: The delay before the first run, in milliseconds. No delay when null

interval.description: The delay between two runs of a `ScheduledEvery` job, in milliseconds. A `ScheduledEvery` job without interval only runs once

cron_expression.description: The quartz cron expression (seconds, minutes, hours, day of month, month, day of week) of a `Cron` job

config.description: The input of the workflow on each run of the job, available to the nodes as `workflow_input`. Free json object, empty when absent

PKCEConfig.description: The PKCE extension (RFC 7636) of the authorization code flow

enabled.description: Use PKCE in the authorization code flow. False when missing

algorithm.description: The code challenge method: `S256` (the SHA-256 hash of the code verifier) or `plain`. Any other value is used as `plain`. `S256` when missing

FormPatch.description: The fields to change, by dotted path, and their new value. A value is read as json when it is `null`, `true`, `false`, a number, an object or an array

additionalProperties.description: The new value of the field

InstanceLocation.description: Where an otoroshi instance runs, as declared in its configuration (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location`). The relay routing uses it to pick the instances that can reach a backend

provider.description: The cloud provider or hosting of the instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.provider` or `otoroshi.instance.provider`, `local` by default). Matched against the `otoroshi-deployment-providers` metadata of a route

zone.description: The availability zone of the instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.zone` or `otoroshi.instance.zone`, `local` by default). Matched against the `otoroshi-deployment-zones` metadata of a route

region.description: The region of the instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.region` or `otoroshi.instance.region`, `local` by default). Matched against the `otoroshi-deployment-regions` metadata of a route

datacenter.description: The datacenter of the instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.datacenter` or `otoroshi.instance.dc`, `local` by default). Matched against the `otoroshi-deployment-dcs` metadata of a route

rack.description: The rack of the instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.rack` or `otoroshi.instance.rack`, `local` by default). Matched against the `otoroshi-deployment-racks` metadata of a route

CustomQuotasIncr.description: A quotas update: the calls counted by a `Custom quotas` plugin on a worker since its last update. The leaders add them to the daily and monthly counters of the plugin for this expression and group

typ.description: Selects the calls counted by a `Custom quotas` plugin (`custquots`): the leaders add them to its counters

e.description: The `expression` of the plugin once evaluated (`${req.ip}` by default): the value the calls are counted by, like the ip address of the client

g.description: The group of the counter once evaluated: the `group` expression of the plugin, the id of the route when absent and `perRoute` is set, `global` otherwise

c.description: The number of calls to add to the counters. Defaults to 0

ApiKeyDeletion.description: The outcome of the deletion of an api key

deleted.description: Always true: the api key is deleted

NgStep.description: A step of the handling of a request where a plugin runs: `Sink` (answers the requests no route matches), `PreRoute`, `ValidateAccess`, `TransformRequest`, `CallBackend`, `TransformResponse`, `MatchRoute` (decides whether a route matches), `Router`, `HandlesTunnel`, `HandlesRequest` (handles the whole request). `Job`, `DataExporterFilter` and `DataExporterTransform` are the steps of the plugins that are jobs or that filter and transform the events of the data exporters

BuiltResourceError.description: A definition that could not be built

error.description: Why it could not be built: an unknown kind, or a definition its format refuses

name.description: The `name` of the definition, `Unknown` when it has none

ResourceVersion.description: The version of a kind of entity

name.description: The name of the version, in the paths of the api

served.description: Whether the generic api serves the version

storage.description: Whether the entities are stored in this version

schema.description: The json schema of the entities. With `schema=false`, only the hand written schema of the core entities, `null` for the entities described by reflection on their class

proxy.otoroshi.io.ErrorTemplate.description: The html pages otoroshi answers instead of its own error pages when a call to a route fails (4xx and 5xx errors, maintenance, build mode). A client asking for json gets a json error instead. The error template of id `global` applies to every route without one of its own

serviceId.description: The id of the route the error template applies to, which is also the id of the error template. `global` for the error template of every route without one of its own

name.description: The display name of the error template, the `serviceId` when missing

description.description: A free text describing the error template, the `serviceId` when missing
description.example: The branded error pages of the users api

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the error template

tags.description: Free tags to search, sort and group the error templates

template40x.description: The html page answered for the 4xx errors (401, 403, 404...). The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

template50x.description: The html page answered for the 5xx errors (502, 503...), and for the errors no other template covers. The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

templateBuild.description: The html page answered while the route is under construction (cause `errors.service.under.construction`). The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

templateMaintenance.description: The html page answered while the route is in maintenance (cause `errors.service.in.maintenance`). The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

additionalProperties.description: The html page answered for the matching causes. The placeholders `${status}`, `${message}`, `${cause}`, `${otoroshiMessage}` and `${errorId}` are replaced by the details of the error

genericTemplates.description: The html pages answered for some causes of error, by cause id. A key is a cause id (like `errors.service.not.found`) or a pattern of cause ids where `*` is a wildcard. These pages take precedence over the other templates

messages.description: Messages replacing the ones of otoroshi in the pages and in the json errors. A key is `message-<status>` (like `message-404`) to replace the message of the errors of a status, or a cause id (like `errors.service.not.found`) to replace the cause

example.name: Users API errors
example.description: The branded error pages of the users api

messages.errors.service.in.maintenance: The users api is in maintenance

NodeCategory.description: A category of nodes of the workflows

id.description: The id of the category, like `core`, `flow`, `transformations` or `functions`

name.description: The readable name of the category, like `JSON Transformations`

description.description: What the nodes of the category do
description.example: Run code, make HTTP requests, etc

nodes.description: The names of the nodes, or of the operators, the category groups. Empty when the category lists none, like `functions`: the functions carry `functions` as their `category` instead

example.name: Core
example.description: Run code, make HTTP requests, etc

DataExporterConfig.webhook.description: A data exporter of type `webhook`: each batch of events is posted as a json array to a url

type.description: The type of the exporter: `webhook`, each batch of events is posted as a json array to a url

enabled.description: Whether the exporter runs. A disabled exporter keeps its settings but exports nothing. Defaults to false

id.description: The unique id of the exporter, the key it is stored under and the `{id}` of its urls in the admin api. The templates generate `data_exporter_<uuid>` (`data_exporter_<env>_<uuid>` outside the `prod` environment)

name.description: The display name of the exporter, shown in the backoffice

desc.description: A description of the exporter. Defaults to `--`
desc.example: Alerts to the ops webhook, managed by the platform team

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the exporter

tags.description: Free tags of the exporter, to search and sort it

bufferSize.description: The maximum number of events waiting to be exported. Once it is reached, the oldest waiting events are dropped. Defaults to 5000

jsonWorkers.description: The number of events turned into json (and enriched) in parallel. Defaults to 1

sendWorkers.description: The number of batches sent in parallel. Defaults to 5

groupSize.description: The maximum number of events of a batch: a batch is sent once it is full or once `groupDuration` is elapsed. Defaults to 100

groupDuration.description: The maximum delay before a batch is sent, in milliseconds, even when it is not full. Defaults to 30000

projection.description: The fields of the events that are exported, as a json object: `{"field": true}` keeps a field, operators like `$at`, `$path`, `$jq` or `$date_from_unix_fmt` compute new ones (see the documentation of the data exporters). An empty object exports the whole events

customFilter.description: A custom filter, applied after `filtering`: the events it refuses are not exported. Null for none

customTransform.description: A custom transformation of the events, applied before they are exported. Null for none

config.description: The url the batches of events are posted to, and the headers and tls settings of the calls

example.name: Alerts to the ops webhook
example.desc: Alerts to the ops webhook, managed by the platform team

NgBackend.description: Where the requests of a route are forwarded: the targets, how one is chosen, how otoroshi calls them and checks their health. A `url` key (or `target`, `target_url`) holding a full url is read too: it replaces `targets` by the single target of the url, and `root` by its path

targets.description: The servers the requests are forwarded to

root.description: The path prepended to the path of the forwarded requests. Defaults to `/`

rewrite.description: Whether the path of the forwarded requests is `root` alone, instead of `root` followed by the path of the request. `root` can then use the expression language, like `/users/${req.pathparams.id}` with the named path params of the frontend. Defaults to `false`

load_balancing.description: How a target is chosen for each request. Defaults to round robin

client.description: How otoroshi calls the targets: retries, timeouts, circuit breaker, http proxy

health_check.description: How otoroshi checks the health of the targets. Null when their health is not checked

UserAnalyticsQueryResponse.description: The result of a user analytics query, with its comparison with the previous period when asked for

compare.description: The result of the same query on the previous period of the same length. Only present when `compare` was asked for and the query supports it

Restrictions.description: Restrictions on the paths an api key can call. With `allowLast` true, the calls matching a `notFound` path are answered 404, the ones matching a `forbidden` path 403, and the others pass. With `allowLast` false, the calls matching an `allowed` path pass, then the ones matching a `notFound` path are answered 404, the ones matching a `forbidden` path 403, and all the others 404

enabled.description: Whether the restrictions are applied. Defaults to false

allowLast.description: When true, only the `notFound` and `forbidden` paths are checked and everything else is allowed. When false, only the `allowed` paths can be called. Defaults to true

allowed.description: The paths the api key can call, checked first when `allowLast` is false. A path that cannot be read is dropped

forbidden.description: The paths answered 403. A path that cannot be read is dropped

notFound.description: The paths answered 404, as if they did not exist. A path that cannot be read is dropped

UserAnalyticsTimeseriesPoint.description: A point of a timeseries: the value of a time bucket. Every bucket of the time range has its point, the buckets without data included

ts.description: The start of the time bucket, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds

value.description: The value for this time bucket (0 when there is no data)

ApiDocumentationSidebarLink.description: A link of a sidebar of a documentation

kind.description: The kind of the entry, `link`, the default

label.description: The label of the link. Defaults to `No label`

icon.description: The icon shown next to the label of the link: a documentation resource holding an image or a css icon class (`css_icon_class`). Optional

link.description: The path or the url the link leads to. Defaults to `#`

DataExporterConfig.jms.description: A data exporter of type `jms`: the events are sent to a JMS queue or topic

type.description: The type of the exporter: `jms`, the events are sent to a JMS queue or topic

enabled.description: Whether the exporter runs. A disabled exporter keeps its settings but exports nothing. Defaults to false

id.description: The unique id of the exporter, the key it is stored under and the `{id}` of its urls in the admin api. The templates generate `data_exporter_<uuid>` (`data_exporter_<env>_<uuid>` outside the `prod` environment)

name.description: The display name of the exporter, shown in the backoffice

desc.description: A description of the exporter. Defaults to `--`
desc.example: Events to ActiveMQ, managed by the platform team

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the exporter

tags.description: Free tags of the exporter, to search and sort it

bufferSize.description: The maximum number of events waiting to be exported. Once it is reached, the oldest waiting events are dropped. Defaults to 5000

jsonWorkers.description: The number of events turned into json (and enriched) in parallel. Defaults to 1

sendWorkers.description: The number of batches sent in parallel. Defaults to 5

groupSize.description: The maximum number of events of a batch: a batch is sent once it is full or once `groupDuration` is elapsed. Defaults to 100

groupDuration.description: The maximum delay before a batch is sent, in milliseconds, even when it is not full. Defaults to 30000

projection.description: The fields of the events that are exported, as a json object: `{"field": true}` keeps a field, operators like `$at`, `$path`, `$jq` or `$date_from_unix_fmt` compute new ones (see the documentation of the data exporters). An empty object exports the whole events

customFilter.description: A custom filter, applied after `filtering`: the events it refuses are not exported. Null for none

customTransform.description: A custom transformation of the events, applied before they are exported. Null for none
