example.desc: Events to ActiveMQ, managed by the platform team

S3Configuration.description: The connection to an S3 compatible object storage, and the object the data is written to

bucket.description: The name of the bucket the objects are written to

endpoint.description: The url of the S3 api

region.description: The region of the bucket. Defaults to `eu-west-1`

access.description: The access key id of the credentials the requests are signed with

secret.description: The secret access key of the credentials, paired with `access`

key.description: The key (path) of the objects in the bucket: the exporters use it as the prefix of the names of the files they upload. A leading `/` is removed when read

chunkSize.description: The size of the chunks of a multipart upload, in bytes. Defaults to 8388608 (8 MB)

v4auth.description: Whether the requests are signed with AWS signature v4 (v2 otherwise). Defaults to true

writeEvery.description: The delay between two uploads of the current file, in milliseconds. Defaults to 60000

acl.description: The canned ACL of the objects written. The names of the canned ACLs (`Private`, `PublicRead`, ...) are read too, an unknown value is read as `private`

pathStyleAccess.description: Whether the bucket is addressed in the path of the urls rather than in their host. Defaults to false

JwtTokenLocation.description: Where a jwt token is in a request: a header (`InHeader`), a query parameter (`InQueryParam`) or a cookie (`InCookie`)

UserAnalyticsQueryRequest.description: The body of `POST /api/analytics/_query`: the id of a query of the catalog, its parameters, the data it runs on, the size of its time buckets and how its result is cached

query.description: The id of the query, as listed by `GET /api/analytics/_schema`

params.description: The parameters of the query, as listed in its `params`, like `{"top_n": 10}` for the top N queries

filters.description: The data the query runs on: the last hour of every request of the tenant (organization) when absent

bucket.description: The time bucket size of timeseries and heatmaps: `1m`, `5m`, `1h`, `6h` or `1d`. When missing or unknown, it depends on the time range: up to 1 hour `1m`, up to 24 hours `1h`, up to 7 days `6h`, `1d` beyond

compare.description: Also run the query on the previous period of the same length and return it in `compare`. Ignored by the queries that do not support it (`supports_compare` in the catalog)

nocache.description: Run the query even if its result is in the cache, and do not cache the new one

SyslogExporterSettings.description: The settings of a syslog exporter: the events are sent as syslog messages, over TCP (optionally over tls), over UDP, or to a unix socket

tcp.description: Whether the messages are sent over TCP. Defaults to false

udp.description: Whether the messages are sent over UDP, when `tcp` is false. Defaults to true

host.description: The host of the syslog server, or the path of the socket when `unix_socket` is true. Defaults to `/var/run/syslog`

port.description: The port of the syslog server. Defaults to 514

unix_socket.description: Whether `host` is the path of a unix socket. Defaults to true

connect_timeout.description: The timeout of the connection, in milliseconds. Defaults to 10000

tls.description: The tls settings of the TCP connection, used when `enabled` is true

ApiStateHook.description: A hook of the lifecycle of an api: a reference and its configuration. Otoroshi stores it, it does not call it itself

ref.description: The reference of the hook. Defaults to an empty string

config.description: The configuration of the hook. Defaults to an empty object

LoadBalancingIpAddressHash.description: The `IpAddressHash` load balancing: sends the requests of a client ip address to the same target, chosen by consistent hashing of the ip address

type.description: Selects the load balancing on the ip address: the requests of a client ip address go to the same target

RemainingQuotas.description: The quotas of an api key: the calls it is allowed to make in the current throttling window, day and month, the calls it made, and the calls it has left. The quotas of an api key without limit are 10000000

authorizedCallsPerWindow.description: The calls the api key is allowed to make during a throttling window (the `throttlingQuota` of the api key, per second for the legacy strategy)

throttlingCallsPerWindow.description: The calls the api key made during the current throttling window

remainingCallsPerWindow.description: The calls the api key can still make during the current throttling window

authorizedCallsPerDay.description: The calls the api key is allowed to make per day (its `dailyQuota`)

currentCallsPerDay.description: The calls the api key made today

remainingCallsPerDay.description: The calls the api key can still make today

authorizedCallsPerMonth.description: The calls the api key is allowed to make per month (its `monthlyQuota`)

currentCallsPerMonth.description: The calls the api key made this month

remainingCallsPerMonth.description: The calls the api key can still make this month

MailjetSettings.description: A mailer sending the emails through the api of Mailjet

type.description: The type of the mailer, `mailjet`

apiKeyPublic.description: The public api key of the Mailjet account

apiKeyPrivate.description: The private api key (secret key) of the Mailjet account

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

InQueryParam.description: A jwt token read from a query parameter of the request

type.description: The location of the token, always `InQueryParam`

name.description: The name of the query parameter holding the token

LetsEncryptDedupReport.description: What the removal of the duplicated let's encrypt certificates found, and deleted

dryRun.description: `true` when nothing was deleted, the report only says what would be

certificates.description: The number of let's encrypt certificates otoroshi holds

duplicates.description: The ids of the let's encrypt certificates that duplicate a certificate kept

expired.description: The ids of the expired let's encrypt certificates whose domains are covered by a certificate kept, when `deleteExpired` is true

deleted.description: The number of certificates deleted, 0 for a dry run

LocalTokensBucketStrategyConfig.description: A token bucket local to each otoroshi instance: a call takes a token, the bucket holds at most `capacity` tokens and is refilled with `refillRequestedTokens` tokens every `refillRequestIntervalMs` milliseconds. The daily and monthly quotas are counted too

id.description: Selects the token bucket strategy: a bucket of tokens local to each otoroshi instance, refilled at a fixed rate

bucketKey.description: The key of the bucket the calls are counted in, an expression language string evaluated on each call (for instance `${req.ip}`). It is only used when the strategy is the config of a rate limiting plugin: the strategy of an api key or of a plan counts the calls of the api key. A random uuid when missing

capacity.description: The maximum number of tokens of the bucket, the size of a burst. Defaults to 300

refillRequestIntervalMs.description: The delay between two refills of the bucket, in milliseconds. Defaults to 50

refillRequestedTokens.description: The number of tokens added by a refill. Defaults to 50

LetsEncryptSettings.description: The settings of the ACME client otoroshi uses to order and renew certificates from Let's Encrypt, or from any ACME server

enabled.description: Order and renew certificates through ACME. `false` when absent

server.description: The ACME directory: `acme://letsencrypt.org` for the Let's Encrypt production server, `acme://letsencrypt.org/staging` for its staging server (whose certificates no browser trusts), or the https url of the directory of any ACME server. `acme://letsencrypt.org/staging` when absent

emails.description: The email addresses of the ACME account, added to its contacts as `mailto:` urls: the ACME server sends them the notices about the account and its certificates. The blank entries are left out

contacts.description: Other contact urls of the ACME account, like `mailto:` urls. The blank entries are left out

publicKey.description: The public key of the ACME account, PEM encoded. When the keys are empty, otoroshi generates an RSA 2048 key pair at the first order and saves it here. Empty when absent

privateKey.description: The private key of the ACME account, PEM encoded (PKCS#8). When the keys are empty, otoroshi generates an RSA 2048 key pair at the first order and saves it here. Empty when absent

preferredChain.description: The common name of the root certificate of the chain to deliver, when the ACME server offers several chains. null or blank: the default chain of the server

renewalPercentage.description: Renew a certificate once less than this percentage of its total lifetime remains. A value out of 1 to 100 reads as 20, the default

renewBeforeDays.description: Renew a certificate this number of days before it expires. It takes precedence over renewalPercentage, which degrades on short lived certificates. null: renewalPercentage applies. A value below 1 reads as null

deleteOldCertificatesAfterRenewal.description: Delete the previous certificate after a successful renewal, and the copies left by the previous renewals, instead of keeping a copy named `[UNTIL EXPIRATION]` until it expires. Only applies to the Let's Encrypt certificates. `false` when absent

OS.description: The operating system an otoroshi instance runs on

name.description: The name of the operating system (the `os.name` system property), `undefined` when a worker does not send it

version.description: The version of the kernel or of the operating system (the `os.version` system property), `undefined` when a worker does not send it

arch.description: The architecture of the processor as java names it (the `os.arch` system property, like `amd64` or `aarch64`), `undefined` when a worker does not send it

ApiLiveStats.description: The live statistics of an api: the statistics of each of the routes it exposes, added up. The values are rounded to two decimals. An id that is not the one of an api answers an empty object

calls.description: The calls the routes of the api served since the statistics were last reset

dataIn.description: The bytes the routes of the api received. Always 0: the statistics of the routes are not added up for this field

dataOut.description: The bytes the routes of the api sent. Always 0: the statistics of the routes are not added up for this field

rate.description: The calls per second the routes of the api serve, over the recent calls

duration.description: The sum, over the routes of the api, of the average duration of their recent calls, in milliseconds

overhead.description: The sum, over the routes of the api, of the average time otoroshi added to their recent calls, in milliseconds

ApiRoute.description: A route of an api: the requests it matches (its frontend), the backend it forwards them to and the flow of plugins they go through. Otoroshi turns it into a route of the proxy engine, the domain and the context path of the api in front of its paths

id.description: The id of the route, unique in the api

enabled.description: Whether the route is served. Defaults to `true`

name.description: The name of the route, `null` for none. The route of the proxy engine is named after it, its methods and its paths

frontend.description: The requests the route matches. Only the path of each of its domains is used: it comes after the domain and the context path of the api

backend.description: The id of the backend the route forwards to: a stored backend, searched first, or a backend of the api. A route whose backend cannot be found is not served

flow_ref.description: The id of the flow of the api whose plugins the route runs. Also read from `plugin_chain`. A route whose flow cannot be found runs no plugin. Defaults to an empty string

ApikeyCallIncr.description: A quotas update: the calls an api key made on a worker since its last update. The leaders add them to the quotas of the api key, an unknown api key is ignored

typ.description: Selects the calls of an api key (`apkincr`): the leaders add `i` to the quotas of the api key

apk.description: The client id of the api key the calls were made with

i.description: The number of calls to add to the quotas of the api key. Defaults to 0

GlobalScripts.description: Deprecated: the legacy scripts run on every request (transformers, validators, pre routings, sinks) and the legacy jobs. Use the plugins of the routes and the global plugins of plugins instead

enabled.description: Run the global scripts. `false` when absent

transformersRefs.description: The ids of the request transformer scripts run on every request. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a plugin of the classpath

transformersConfig.description: The configuration of the transformers, any json object: each script reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

validatorRefs.description: The ids of the access validator scripts run on every request. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a plugin of the classpath

validatorConfig.description: The configuration of the validators, any json object: each script reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

preRouteRefs.description: The ids of the pre routing scripts run on every request. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a plugin of the classpath

preRouteConfig.description: The configuration of the pre routings, any json object: each script reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

sinkRefs.description: The ids of the request sink scripts, which answer the requests that match no route. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a plugin of the classpath

sinkConfig.description: The configuration of the sinks, any json object: each script reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

jobRefs.description: The ids of the job scripts run by the instance. Empty when absent

items.description: The id of a script, or `cp:` followed by the class name of a job of the classpath

jobConfig.description: The configuration of the jobs, any json object: each job reads the key it expects. `{}` when absent

GenericMailerSettings.description: A mailer calling an http api of your own: each email is posted as a json object with its `from`, `to`, `subject` and `html` fields

type.description: The type of the mailer, `generic`

url.description: The url the emails are posted to

headers.description: The http headers added to each call, for instance to authenticate it. Empty when absent

to.description: The recipients of the events, when the mailer is the one of a data exporter. Empty when absent

LdapAuthModuleConfig.description: An LDAP auth module: the users log in with their credentials of an LDAP directory (Active Directory, OpenLDAP...)

type.description: The type of the auth module, `ldap` for an LDAP auth module

id.description: The unique id of the auth module, named by the `module` of the `Authentication` plugin of the routes, the `modules` of the `Multi Authentication` plugin, or the `backOfficeAuthRef` of the global configuration

name.description: The display name of the auth module, shown in the backoffice and on the login page of the routes that offer several auth modules (`Multi Authentication` plugin)

desc.description: The description of the auth module. `--` when missing
desc.example: Login with the company identity provider

basicAuth.description: Also accept the credentials of an `Authorization: Basic` header, without going through the login page. False when missing

allowEmptyPassword.description: Accept an empty password, for the directories that allow anonymous binds. False when missing

clientSideSessionEnabled.description: Also keep the session of the users of the private apps in an encrypted cookie, so that a session missing from the datastore of otoroshi (not synchronized yet on an instance of the cluster, lost by a restart) is restored from it. True when missing

sessionMaxAge.description: How long a session lasts, in seconds. 86400 (a day) when missing

userValidators.description: The checks of the profile of a user that logs in. Every check has to pass for the user to get in

example.error: the user is not a member of the admins group

remoteValidators.description: The remote services that validate a user that logs in. Every service has to accept the user

serverUrls.description: The urls of the LDAP servers, tried in turn when one does not answer. A legacy `serverUrl` string is read as a single url

items.description: The url of an LDAP server

searchBase.description: The base DN of the searches of users and groups

userBase.description: The DN, relative to `searchBase`, under which the users are searched. Null to search the whole `searchBase`

groupFilters.description: The groups whose members can log in, with the rights they get. Every user found can log in when empty. A legacy `groupFilter` string is read as one group for each team of the module

searchFilter.description: The LDAP filter finding the user, `${username}` being replaced by the login typed by the user

adminUsername.description: The DN of the account binding to the directory to search the users, null for an anonymous bind

adminPassword.description: The password of `adminUsername`, null for an anonymous bind. It can be a vault reference like `${vault://local/ldap-password}`

nameField.description: The attribute holding the name of the user

emailField.description: The attribute holding the email of the user

metadataField.description: The attribute holding the otoroshi data of the user, as a json object. Null when there is none

extraMetadata.description: A json object merged into the otoroshi data of the users that log in, sent to the backends of the private apps

metadata.description: The metadata of the auth module, free key/value pairs

tags.description: Free tags of the auth module, to search and sort it

sessionCookieValues.description: The `HttpOnly` and `Secure` flags of the session cookies set on the private apps once a user has logged in through the module. Both true when missing

superAdmins.description: Give super admin rights to every user that logs in to the backoffice. False when missing

extractProfile.description: Put the attributes of the user in its profile. False when missing

extractProfileFilter.description: The regexes of the attributes put in the profile when `extractProfile` is true. Every attribute when empty

extractProfileFilterNot.description: The regexes of the attributes left out of the profile when `extractProfile` is true

rightsOverride.description: The rights given to some users in the backoffice, by email. They replace the rights the user gets otherwise

additionalProperties.description: The rights of the user. `[{"tenant": "*:rw", "teams": ["*:rw"]}]` makes a super admin

dataOverride.description: The otoroshi data of some users, by email: merged into the otoroshi data of the user sent to the backends of the private apps

additionalProperties.description: The otoroshi data of the user, any json object

allowedUsers.description: The users allowed to log in, by email. Everybody when empty

items.description: A user allowed to log in. An email, or a pattern: `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `Not(x)`, `ContainedIn(a, b)` or `NotContainedIn(a, b)`

deniedUsers.description: The users that cannot log in, by email

items.description: A user that cannot log in. An email, or a pattern: `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `Not(x)`, `ContainedIn(a, b)` or `NotContainedIn(a, b)`

groupRights.description: Virtual groups giving rights in the backoffice to some users, by name of group

adminEntityValidatorsOverride.description: The validators the entities written in the backoffice by some users have to pass, by email of the user, then by entity kind

additionalProperties.description: The validators of the entities written by the user, keyed by the singular name of the entity kind or `all`
The validators of an entity kind, keyed by the singular name of the kind (`route`, `apikey`, `certificate`...) or `all` for every kind. Every validator has to pass for the entity to be written

route.error: routes can only be exposed on oto.tools
routes can only be exposed on oto.tools

example.name: Company directory
example.desc: Login with the LDAP directory of the company

DefaultTemplates.description: Json objects deep merged into the template the api serves for each kind of new entity (the `_template` operations, the new entities of the backoffice), to give the new entities of the instance defaults of their own. A null or empty template leaves the template unchanged. A string holding the json of the whole object is read too

route.description: Merged into the template of the new routes

service.description: Merged into the template of the new route compositions

backend.description: Merged into the template of the new backends

target.description: Not used yet: no template of a target reads it

descriptor.description: Merged into the template of the removed service descriptors, kept for compatibility

apikey.description: Merged into the template of the new api keys

group.description: Merged into the template of the new service groups

template.description: Not used yet: no template of an error template reads it

verifier.description: Merged into the template of the new jwt verifiers

authConfig.description: Merged into the template of the new auth modules

certificate.description: Merged into the template of the new certificates

script.description: Merged into the template of the new scripts and of the new wasm plugins

draft.description: Merged into the template of the new drafts

api.description: Merged into the template of the new apis

tcpService.description: Merged into the template of the new tcp services

dataExporter.description: Merged into the template of the new data exporters

tenant.description: Merged into the template of the new organizations (tenants)

team.description: Merged into the template of the new teams

apiSubscription.description: Merged into the template of the new api subscriptions

routeTemplate.description: Merged into the template of the new route templates

userDashboardTemplate.description: Merged into the template of the new user dashboards

userAlertTemplate.description: Merged into the template of the new user alerts

DefaultToken.description: Generates a token when the request has none. In strict mode the token is signed with the `algoSettings` of the verifier and written in its `source`, and a request already holding a token is refused. Otherwise a request without token goes through without one, and a request holding one has it verified

type.description: The strategy, always `DefaultToken`

strict.description: Generate the token for the requests without one, and refuse the requests that already hold one. True when missing

token.description: The claims of the generated token. The string values can hold expressions like `${apikey.clientName}`, `${token.jti}`, `${token.iat}`, `${token.nbf}`, `${token.exp}` (in a minute), `${token.iss}` (`Otoroshi`), `${token.sub}` (the `clientName` of the api key, or the email of the user, `anonymous` otherwise) and `${token.aud}` (`backend`) giving default values. The `iat`, `nbf` and `exp` claims are converted to numbers

verificationSettings.description: The claims a token found in the request has to hold

NgMinimalBackend.description: The backend of a route of a route composition: its targets, the client settings coming from the composition

targets.description: The servers the requests are forwarded to

root.description: The path prepended to the path of the forwarded requests. Defaults to `/`

rewrite.description: Whether the path of the forwarded requests is `root` alone (where the expression language can use the named path params of the frontend), instead of `root` followed by the path of the request. Defaults to `false`

load_balancing.description: How a target is chosen for each request. Defaults to round robin

DataExporterConfig.kafka.description: A data exporter of type `kafka`: the events are sent to a Kafka topic

type.description: The type of the exporter: `kafka`, the events are sent to a Kafka topic

enabled.description: Whether the exporter runs. A disabled exporter keeps its settings but exports nothing. Defaults to false

id.description: The unique id of the exporter, the key it is stored under and the `{id}` of its urls in the admin api. The templates generate `data_exporter_<uuid>` (`data_exporter_<env>_<uuid>` outside the `prod` environment)

name.description: The display name of the exporter, shown in the backoffice

desc.description: A description of the exporter. Defaults to `--`
desc.example: Events to Kafka, managed by the platform team

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the exporter

tags.description: Free tags of the exporter, to search and sort it

bufferSize.description: The maximum number of events waiting to be exported. Once it is reached, the oldest waiting events are dropped. Defaults to 5000

jsonWorkers.description: The number of events turned into json (and enriched) in parallel. Defaults to 1

sendWorkers.description: The number of batches sent in parallel. Defaults to 5

groupSize.description: The maximum number of events of a batch: a batch is sent once it is full or once `groupDuration` is elapsed. Defaults to 100

groupDuration.description: The maximum delay before a batch is sent, in milliseconds, even when it is not full. Defaults to 30000

projection.description: The fields of the events that are exported, as a json object: `{"field": true}` keeps a field, operators like `$at`, `$path`, `$jq` or `$date_from_unix_fmt` compute new ones (see the documentation of the data exporters). An empty object exports the whole events

customFilter.description: A custom filter, applied after `filtering`: the events it refuses are not exported. Null for none

customTransform.description: A custom transformation of the events, applied before they are exported. Null for none

config.description: The Kafka cluster and the topic the events are sent to

example.name: Events to Kafka
example.desc: Events to Kafka, managed by the platform team

apim.otoroshi.io.Apikey.description: An api key: the credentials (a client id and a client secret) a client presents to call the routes and apis it is authorized on, with its quotas, its path restrictions and the rotation of its secret. The api also writes `bearer`, a token holding the same credentials

clientId.description: The id of the api key, sent by the clients as `client_id`. 16 random lowercase alphanumerical characters when otoroshi generates it, but any non blank string unique among the api keys is accepted

clientSecret.description: The secret of the api key, sent by the clients as `client_secret`. 64 random lowercase alphanumerical characters when otoroshi generates it, but any non blank string is accepted

clientName.description: The name of the api key, for humans. It must not be blank

description.description: A free text describing the api key, shown in its form of the backoffice. Empty when absent. An api key minted for the plan of an api gets the description of the plan
description.example: The apikey of the mobile application of ACME

authorizedGroup.description: Legacy view of the authorizations: the id of the first service group of `authorizations`, null when there is none. When read, the group is added to the authorizations

authorizedEntities.description: Legacy view of the authorizations: each entity as a prefixed id, `group_<id>` for a service group, `route_<id>` for a route, `api_<id>` for an api, `route-composition_<id>` for a route composition, `service_<id>` for a service descriptor. An id without a known prefix is a service group id. When read, the entities are added to the authorizations

items.description: A prefixed id of an entity

authorizations.description: The entities the api key can call: service groups (and then all their routes), routes, apis and route compositions. The union of `authorizations`, `authorizedEntities` and `authorizedGroup` is read, and the three are written from it. A prefixed id (`route_<id>`, see `authorizedEntities`) is read too

enabled.description: Whether the api key can be used. It is written false once `validUntil` is past. Defaults to true

readOnly.description: When true, the api key only allows calls with the GET, HEAD and OPTIONS methods

allowClientIdOnly.description: When true, the api key can be presented with its client id only, without its secret, on the routes that accept the client id alone

throttlingStrategy.description: How the calls of the api key are counted. When set, the quotas of the strategy replace `throttlingQuota`, `dailyQuota` and `monthlyQuota`. When null, the default strategy of otoroshi counts them with those quotas

throttlingQuota.description: The number of calls allowed per throttling window (10 seconds by default, `app.throttlingWindow`). Defaults to 10000000

dailyQuota.description: The number of calls allowed per day. Defaults to 10000000

monthlyQuota.description: The number of calls allowed per month. Defaults to 10000000

constrainedServicesOnly.description: When true, the api key can only be used on the routes that constrain the api keys they accept (with tag or metadata based routing)

apiRef.description: The api, plan and subscription the api key was minted for, when it comes from the subscription to a plan of an api (`apis.otoroshi.io`): it then gets the plugins of the plan. Null otherwise

plugins.description: Plugins run on the calls made with the api key, after the plugins of its plan if any. Null when there is none

validUntil.description: The date the api key expires at, a timestamp in milliseconds. Once past, the api key is disabled. Null when it never expires

tags.description: Free tags of the api key. The routes can accept or refuse an api key on its tags

metadata.description: Free key/value metadata of the api key. The routes can accept or refuse an api key on its metadata, and `otoroshi-access-rights` holds the rights of the api key on the admin api. A value that is not a string is read as its json text

bearer.description: A bearer token standing for the credentials of the api key, that clients can send in an `Authorization: Bearer` header instead of the id and the secret: `otoapk_<clientId>_<signature>`, the signature being the HMAC-SHA256 of `otoapk_<clientId>` keyed with the secret. Computed by otoroshi, not read back

example.description: The apikey of the mobile application of ACME

GenKeyPairQuery.description: The settings of a key pair to generate. Every field is optional, an empty object generating a 2048 bits rsa key pair

algo.description: The algorithm of the key pair, as known by BouncyCastle: `rsa`, `ecdsa` (an elliptic curve key pair, its curve picked from the size), or another algorithm name such as `ec` or `dsa`. Defaults to `rsa`

size.description: The size of the key in bits, 2048 by default: 2048 or 4096 for an rsa key; 256, 384 or 521 for an `ecdsa` key (the curves secp256r1, secp384r1 and secp521r1, any other size giving secp256r1)

LoadBalancingNaiveFailover.description: The `NaiveFailover` load balancing: sends the requests to the first target, each retry going to the next target of the list

type.description: Selects the failover load balancing: the requests go to the first target, the retries to the next ones in turn

WasmExporterSettings.description: The settings of a wasm exporter: the events are given to the `export_events` function of a wasm plugin

params.description: Parameters given to the wasm function with the events

wasm_ref.description: The id of the wasm plugin (`plugins.otoroshi.io/v1/wasm-plugins`). A blank value is read as null, and nothing is exported then

BasicAuthModuleConfig.description: An in memory auth module: its users and their passwords are stored in the module itself

type.description: The type of the auth module, `basic` for an in memory auth module

id.description: The unique id of the auth module, named by the `module` of the `Authentication` plugin of the routes, the `modules` of the `Multi Authentication` plugin, or the `backOfficeAuthRef` of the global configuration

name.description: The display name of the auth module, shown in the backoffice and on the login page of the routes that offer several auth modules (`Multi Authentication` plugin)

desc.description: The description of the auth module. `--` when missing
desc.example: Login with the company identity provider

basicAuth.description: Also accept the credentials of an `Authorization: Basic` header, without going through the login page. False when missing

webauthn.description: Let the users log in with a WebAuthn device (security key, biometrics). False when missing

clientSideSessionEnabled.description: Also keep the session of the users of the private apps in an encrypted cookie, so that a session missing from the datastore of otoroshi (not synchronized yet on an instance of the cluster, lost by a restart) is restored from it. True when missing

sessionMaxAge.description: How long a session lasts, in seconds. 86400 (a day) when missing

metadata.description: The metadata of the auth module, free key/value pairs

tags.description: Free tags of the auth module, to search and sort it

users.description: The users that can log in through the module, with their email, their bcrypt hashed password, their profile data and their rights in the backoffice. Empty when missing

sessionCookieValues.description: The `HttpOnly` and `Secure` flags of the session cookies set on the private apps once a user has logged in through the module. Both true when missing

userValidators.description: The checks of the profile of a user that logs in. Every check has to pass for the user to get in

example.error: the user is not a member of the admins group

allowedUsers.description: The users allowed to log in, by email. Everybody when empty

items.description: A user allowed to log in. An email, or a pattern: `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `Not(x)`, `ContainedIn(a, b)` or `NotContainedIn(a, b)`

deniedUsers.description: The users that cannot log in, by email

items.description: A user that cannot log in. An email, or a pattern: `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `Not(x)`, `ContainedIn(a, b)` or `NotContainedIn(a, b)`

remoteValidators.description: The remote services that validate a user that logs in. Every service has to accept the user

example.name: In memory users
example.desc: The users of the team

WSProxyServer.description: An http proxy the calls of otoroshi go through. It is only used when its host and its port are set

host.description: The host name or the ip address of the proxy. A blank host disables the proxy, the calls are then direct

port.description: The port the proxy listens on. Without a port, the proxy is not used

protocol.description: The protocol used to talk to the proxy, `http` when null

principal.description: The user to authenticate on the proxy

password.description: The password to authenticate on the proxy

ntlmDomain.description: The NTLM domain of the user, for a proxy using NTLM authentication

encoding.description: The charset of the credentials sent to the proxy

nonProxyHosts.description: The hosts called directly, without the proxy, compared without case: a host name, or a pattern with a `*` at its start or at its end (`*.internal.oto.tools`, `10.0.*`)

items.description: A host or a host pattern

CustomThrottlingIncr.description: A quotas update: the calls counted by a `Custom throttling` plugin on a worker since its last update. The leaders add them to the counter of the current throttling window for this expression and group

typ.description: Selects the calls counted by a `Custom throttling` plugin (`custthrot`): the leaders add them to its counter

e.description: The `expression` of the plugin once evaluated (`${req.ip}` by default): the value the calls are counted by, like the ip address of the client

g.description: The group of the counter once evaluated: the `group` expression of the plugin, the id of the route when absent and `perRoute` is set, `global` otherwise

c.description: The number of calls to add to the counter. Defaults to 0

t.description: The duration of the throttling window, in milliseconds: `app.throttlingWindow` seconds (10 by default). Defaults to 0

TrafficEvents.description: A page of the gateway events of the traffic, read from the Elasticsearch cluster of the global configuration (`elasticReadsConfig`)

type.description: What the events are filtered on: `Service` (a route), `ApiKey`, `Group`, or `None` for the whole traffic

events.description: The gateway events, in the order asked for

items.description: A `GatewayEvent`, as otoroshi sent it to Elasticsearch: the request, the route, the backend, the durations, the status...

AnonymousReportNode.description: A member of the cluster as the anonymous report lists it: an excerpt of the member registered in the datastore, with the system statistics it last sent

id.description: The id of the member: `node_` and a random uuid generated when the member starts (`tmpnode_` and a random uuid for a worker that did not send its id)

version.description: The version of otoroshi the member runs

type.description: Whether the member is a `Leader` or a `Worker` of the cluster

cpu_usage.description: The cpu usage of the process of the member, in percent. Null until the member sent its first stats

load_average.description: The load average of the system of the member over the last minute, negative when the system does not provide it. Null until the member sent its first stats

heap_used.description: The heap memory used by the jvm of the member, in megabytes. Null until the member sent its first stats

heap_size.description: The heap memory the jvm of the member has reserved, in megabytes. Null until the member sent its first stats

relay.description: Whether the relay routing is enabled on the member (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.enabled`)

tunnels.description: The number of tunnels connected to the member: otoroshi instances of private networks that opened a tunnel to it to expose their services

NgMinimalRoute.description: A route of a route composition: its frontend and its backend, the other settings coming from the composition

backend.description: Where the matched requests are forwarded. When `backend_ref` is set, the value sent is ignored and replaced by the stored backend it references (the empty backend when there is none)

backend_ref.description: The id of a stored backend (proxy.otoroshi.io.Backend) the route uses instead of its own `backend`. Null when the route has its own backend

override_plugins.description: Whether the plugins of the route replace the plugins of the composition, instead of running before them. Only written when true, defaults to `false`

plugins.description: The plugins applied to the calls of this route only. Only written when not empty

RouteCallIncr.description: A quotas update: the traffic of a route on a worker since its last update. The leaders add the calls and the bytes to the statistics of the route (when the embedded metrics of the global configuration are enabled), and give the whole update to the green score extension when it is enabled. A route the leaders do not know is ignored

typ.description: Selects the traffic of a route (`srvincr`): the leaders add it to the statistics of the route

srv.description: The id of the route the calls went through. Workers also send a line with `global` for the sum of the traffic of all their routes

c.description: The number of calls to the route. Defaults to 0

di.description: The number of bytes received from the clients. Defaults to 0

do.description: The number of bytes sent to the clients. Defaults to 0

oh.description: The cumulated overhead of otoroshi, in milliseconds. Defaults to 0

du.description: The cumulated duration of the calls, in milliseconds. Defaults to 0

bdu.description: The cumulated duration of the calls to the backends (the backend call step), in milliseconds. Defaults to 0

hi.description: The number of bytes of the request headers received, request line included. Defaults to 0

ho.description: The number of bytes of the response headers sent, status line included. Defaults to 0

LoadBalancingLeastConnections.description: The `LeastConnections` load balancing: sends the requests to the target with the fewest calls in progress on this otoroshi instance, in turn among the ties

type.description: Selects the least connections load balancing: the requests go to the target with the fewest calls in progress

NgTarget.description: A server a backend forwards requests to

id.description: The id of the target, unique in its backend. Defaults to the url of the target

hostname.description: The host name of the target, without scheme nor port

port.description: The port the requests are sent to on the target, usually `443` when `tls` is true and `80` otherwise. Required

tls.description: Whether the target is called over https. Defaults to `false`

weight.description: The weight of the target in the load balancing: a target of weight 2 gets twice the requests of a target of weight 1. Defaults to `1`

backup.description: Whether the target is a backup target, only receiving the requests when no primary target is available (unhealthy, circuit breaker open or predicate not matching), and the retries once every primary target has been tried. Defaults to `false`

predicate.description: Which requests the target can serve. Defaults to any request

protocol.description: The http protocol used to call the target. Defaults to `HTTP/1.1`

ip_address.description: The ip address the calls are made to, instead of the resolution of `hostname`, which is still used for tls (sni and certificate check). Null to resolve `hostname`

tls_config.description: The tls settings of the calls to the target

TripleBounds.description: The bounds of a metric of the dynamic green score, in the unit of the metric: the mean of the metric is excellent up to `excellent`, sufficient up to `sufficient`, poor above. The score of the metric goes down from its best at 0 to its lowest at `poor`

excellent.description: The value up to which (included) the metric is excellent

sufficient.description: The value up to which (included) the metric is sufficient, when it is above `excellent`

poor.description: The value from which the score of the metric is at its lowest. The metric is poor above `sufficient`

LoadBalancingBestResponseTime.description: The `BestResponseTime` load balancing: sends the requests to the target with the lowest average response time, the targets without a measure being tried first. The measures are kept by each otoroshi instance

type.description: Selects the load balancing on the response time: the requests go to the target answering the fastest on average

CleverCloudSettings.description: The OAuth 1.0 credentials of a Clever Cloud application, used to call the api of Clever Cloud on an organization. The settings read as null unless all their fields are set and not empty

consumerKey.description: The consumer key of the OAuth 1.0 application

consumerSecret.description: The consumer secret of the OAuth 1.0 application

token.description: The OAuth 1.0 access token of the Clever Cloud user the api is called as, sent as `oauth_token`

secret.description: The secret of the access token, used with the consumer secret to sign the calls

orgaId.description: The id of the Clever Cloud organization

SAMLSignature.description: How the requests of a SAML auth module are signed

algorithm.description: The signature algorithm, read without case. `rsa_sha256` when missing or unknown

canocalizationMethod.description: The canonicalization method of the XML signatures: `exclusive` (exclusive canonicalization without comments) or `with_comments`, read without case. `exclusive` when missing or unknown

BadResponsesFaultConfig.description: A fault of the snow monkey that answers an error response, picked at random, instead of calling the backend

ratio.description: The share of the requests affected by the fault, between 0 and 1

responses.description: The responses an affected request can get

GenCsrResponse.description: A certificate signing request generated by the pki of otoroshi, with the key pair it was generated for. Nothing is stored

csr.description: The certificate signing request, PEM encoded

publicKey.description: The public key of the certificate signing request, PEM encoded

privateKey.description: The private key of the certificate signing request, PEM encoded (PKCS#8)

SessionCookieValues.description: The flags of the session cookie otoroshi sets once a user is logged in through the auth module

httpOnly.description: Set the `HttpOnly` flag on the session cookie, so that the scripts of the pages cannot read it. True when missing

secure.description: Set the `Secure` flag on the session cookie, so that browsers only send it over https. True when missing

Widget.description: A widget of a user analytics dashboard: an analytics query and the way its result is drawn

id.description: The id of the widget, unique within its dashboard. A random one is generated when it is missing or empty

title.description: The title shown in the header of the widget, the id of its query when empty. The backoffice fills it with the name of the query when the widget is created

query.description: The id of an analytics query of the catalog (`GET /api/analytics/_schema` lists them), like `requests_total`, `error_rate_ts` or `duration_avg_ts`

params.description: The parameters of the query, as listed in the catalog of the queries (for instance `top_n`)

type.description: How the result is drawn. It must suit the shape of the result of the query: `line` or `area` for a timeseries, `bar`, `pie`, `donut` or `table` for a top, `scalar` or `metric` for a single value, `heatmap` for a heatmap. Defaults to `line`

width.description: The width of the widget, in columns of the grid. Defaults to 4

height.description: The height of the widget, in rows of the grid. Defaults to 2

options.description: The display options of the widget, read by the backoffice: `format` (`count`, `number`, `compact`, `currency`, `rps`, `ms`, `percent`, `bytes`), `decimals`, `unit`, `currency`, `legend`, `stacked`, `thresholds`, `title`

AlertEvent.description: An alert event as stored by otoroshi: something an admin should know about. Every kind of alert adds its own fields to the ones described here: an `AdminLoggedInAlert`, for instance, adds `user` and `from`

@id.description: The unique id of the event: a snowflake id generated by the otoroshi instance that emitted it, a number written as a string that grows with time

@timestamp.description: When the event happened, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds

@type.description: The family of the event, always `AlertEvent` here

@product.description: The name of the product that emitted the event, the `otoroshi.events.name` setting (`otoroshi` by default)

@serviceId.description: The id of the entity the event is about, `--` for the events of otoroshi itself

@service.description: The name of the entity the event is about, `Otoroshi` for the events of otoroshi itself

@env.description: The environment of the otoroshi instance (the `app.env` setting)

alert.description: The kind of the alert, like `AdminLoggedInAlert`, `ApiKeyCreatedAlert`, `CircuitBreakerOpenedAlert` or `UserAnalyticsAlert`

user-agent-details.description: What the user agent detection of the global configuration found about the user agent of the caller. `null` when it is disabled or found nothing

origin-details.description: What the geolocation of the global configuration found about the ip address of the caller. `null` when it is disabled or found nothing

instance-number.description: The number of the otoroshi instance that emitted the event (the `app.instance.number` setting)

instance-name.description: The name of the otoroshi instance that emitted the event

instance-zone.description: The zone of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.zone`)

instance-region.description: The region of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.region`)

instance-dc.description: The datacenter of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.datacenter`)

instance-provider.description: The provider of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.provider`)

instance-rack.description: The rack of the otoroshi instance (`otoroshi.cluster.relay.location.rack`)

cluster-mode.description: The cluster mode of the otoroshi instance

cluster-name.description: The name of the otoroshi instance in its cluster, `none` when it is not part of a cluster

JsonPatch.description: A json patch (RFC 6902): the operations to apply, in order

enabled.description: Whether the exporter runs. A disabled exporter keeps its settings but exports nothing. Defaults to false

id.description: The unique id of the exporter, the key it is stored under and the `{id}` of its urls in the admin api. The templates generate `data_exporter_<uuid>` (`data_exporter_<env>_<uuid>` outside the `prod` environment)

Webhook.description: A webhook otoroshi posts events to, as json arrays of events

url.description: The url the events are posted to

headers.description: The http headers added to each call, for instance to authenticate it. Empty when absent

ResourceDefinition.description: A partial definition of an entity: its `kind` and the fields that differ from its template, or a kubernetes like resource holding them in its `spec`

TargetPredicateGeolocationMatch.description: A target predicate on the geolocation of the client: the target only serves the requests coming from near one of its positions. It needs a plugin giving the geolocation of the client, every request matches without it

type.description: Selects the predicate on the geolocation of the client: the target only serves the clients near one of its `positions`

items.description: A position written `<latitude>:<longitude>:<radius>`, in degrees for the coordinates and in kilometers for the radius. `;` is read as a separator too

positions.description: The positions the client must be near one of

EntityLocation.description: Where an entity lives: the tenant (organization) it belongs to, and the teams that can see and change it. The rights of the admins are checked against it

tenant.description: The id of the tenant (organization) of the entity

teams.description: The ids of the teams of the entity. `*` stands for every team of the tenant (organization)

WorkflowDescriptor.description: What the workflows of otoroshi can use: the nodes, grouped in categories, the functions and the operators

categories.description: The categories the workflow editor groups the nodes, the functions and the operators in

nodes.description: The nodes a workflow is made of

functions.description: The functions a `call` node can run

operators.description: The operators that compute values in the expressions of a workflow

categories.name: Core
categories.description: Run code, make HTTP requests, etc

nodes.name: call
nodes.description: This node calls a function an returns its result

StorageExportLine.description: A key of the datastore of otoroshi, with its value, its type and its expiration: a line of the ndjson export of the datastore and of the state of the cluster

k.description: The key in the datastore, prefixed by the storage root of otoroshi (`otoroshi` by default)

v.description: The value of the key: a string for a `string` key (a counter included), an object of strings for a `hash`, an array of strings for a `list` or a `set`

oneOf.description: The items of a `list` or a `set` key

t.description: When the key expires, a timestamp in milliseconds, -1 when it never expires

w.description: The type of the key. `counter` (a number) is only read by the import, the export writing counters as `string`

Thresholds.description: The bounds of the dynamic score of a green score group: for each metric of the traffic of a route, averaged over the calls, the values up to which it is excellent, sufficient, and from which it is poor

overhead.description: The bounds of the time otoroshi spends on a call, backend excluded, in milliseconds. 5, 10, 15 by default

duration.description: The bounds of the whole duration of a call, in milliseconds. 5, 10, 15 by default

backendDuration.description: The bounds of the time the backend takes to answer, in milliseconds. 5, 10, 15 by default

calls.description: The bounds of the rate of calls of the route, in calls per second over the last minute. 5, 10, 15 by default

dataIn.description: The bounds of the size of the data otoroshi receives from the client, in bytes. 100, 500, 1000 by default

dataOut.description: The bounds of the size of the data otoroshi sends back to the client, in bytes. 100, 500, 1000 by default

headersOut.description: The bounds of the size of the status line and headers of the response, in bytes. 10, 30, 50 by default

headersIn.description: The bounds of the size of the request line (method, url, protocol) and headers of the request, in bytes. 10, 30, 50 by default

NewRelicCallSettings.description: The settings of a New Relic exporter: the events are sent to the New Relic log api

service.description: The `service` of the logs, `otoroshi` when unset. Not written when unset

hostname.description: The `hostname` of the logs, the host called when unset. Not written when unset

WasmPluginValidator.description: A check of a json document delegated to a wasm plugin: its `validate` function receives the document and answers `{"result": true}` when the document is valid

kind.description: The kind of the validator, always `wasm-plugin-validator`

ref.description: The id of the wasm plugin that checks the document

error.description: The error message given when the check fails, null for the generic message

JsonPathValidator.description: A check of a json document: the value found at a json path of the document is compared to an expected value. It checks the profile of a logged in user (user validators of auth modules) or the json of an entity an admin writes (admin entity validators)

kind.description: The kind of the validator, always `json-path-validator`. A validator without kind is read as a json path validator

path.description: The json path (https://goessner.net/articles/JsonPath/) of the checked value in the document, like `$.profile.email`. A filter path like `[?(@.enabled == true)]` with a `true` value passes when it selects something

value.description: The expected value: any json value, compared as is to the value found at the path. A string can hold an operator instead: `IsDefined()` and `NotDefined()` check the presence of the path, `Not(x)`, `Regex(x)`, `RegexNot(x)`, `Wildcard(x)`, `WildcardNot(x)`, `Contains(x)`, `ContainsNot(x)`, `StartsWith(x)`, `DontStartsWith(x)`, `ContainedIn(a, b)`, `NotContainedIn(a, b)`, `JsonContains(x)` and `JsonContainsNot(x)` check a string, `Size(n)`, `SizeNot(n)`, `SizeGt(n)`, `SizeGte(n)`, `SizeLt(n)`, `SizeLte(n)`, `Contains(x)`, `Contains(Regex(x))` and `Contains(Wildcard(x))` check an array

error.description: The error message given when the check fails, null for the generic message

AlgoSettings.description: How the signature of a jwt token is verified, or how a token is signed. Its `type` selects the algorithm and where the keys come from: a shared secret (`HSAlgoSettings`), PEM keys (`RSAlgoSettings`, `ESAlgoSettings`), a key pair of a certificate of otoroshi (`RSAKPAlgoSettings`, `ESKPAlgoSettings`), the key pair matching the `kid` of the token (`KidAlgoSettings`) or a remote JSON Web Key Set (`JWKSAlgoSettings`)

security.otoroshi.io.JwtVerifier.description: A jwt verifier: it finds a jwt token in the requests (`source`), verifies its signature (`algoSettings`) and its claims, then sends it to the backend as is, signed again or transformed (`strategy`). Routes use it through the `JwtVerification` plugin

type.description: The kind of verifier, always `global` for the verifiers of the admin api. Not read, always written

id.description: The unique id of the jwt verifier, listed in the `verifiers` of the `JwtVerification` plugins of the routes that use it

name.description: The display name of the jwt verifier, shown and searched in the list of the jwt verifiers of the backoffice

desc.description: The description of the verifier. `--` when missing

strict.description: Refuse the requests without token (400 `error.expected.token.not.found`). When false they go through unchecked. False when missing (the template of the api sets it to true)

source.description: Where the token is found in the requests

algoSettings.description: How the signature of the token is verified. For the `DefaultToken` strategy, how the generated token is signed

strategy.description: What the verifier does with the token

metadata.description: The metadata of the verifier, free key/value pairs

tags.description: Free tags of the jwt verifier, to search and sort it

NodeMetric.description: A metric of an otoroshi instance, its fields depending on its type: a gauge has a `value`, a counter a `count`, a histogram a `count` and the statistics of its values, a meter a `count` and its rates, a timer all of them

name.description: The name of the metric without its tags (`jvm.memory.total.used`, `ng-proxy-state-refresh`...)

type.description: The group of the metric: `gauges`, `counters`, `histograms`, `meters`, `timers`, or `metrics`, the group of every metric whatever its type, so most metrics show up twice. With a filter, the singular `gauge`, `counter`, `histogram`, `meter` or `timer`, and no `metrics` group

value.description: The value of a gauge: a number, a string, or an array

count.description: The number of values recorded (histogram), of events (meter) or of calls (timer), or the value of a counter

max.description: The largest of the values the histogram or the timer keeps (in `duration_units` for a timer)

mean.description: The mean of the values the histogram or the timer keeps (in `duration_units` for a timer)

min.description: The smallest of the values the histogram or the timer keeps (in `duration_units` for a timer)

p50.description: The median of the values the histogram or the timer keeps (in `duration_units` for a timer)

stddev.description: The standard deviation of the values the histogram or the timer keeps

m5_rate.description: The rate over the last five minutes (an exponentially weighted moving average), in `rate_units` for a timer, `units` for a meter

m15_rate.description: The rate over the last fifteen minutes (an exponentially weighted moving average), in `rate_units` for a timer, `units` for a meter

coraza-waf.extensions.otoroshi.io.Coraza.description: A configuration of the coraza web application firewall (its wasm build), that the Coraza WAF plugin of a route applies through its `ref`: the seclang directives of the firewall, with or without the OWASP core rule set, in blocking or detection mode

tags.description: Free tags of the coraza configuration, to sort and search the configurations

inspect_in_body.description: Whether coraza inspects the bodies of the requests, true when absent

inspect_out_body.description: Whether coraza inspects the bodies of the responses, true when absent

When absent, the `default` directives of the legacy `config.directives_map` field are read, none otherwise

clientNamePattern.description: The expression language template of the name of the api keys, evaluated with the api (`${api.id}`, `${api.name}`) and the plan (`${plan.id}`, `${plan.name}`). `null` for a random name

authorizations.description: The same entities as `authorizedEntities`, written as objects. Read too, prefixed ids being accepted in place of the objects

restrictions.description: The restrictions of the api keys: the paths and the methods they are allowed, forbidden or not found on

metadata.description: The metadata of the api keys, the metadata of the subscription being added to them. Empty keys are left out
